unique: A 1916 Italian Renaissance villa on Biscayne Bay, built by an industrialist with European rooms, formal gardens and a stone barge breakwater.
buzz: The house and the gardens are equally good, and the bay terrace is the photo. Go early before the tour buses.

name: Fairchild Tropical Botanic Garden
unique: Eighty three acres of tropical plants, with a rainforest, a butterfly conservatory, a palm collection and a tram tour.
buzz: The butterfly house and the tram are the easy wins, and the collection is world class. Hot in summer, so go early.

name: Little Havana
unique: A Cuban neighborhood centered on Calle Ocho, with cigar rollers, ventanitas, domino players at Maximo Gomez Park and croquetas on every block.
buzz: Go hungry and walk Calle Ocho, then sit in the domino park. The cigar shops are happy to show you how it is done.

name: Deering Estate
unique: A 1920s stone house on Biscayne Bay with fossil beds, a hardwood hammock and a canoe trail through the mangroves.
buzz: The house tour and the nature trail are both good, and the bay is calm for kayaking. Less crowded than Vizcaya.

name: Bonnet House Museum and Gardens
unique: A 1920s artist's estate between the beach and the intracoastal, with a shell museum, a courtyard and gardens that survived the condo boom.
buzz: The house is eccentric and personal, and the grounds are a green surprise in the middle of Fort Lauderdale. Guided tours only.

name: Sawgrass Recreation Park
unique: An airboat ride into the Everglades with alligators, wading birds and a sawgrass maze, plus a small animal exhibit.
buzz: The airboat is loud and fast and kids love it. The wildlife show is cheesy but the swamp is real.

name: Flamingo Gardens
unique: A 60 acre botanical garden and wildlife sanctuary with flamingos, a bobcat, otters and a 1930s house, plus a tram through the citrus grove.
buzz: The flamingos and the tram are the kid draw, and the gardens are shady. Good for a hot day.

name: Morikami Museum and Japanese Gardens
unique: A Japanese garden and museum built around a 1900s farming colony, with a tea house, koi ponds, bonsai and a taiko drum festival.
buzz: The gardens are genuinely serene and the museum explains the Japanese settlement of Florida. The bonsai collection is excellent.

name: Lion Country Safari
unique: A drive through safari park with lions, rhinos, giraffes and zebras loose around the car, plus a walk through amusement area.
buzz: The drive is the fun, especially for kids who have never seen a lion outside a cage. Go early when the animals are active.

name: Loggerhead Marinelife Center
unique: A sea turtle hospital with tanks of recovering turtles, a surgical suite and nesting beach programs, free to visit.
buzz: The turtles are close and the staff explain the injuries and the nesting season. Free, with a donation suggested.

name: Bahia Honda State Park
unique: A state park on a keys island with a sand beach, a historic bridge ruin, snorkeling and campsites on the water.
buzz: The beach is one of the best in the keys and the old bridge is the photo. Book camping months ahead.

name: John Pennekamp Coral Reef State Park
unique: The first undersea park in the country, with coral reefs, a sunken statue garden and snorkel and dive boats leaving from the marina.
buzz: The snorkel trip is the reason to come, and the reef is shallow enough for beginners. Book ahead in season.

name: Ernest Hemingway Home and Museum
unique: The Spanish colonial house where Hemingway wrote in the 1930s, with his furniture, his typewriter and dozens of polydactyl cats descended from his own.
buzz: The cats are the fun and the writing studio is the history. Tours run continuously and are worth the ticket.

name: Crystal River Archaeological State Park
unique: A 14 acre mound complex built by the Woodland culture 1,500 years ago, with burial mounds, a plaza and a museum on the river.
buzz: The mounds are subtle but the story is fascinating, and the river setting is pretty. Combine it with a manatee swim.

name: Cedar Key
unique: A tiny old Florida fishing and clam town on a Gulf island, with a boardwalk, a dock, clam shacks and sunsets over the marsh.
buzz: The clams and the sunset are the reasons, and the town is small enough to walk. Quiet midweek.

name: Chassahowitzka River
unique: A spring fed river with clear water, cypress and mangrove tunnels, manatees in winter and a campground at the launch.
buzz: The paddle is easy and the spring runs are beautiful. Rent a kayak at the campground and go early.

name: Anastasia State Park
unique: A state park on a barrier island with a wide beach, dunes, a salt marsh and campsites under oaks, minutes from the old city.
buzz: The beach is quieter than the city beaches and the camping is shaded. Good for a combination history and beach day.

name: Werner-Boyce Salt Springs
unique: A coastal spring and salt marsh park with a deep spring, paddling trails and a boardwalk, hidden behind the commercial strip.
buzz: The spring is a surprise and the paddle is quiet. Bring bug spray.

name: Peace River Wildlife Center
unique: A rehabilitation center for injured birds and small wildlife, with pelicans, owls, eagles and a turtle pond, run by volunteers.
buzz: Small and free, with staff who explain each animal's story. Good for kids.

name: Circle B Bar Reserve
unique: A 1,200 acre former ranch turned wetland preserve with a boardwalk, oak hammocks and alligators everywhere, one of the best wildlife walks in central Florida.
buzz: The alligators are close and the birds are abundant. Go early and stay on the path.

name: Six Mile Cypress Slough Preserve
unique: A 3,500 acre wetland preserve with a 1.2 mile boardwalk through cypress, ferns and orchids, with otters, herons and alligators.
buzz: The boardwalk is easy and cool, and the wildlife is close. A good break from the beach.

name: Florida Museum of Natural History
unique: A free museum with a butterfly rainforest, fossil skeletons, Florida's native cultures and a giant shark jaw, on the UF campus.
buzz: The butterfly rainforest is the kid hit and the fossils are serious. Free, with a small fee for the butterfly house.

name: Tallahassee Museum
unique: A 52 acre museum of Florida history and wildlife with a 1880s farm, a caboose, a zip line and native animals including panthers and bears.
buzz: The mix of history and animals works for kids, and the zip line is the adrenaline add on.

name: Air Force Armament Museum
unique: A museum of bombs, missiles, guns and aircraft, with a B-52, an SR-71 and a MOAB, on the Eglin base.
buzz: The hardware is impressive and free. Bring ID for base access.

name: Seaside
unique: The planned New Urbanist town where The Truman Show was filmed, with pastel cottages, picket fences, a pavilion and a walkable center.
buzz: The architecture is the attraction and the beach is gorgeous. Busy in summer, quiet in winter.

name: Mount Vernon
unique: George Washington's plantation on the Potomac, with the mansion, the tomb, the slave quarters, a working farm and a distillery.
buzz: The house tour and the slave memorial together tell the whole story, and the river view is beautiful. Allow three hours.

name: Wolf Trap National Park for the Performing Arts
unique: The only national park for the performing arts, with a covered amphitheater and lawn seating under the trees, plus a barn theater for smaller shows.
buzz: Bring a picnic and a blanket for the lawn. The sound is good and the setting is hard to beat.

name: Arlington National Cemetery
unique: The national cemetery on the Potomac, with the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, the changing of the guard, Kennedy's grave and rows of markers on the hills.
buzz: Sobering and beautifully kept. Take the tram if you want to cover the ground, and stay for the guard change.

name: Marine Corps War Memorial
unique: The Iwo Jima flag raising statue in bronze, with a view across the river to the Washington monuments and a nightly sunset ceremony in summer.
buzz: The scale of the statue surprises people, and the skyline view is excellent. Free and quick.

name: Leesburg Historic District
unique: A courthouse square of 18th and 19th century buildings, brick sidewalks, a brewery and restaurants, in the middle of Virginia wine country.
buzz: The downtown is walkable and busy on weekends, with good lunch spots and a farmers market.

name: Morven Park
unique: A 1,000 acre estate with a Greek Revival mansion, formal gardens, a carriage museum and equestrian grounds.
buzz: The carriage collection is the surprise, and the grounds are quiet. Check tour times.

name: University of Virginia Rotunda
unique: Jefferson's rotunda and the lawn of pavilions and student rooms, a UNESCO World Heritage site and a working university.
buzz: The lawn is the walk and the rotunda tour explains Jefferson's design. Free and central.

name: Carter Mountain Orchard
unique: A pick your own orchard on a ridge above Charlottesville, with apple cider doughnuts, a bakery and a view of Monticello and the Blue Ridge.
buzz: The view and the doughnuts are the reason, and picking is a fall ritual. Go early on weekends.

name: Lexington Historic District
unique: A small Shenandoah Valley town with Washington and Lee and VMI, Stonewall Jackson's house, a historic courthouse and brick streets.
buzz: The colleges and the old houses make a compact walk, and the VMI museum is free.

name: Mill Mountain Star
unique: A 88 foot neon star on a mountain above Roanoke, with a viewpoint over the valley and the city lights at night.
buzz: The drive up is easy and the view is the payoff, especially at dusk. Free.

name: Taubman Museum of Art
unique: A free museum in a striking modern building with regional art, American painting, folk art and a sculpture gallery.
buzz: The building is the photo and the collection is free. Good rainy day stop.

name: Chateau Morrisette
unique: A winery on the Blue Ridge Parkway with a tasting room, a restaurant and a lawn, making wine since the 1970s.
buzz: The setting is the sell and the restaurant is good for lunch. Check hours in winter.

name: Natural Tunnel State Park
unique: A 850 foot natural tunnel carved by a creek through a mountain, with a chairlift, a train line through it and trails above.
buzz: The tunnel is genuinely dramatic and the chairlift saves the climb. Go when the train passes through.

name: Cumberland Gap National Historical Park
unique: The mountain pass that opened the westward trail through the Appalachians, with earthworks, a visitor center and a ridge trail across three states.
buzz: The view from the pinnacle is worth the climb, and the history is foundational. Free.

name: Jamestown Settlement
unique: A living history museum with replicas of the Susan Constant, a Powhatan village and a fort, telling the 1607 story.
buzz: Kids can climb the ships and try on armor, and the museum covers the hard history of the colony. Good for a family day.

name: Yorktown Battlefield
unique: The battlefield where Cornwallis surrendered in 1781, with earthworks, a siege line and a driving tour through the woods.
buzz: The ranger talks make the siege make sense, and the earthworks are well preserved. Pair it with the American Revolution Museum.

name: Virginia Museum of Fine Arts
unique: A free encyclopedic museum with Art Nouveau, African art, Faberge and a sculpture garden, plus a strong photography program.
buzz: Free and world class, with a good cafe and a sculpture garden. The Faberge collection is the surprise.

name: Lewis Ginter Botanical Garden
unique: Fifty acres of themed gardens with a conservatory, a children's garden, a rose garden and a lake, plus a holiday lights show.
buzz: The conservatory is the winter win and the children's garden is genuinely good. Holiday lights sell out.

name: Virginia Beach Boardwalk
unique: A three mile oceanfront boardwalk with restaurants, a fishing pier, a statue of Neptune and separate bike and walking lanes.
buzz: The boardwalk is wide and clean, and the Neptune statue is the photo. Busy in summer, pleasant in the off season.

name: Battleship Wisconsin
unique: An Iowa class battleship docked at Nauticus, with turrets, crew quarters and a deck you can walk, plus a science center next door.
buzz: The ship is enormous and the tour is self guided, so you can go at your pace. Good for kids.

name: Birmingham Civil Rights Institute
unique: A museum across from the 16th Street Baptist Church tracing the Birmingham movement, from the children's crusade to the bombing that killed four girls.
buzz: Powerful and specific, with the church across the street as part of the experience. Give it two hours.

name: Birmingham Museum of Art
unique: A free museum with a strong collection of American and European art, African masks, Asian ceramics and a sculpture garden.
buzz: Free and better than expected, with a good cafe. The African collection is the surprise.

name: Railroad Park
unique: A 19 acre linear park built along the railroad tracks downtown, with lawns, a skate park, a playground and a view of the viaducts.
buzz: The design turned a dead edge into the city's front yard. Good for a walk and a coffee.

name: McWane Science Center
unique: A hands on science center with a dinosaur hall, an aquarium, an IMAX and a bed of nails, in a former department store.
buzz: Good for kids of all ages, with enough to fill a rainy afternoon. The aquarium is smaller than it looks.

name: Rosa Parks Museum
unique: A museum at the site of the bus stop where Parks was arrested, with a reconstructed bus, original documents and a video of the boycott.
buzz: The bus and the archive are the strongest parts. Small enough for an hour and serious throughout.

name: Dexter Avenue King Memorial Baptist Church
unique: The church where Martin Luther King Jr. pastored during the Montgomery bus boycott, with the pulpit, the stained glass and a basement exhibit.
buzz: The sanctuary is still in use and the guides tell the boycott story from the pews. Dress respectfully.

name: The Legacy Museum
unique: A museum built on a former slave warehouse, tracing the line from slavery to mass incarceration with original testimony, art and data.
buzz: Heavy and essential, and the companion memorial nearby completes it. Give it time and go with someone.

name: Hank Williams Museum
unique: A collection of the country singer's suits, guitars, cars and handwritten lyrics, a few blocks from the stage where he started.
buzz: For fans it is a pilgrimage, and the 1952 Cadillac is the centerpiece. Small and earnest.

name: Bellingrath Gardens
unique: Sixty five acres of azaleas, camellias and roses on the Fowl River, with a 1930s mansion and a river cruise.
buzz: The spring azaleas are the show, and the house tour is a bonus. Hot in summer, so go early.

name: Mobile Carnival Museum
unique: A museum of Mardi Gras in the city that started it, with elaborate trains, crowns, robes and the story of the mystic societies.
buzz: The costumes are spectacular and the history explains why Mobile, not New Orleans, claims the first carnival.

name: Dauphin Street
unique: A downtown street of bars, restaurants and live music in historic buildings, with a Mardi Gras parade route running through it.
buzz: The bars are close together and the crowds are friendly. Busy on weekends and during carnival.

name: US Space and Rocket Center
unique: A museum with a Saturn V rocket overhead, a space shuttle, simulators and the original Space Camp, on the arsenal road.
buzz: The Saturn V hall is awe inspiring and the simulators are fun for kids. Allow half a day.

name: Monte Sano State Park
unique: A CCC park on a mountain above Huntsville with trails, a lodge, cabins and overlooks of the Tennessee Valley.
buzz: The trails are well built and the overlooks are the payoff. Less crowded than the space center.

name: Moundville Archaeological Park
unique: A Mississippian mound complex with 29 mounds, a plaza and a museum of engraved pottery and copper, on the Black Warrior River.
buzz: The scale is impressive and the museum explains the culture well. Climb the big mound for the view.

name: Paul W. Bryant Museum
unique: A museum of Alabama football with championship trophies, game film and the story of Bear Bryant, on the campus.
buzz: Even non fans get pulled into the history. Game weekends are packed.

name: DeSoto Falls
unique: A 104 foot waterfall in a stone gorge on Lookout Mountain, with a short trail and a swimming area below.
buzz: The falls are easy to reach and the pool is cold. A good stop on the way to Little River Canyon.

name: Little River Canyon
unique: A 600 foot deep canyon on Lookout Mountain with a rim drive, waterfalls and trails, one of the deepest canyons east of the Mississippi.
buzz: The rim drive has the overlooks and the canyon floor has the waterfalls. Go after rain for the flow.

name: Noccalula Falls
unique: A 90 foot waterfall in a city park with a gorge trail, a miniature train, a campground and a statue of the Cherokee woman the falls are named for.
buzz: The gorge trail gets you behind the falls, which kids love. The park is old fashioned and cheap.

name: Jule Collins Smith Museum of Fine Art
unique: A university museum with American and European art, a sculpture garden and a cafe, free to the public.
buzz: Small and free, with good temporary shows. A quiet break from campus.

name: Edmund Pettus Bridge
unique: The bridge where marchers were beaten on Bloody Sunday in 1965, now a National Historic Landmark with a view of the Alabama River.
buzz: Walking across is the experience, and the interpretive center nearby explains the march. Quiet and heavy.

name: Old Courthouse Museum
unique: A courthouse museum in the town that shaped Harper Lee and Truman Capote, with a courtroom modeled on the one in To Kill a Mockingbird.
buzz: For readers it is a pilgrimage, and the annual play is performed in the courtroom. Check the schedule.

name: Clinton Presidential Center
unique: A presidential library on the Arkansas River with the Oval Office, the campaign memorabilia and a park and bridge on the riverfront.
buzz: The exhibits are well done and the river park is free. Allow two hours.

name: Little Rock Central High School National Historic Site
unique: The school at the center of the 1957 desegregation crisis, with a visitor center across the street and ranger led walks.
buzz: The rangers tell the story with people who lived it, and the school is still operating. Powerful and free.

name: Arkansas Museum of Fine Arts
unique: A rebuilt art museum with a strong collection of American and Southern art, a sculpture garden and a restaurant.
buzz: The renovation is impressive and the collection is free on some days. Good rainy day stop.

name: River Market District
unique: A downtown market hall, food stalls, a farmers market and the riverfront park, connected by a streetcar to the museums.
buzz: The market is the lunch stop and the river walk is the stroll. Busy on Saturday mornings.

name: Garvan Woodland Gardens
unique: Two hundred acres of gardens on a Lake Hamilton peninsula, with a glass chapel, a bonsai collection and a children's garden.
buzz: The Anthony Chapel is the photo and the gardens are beautiful in every season. Holiday lights are a big draw.

name: Oaklawn Racing
unique: A historic thoroughbred track with a casino, a grandstand and a racing season that has run for over a century.
buzz: The cheap seats are close to the rail and the corned beef is a local tradition. Check the racing calendar.

name: Walmart Museum
unique: A museum in Sam Walton's original five and dime, with the first store, the pickup truck and the story of the retail empire.
buzz: Free and more interesting than expected, especially for anyone in business. The soda fountain is still there.

name: The Momentary
unique: A contemporary art satellite of Crystal Bridges in a former cheese factory, with exhibitions, a rooftop bar and live music.
buzz: The industrial space and the programming are both good, and the bar makes it a evening stop.

name: Eureka Springs Historic District
unique: A Victorian mountain town of steep streets, stone walls, springs and a loop of shops and inns, built around healing water.
buzz: The town is hilly and charming, with a famous passion play and a haunted hotel. Park and walk.

name: Thorncrown Chapel
unique: A glass and wood chapel in the woods by Fay Jones, with 425 windows and no walls, an AIA landmark.
buzz: The light and the trees are the experience, and it is free. Go on a weekday morning for quiet.

name: Hemmed-in-Hollow Falls
unique: A 209 foot waterfall, the tallest between the Rockies and the Appalachians, reached by a steep trail from the Buffalo River.
buzz: The hike is rough and the reward is real. Bring water and check the river level.

name: Blanchard Springs Caverns
unique: A living cave with guided tours through cathedral sized rooms, flowstone and a underground stream, run by the Forest Service.
buzz: The living cave is the real thing, not a commercial show cave. Book the longer tour.

name: Petit Jean State Park
unique: Arkansas's first state park, with Cedar Falls, a canyon, a lodge built by the CCC and trails through the Ouachita foothills.
buzz: Cedar Falls is the hike and the lodge is the sleep. Go after rain for the waterfall.

name: Mount Magazine State Park
unique: The highest point in Arkansas, with a lodge on the rim, hang gliding, trails and a view over the Arkansas River valley.
buzz: The drive up is the adventure and the overlooks are the payoff. The lodge is a good base.

name: Arkansas Railroad Museum
unique: A museum in the old Cotton Belt shops with locomotives, cabooses and a steam engine you can climb on.
buzz: Volunteers run it and the engines are close enough to touch. Cheap and good for kids.

name: Dickson Street
unique: A street of bars, restaurants and music venues next to the university, with the Walton Arts Center at one end.
buzz: Busy on weekends and game days, with good local music. Walk it before a show.

name: Fort Smith National Historic Site
unique: A frontier fort and federal courthouse with the gallows, the jail and the story of the Trail of Tears passing through.
buzz: The courtroom and the gallows are the sobering highlights, and the rangers tell the story well.

name: Delta Cultural Center
unique: A museum of Delta music and life in a former railroad depot, with the King Biscuit Time radio show and the blues trail.
buzz: The music exhibits are excellent and free, and the town is ground zero for Delta blues radio.

name: Churchill Downs
unique: The track that hosts the Kentucky Derby, with the twin spires, the paddock and a museum of racing history.
buzz: The Derby is the bucket list event, but a regular race day is cheaper and easier. Take the tour if no race is running.

name: Muhammad Ali Center
unique: A museum of Ali's life and values, with fight footage, the Olympic medal, his poetry and the civil rights context.
buzz: More moving than a sports museum, and the six core values exhibits are the heart. Allow two hours.

name: Louisville Mega Cavern
unique: A 17 mile underground cavern with zip lines, a ropes course, mountain bike trails and a tram tour, in a former limestone mine.
buzz: The underground zip line is the novelty and the bike trails are real. Book ahead.

name: 21c Museum Hotel
unique: A hotel with a free contemporary art museum in its public spaces, including the famous red penguins and rotating installations.
buzz: The art is free and the bar is good, so it works as a stop even if you are not staying.

name: Mary Todd Lincoln House
unique: The girlhood home of Mary Todd Lincoln, with period rooms and the story of her family and the White House years.
buzz: The guides are good and the house is intimate. Pair it with the Lexington walking tour.

name: The Arboretum
unique: A 100 acre public garden with a rose garden, a children's garden, a wetland and trails, on the university campus.
buzz: Free and well kept, with good shade and a visitor center. A quiet break in horse country.

name: My Old Kentucky Home
unique: The Federal style mansion that inspired the state song, with period rooms, outbuildings and the story of the Rowan family and the enslaved people they held.
buzz: The house tour is honest about slavery and the song's complicated history. The grounds are pretty.

name: Perryville Battlefield
unique: The site of the largest Civil War battle in Kentucky, with earthworks, a museum and a driving tour through the rolling farmland.
buzz: The museum explains a battle most people have never heard of, and the fields are quiet.

name: Shaker Village of Pleasant Hill
unique: The largest restored Shaker community in the country, with 34 buildings, a working farm, craft demos and trails.
buzz: The village is beautiful and the craft demonstrations are real. Stay for a meal in the trustee's house.

name: Abraham Lincoln Birthplace
unique: A memorial building over the symbolic birth cabin of Lincoln, with a spring, a museum and the farm site.
buzz: The memorial is impressive and the story is well told. Free or cheap, and quick.

name: Hidden River Cave
unique: A cave tour with a underground river, a suspension bridge over the gorge and a museum of cave science.
buzz: The bridge and the river are the highlights, and the tour is more physical than a show cave.

name: Renfro Valley
unique: A barn based music venue that has hosted country and bluegrass since the 1930s, with a theater, a lodge and a general store.
buzz: The barn shows are the real thing, with a house band and a radio history. Check the schedule.

name: Kingdom Come State Park
unique: A mountaintop park with sandstone cliffs, a lake and overlooks into the Cumberland Mountains, one of the highest parks in the state.
buzz: The views are expansive and the trails are short. Quiet and free.

name: Lake Cumberland
unique: A 65,000 acre lake with 1,200 miles of shoreline, houseboat rentals and a reputation for striped bass.
buzz: The lake is huge and the coves are quiet. Rent a houseboat for a weekend if you can.

name: Land Between the Lakes
unique: A 170,000 acre national recreation area between two lakes, with a bison and elk prairie, a planetarium and trails.
buzz: The elk and bison range is the kid draw, and the lakes are good for boating. Allow a full day.

name: Woodford Reserve
unique: A small distillery in a stone building with copper stills, rickhouses and a tasting, on the Kentucky Bourbon Trail.
buzz: The tour is polished and the setting is beautiful. Book ahead on weekends.

name: Natural Bridge State Resort Park
unique: A 60 foot natural sandstone arch on a ridge above Red River Gorge, with a skylift, a lodge and trails.
buzz: The arch is an easy walk and the skylift saves the climb. Busy in fall.

name: Cave Run Lake
unique: A 8,000 acre lake in the Daniel Boone National Forest with public ramps, camping and muskie fishing.
buzz: The lake is quiet and the forest setting is pretty. Good for a day on the water.

name: The National WWII Museum
unique: A vast museum with a restored Higgins boat, a Sherman tank, a 4D theater and the personal stories of the war in Europe and the Pacific.
buzz: One of the best museums in the country, and it takes most of a day. Start with the film and the train car.

name: City Park
unique: A 1,300 acre park with live oaks, a sculpture garden, a children's amusement park, a botanical garden and paddle boats on a lagoon.
buzz: The sculpture garden is free and the oaks are magnificent. Rent a bike or a boat.

name: St. Louis Cemetery No. 1
unique: The oldest cemetery in the city, with above ground tombs, the grave of Marie Laveau and a maze of family vaults.
buzz: You can only enter with a guide now, and the history of the burial customs is the point. Book ahead.

name: Frenchmen Street
unique: A strip of live music clubs, bars and restaurants just outside the French Quarter, where locals go to hear brass, funk and jazz.
buzz: The clubs are close together and the cover charges are low. Start early and follow your ears.

name: Mardi Gras World
unique: The warehouse where parade floats are built, with giant figures, props and a tour through the painting and sculpting shops.
buzz: The scale of the floats is the fun and kids love it. The tour includes a slice of king cake.

name: USS Kidd
unique: A World War II destroyer docked on the Mississippi, restored and open for self guided tours through the decks and turrets.
buzz: The ship is tight and real, and the museum explains the Pacific war. Good for kids who like machines.

name: LSU Rural Life Museum
unique: A 450 acre museum of Louisiana rural life with a plantation complex, slave cabins, a country store and farm equipment.
buzz: The slave cabins and the working farm are the powerful parts. The grounds are shady and quiet.

name: Louisiana State Capitol
unique: The tallest state capitol in the country, with an Art Deco interior, a observation deck and the spot where Huey Long was shot.
buzz: The observation deck view is the reason, and the building is a monument to Long's ambition. Free.

name: Vermilionville
unique: A living history village of Acadian, Creole and Native American houses on the bayou, with music, cooking and craft demonstrations.
buzz: The music and food demos are the best part, and the village is shady and walkable. Good for kids.

name: Natchitoches Historic District
unique: The oldest settlement in Louisiana, with a brick main street, a river walk, a fort site and 18th century houses.
buzz: The river street is the photo and the meat pies are the local food. Christmas lights are a big draw.

name: Sci-Port Discovery Center
unique: A hands on science center with a planetarium, an IMAX, a space exhibit and a toddler area on the Shreveport riverfront.
buzz: Good for a rainy day with kids, with enough to fill an afternoon. The planetarium is a bonus.

name: Biedenharn Museum and Gardens
unique: The home of the first bottler of Coca-Cola, with the original bottling plant, a museum and formal gardens.
buzz: The bottling equipment and the family story are the interesting parts. The gardens are a bonus.

name: Southdown Plantation
unique: A 1859 sugar plantation house with a museum of the sugar industry, the enslaved workers and the Cajun culture that followed.
buzz: The sugar history is well told and the house is handsome. Check hours before driving out.

name: Los Islenos Museum
unique: A museum of the Canary Islanders who settled the parish in the 1770s, with a village, a church and the story of the 2005 flood.
buzz: The Isleno history is unique and the flood exhibit is moving. Free.

name: Madewood Plantation
unique: A Greek Revival mansion on Bayou Lafourche, still family owned and open for tours and overnight stays.
buzz: The house is stunning and the family story is personal. Book ahead for a tour or a night.

name: Fort Jackson
unique: A brick fort on the Mississippi below New Orleans, used in the Civil War and later as a prison, with a moat and a river view.
buzz: The fort is weathered and quiet, and the river is right there. A good stop on the way to the delta.

name: Abbeville Shrimp Festival
unique: A street festival in the shrimp capital of Louisiana, with boiled shrimp, gumbo, music and a parade.
buzz: The food is the point and the shrimp are fresh. Go early for parking.

name: Brownell Memorial Park
unique: A small park with a 100 foot observation tower, a cypress swamp and a rookery full of egrets and herons.
buzz: The tower gives a canopy view of the swamp and the birds are close. Free.

name: Mississippi Civil Rights Museum
unique: A state museum that tells the movement county by county, with the names of the dead, a burned church bell and the story of Freedom Summer.
buzz: One of the best civil rights museums in the country, and the scale of the local detail is what makes it. Pair it with the adjacent history museum.

name: Mississippi Museum of Art
unique: A state art museum with a strong collection of Mississippi and Southern artists, photography and a sculpture garden.
buzz: The Southern art is the reason, and the museum is quiet and well organized. Free on some days.

name: Fondren
unique: A walkable neighborhood of bungalows, coffee shops, bars, a brewery and a cinema, the social center of young Jackson.
buzz: The district is compact and busy on weekends, with a good brunch scene. Park once and walk.

name: Longwood
unique: The largest octagonal house in the country, unfinished since the Civil War, with its original crates and tools still inside.
buzz: The unfinished interior is the fascinating part, and the tour explains why construction stopped. Book ahead in pilgrimage season.

name: Melrose
unique: A Greek Revival mansion in the Natchez National Historical Park, with original furniture and the story of the enslaved people who ran the estate.
buzz: The ranger tours are excellent and the slave quarters exhibit is part of the visit. Less flashy than the private houses and more honest.

name: Old Court House Museum
unique: A 1858 courthouse on a hill with a museum of the siege, Confederate and Union relics, and a view over the Mississippi.
buzz: The collection is old fashioned and dense, and the view from the hill is the best in town. Pair it with the military park.

name: Oxford Square
unique: A courthouse square of bookshops, bars, boutiques and restaurants, with the university a few blocks away and game day crowds that fill it.
buzz: The square is the town's living room, busy on weekends and game days. The independent bookstore is the local anchor.

name: Rowan Oak
unique: William Faulkner's home, preserved with his books, his outline of A Fable on the wall and the grounds he walked.
buzz: Pilgrimage for readers, and the self guided tour lets you linger. The cedar grove is quiet.

name: Delta Blues Museum
unique: A museum in a former railroad depot with Muddy Waters' cabin, guitars, photographs and the story of the Delta blues.
buzz: The cabin and the instruments are the highlights, and Clarksdale itself is the experience. Go to a juke joint after.

name: GRAMMY Museum Mississippi
unique: A museum of recorded music with instruments, stage clothes and interactive mixing stations, focused on Mississippi's outsize role in American music.
buzz: The interactive studios are fun for kids and the artifacts are serious. A surprise for a small Delta town.

name: Dentzel Carousel
unique: A 1909 Dentzel menagerie carousel with hand carved animals, still running in a pavilion in Highland Park.
buzz: The animals are beautiful and the ride costs a dollar. A genuine piece of Americana.

name: African American Military History Museum
unique: A museum in a 1942 USO building telling the stories of Black soldiers from the Revolution to today, with uniforms, medals and oral histories.
buzz: Personal and well curated, and free. The local soldiers' stories are the strongest part.

name: Beauvoir
unique: Jefferson Davis's last home and presidential library, with the house, the Confederate cemetery and the grounds on the Gulf.
buzz: The house and the library are the visit, and the view of the Gulf is a bonus. The history is presented uncritically, so bring your own context.

name: Biloxi Lighthouse
unique: A 1848 lighthouse standing in the middle of a highway, with a climb to the top and a view of the beach and the bay.
buzz: The setting in the median is strange and the climb is short. A quick photo stop.

name: Shearwater Pottery
unique: A family pottery studio founded by the Anderson family, with a showroom of glazed pots and tiles made on site.
buzz: The pottery is beautiful and the prices are fair for handmade work. Pair it with the Walter Anderson Museum.

name: Tennessee Williams Home
unique: The boyhood home of the playwright, with family furniture, photographs and the bedroom where he wrote his first stories.
buzz: Small and personal, best for theater people. The Columbus historic district around it is worth a walk.

name: Cotton District
unique: A neighborhood of restored mill cottages, bars and restaurants next to the Mississippi State campus, rebuilt after a tornado.
buzz: The district is walkable and busy on game weekends. Good for a casual dinner.

name: Natchez Trace Visitor Center
unique: The headquarters of the Natchez Trace Parkway, with a museum on the old trace, a film and the start of the 444 mile drive.
buzz: The film and the exhibits explain why the trace exists, and the parkway is the real attraction. Free.

name: Keeper of the Plains
unique: A 44 foot steel sculpture of a Native American figure at the confluence of two rivers, with a fire ring lit at dusk and a bridge over the water.
buzz: The sculpture is striking and the sunset fire is the moment. Free and quick.

name: Sedgwick County Zoo
unique: A 247 acre zoo with elephants, gorillas, a farm, a train and a children's petting area, one of the best in the Plains.
buzz: Big enough for a full day and shady in stretches. The train is the kid favorite.

name: Exploration Place
unique: A hands on science center on the Arkansas River with a design studio, a flight simulator and a dome theater.
buzz: Good for a rainy day, with enough for kids of different ages. The river setting is nice.

name: Massachusetts Street
unique: A wide main street of independent shops, bars and restaurants beside the university, with a history of free state politics.
buzz: The street is walkable and busy on weekends. The burger joints and bookshops are the local institutions.

name: KU Natural History Museum
unique: A university museum with dinosaur fossils, a giant mosasaur, Kansas fossils and a live beehive.
buzz: Free and genuinely good, especially the mosasaur. A quick stop for kids.

name: Strataca
unique: A tour 650 feet underground in a working salt mine, with tunnels, mining equipment and a underground vault.
buzz: The descent and the scale of the mine are the experience. Bring a jacket, it is cool down there.

name: Brown v. Board of Education National Historical Park
unique: A museum in the Monroe Elementary School, one of the segregated schools in the case, with the story of the five lawsuits that ended school segregation.
buzz: The school itself is the exhibit and the ranger talks are excellent. Free.

name: Kansas State Capitol
unique: A copper domed capitol with a mural by John Steuart Curry, a legislative chamber and a dome tour to the top.
buzz: The Curry mural and the dome climb are the reasons. Free, with tours on the hour.

name: Little Sweden
unique: A Swedish heritage town with a main street of Dala horses, a folk art center, a college and a annual Svensk Hyllningsfest.
buzz: The Dala horses are everywhere and the town is charming. The Swedish pancakes are the lunch.

name: Old Market
unique: A warehouse district of cobblestone streets, brick buildings, galleries and restaurants, with horse drawn carriages and buskers.
buzz: The streets are photogenic and the food is good. Busy on weekend evenings.

name: Joslyn Art Museum
unique: A free museum in a Art Deco building with European and American art, Native American works and a sculpture garden.
buzz: Free and strong, with a beautiful building and a good cafe. The Western art collection is the local specialty.

name: The Durham Museum
unique: A museum in the Art Deco Union Station, with trains, a soda fountain, a street of old storefronts and the history of the Union Pacific.
buzz: The station itself is gorgeous and the trains are the kid draw. Allow two hours.

name: Lauritzen Gardens
unique: A 100 acre botanical garden with a conservatory, a model train garden, a rose garden and a woodland trail.
buzz: The model trains are the kid hit and the conservatory is the winter escape. Good in every season.

name: Sheldon Museum of Art
unique: A free university art museum in a Philip Johnson building, with American art, modernism and a sculpture garden.
buzz: The building is the draw and the collection is free. Quiet on weekdays.

name: Nebraska State Capitol
unique: A 400 foot tower with a Nebraska life mural, a unicameral chamber and an observation deck with a view of the plains.
buzz: The building is one of the best state capitols, and the dome tour is worth it. Free.

name: Ashfall Fossil Beds
unique: A fossil bed where a volcanic ash fall killed a herd of rhinos, horses and camels 12 million years ago, now exposed in a working quarry.
buzz: The skeletons are still in the ground where they died, which is the fascinating part. Seasonal, so check dates.

name: Niobrara River
unique: A spring fed river through the Sandhills with waterfalls, pine bluffs and a gentle current, one of the best floats in the Plains.
buzz: The water is clear and the trip is easy. Rent a tube or a canoe and go in summer.

name: Scotts Bluff National Monument
unique: A bluff that guided Oregon Trail wagons, with a summit road, trails and a museum of the westward migration.
buzz: The summit drive has the view and the trail is short. The Oregon Trail ruts are nearby.

name: Philbrook Museum of Art
unique: A 1920s Italianate villa turned art museum, with a strong Native American collection and formal gardens.
buzz: The house and the gardens are as good as the art, and the Native American collection is excellent.

name: Woody Guthrie Center
unique: A museum of the folk singer's life, with his lyrics, drawings, guitars and the archive of his recordings.
buzz: The archive is serious and the story is moving. Good for anyone interested in American music.

name: Cain's Ballroom
unique: A 1924 dance hall where Bob Wills and the Texas Playboys broadcast, still booking rock, country and indie acts under the original sign.
buzz: The room is legendary and the sound is good. Check the calendar and buy ahead.

name: National Cowboy and Western Heritage Museum
unique: A museum of the American West with Western paintings, saddles, firearms, a reconstructed town and the End of the Trail sculpture.
buzz: Bigger and better than expected, with serious art alongside the cowboy gear. Allow two hours.

name: Bricktown
unique: A warehouse district of brick buildings, restaurants, a canal with water taxis and a ballpark, next to downtown.
buzz: The canal walk is the thing to do and the food is decent. Busy on weekends.

name: Myriad Botanical Gardens
unique: A 17 acre downtown garden with a glass conservatory, a children's garden, a lake and an ice rink in winter.
buzz: The conservatory is the rainy day win and the outdoor gardens are free. Good for kids.

name: Price Tower
unique: Frank Lloyd Wright's only built skyscraper, a 19 story copper and concrete tower with tours and a small hotel.
buzz: For architecture people it is a pilgrimage, and the tour explains the design. The top floor view is a bonus.

name: Medicine Park
unique: A cobblestone resort town at the edge of the Wichita Mountains, with a creek, a swimming hole, cabins and a dam built of river rock.
buzz: The cobblestone buildings are charming and the creek is cool. Good base for the wildlife refuge.

name: Forest Park
unique: A 1,300 acre park larger than Central Park, holding the zoo, the art museum, the science center, a lake and miles of trails, most of them free.
buzz: You can spend a whole day here without paying admission. The boathouse and the art museum are the anchors.

name: Anheuser-Busch Brewery Tour
unique: A tour of the historic brewery with the red brick buildings, the Clydesdale stables and a tasting at the end.
buzz: The Clydesdales are the highlight and the tour is free. Book ahead and bring ID.

name: Missouri Botanical Garden
unique: A 79 acre garden with a Victorian conservatory, a Japanese garden, a climatron dome and an extensive orchid collection.
buzz: The Climatron and the Japanese garden are the highlights. Spring and fall are the best seasons.

name: Cathedral Basilica of Saint Louis
unique: A Romanesque cathedral with the largest mosaic collection in the world, 41 million pieces covering the ceiling in gold and color.
buzz: The mosaics are astonishing and it is free. Go on a weekday for quiet.

name: National WWI Museum and Memorial
unique: The national museum of the First World War, with trenches, weapons, personal letters and a tower with a view of the city.
buzz: One of the best war museums in the country, and the tower is worth the climb. Allow three hours.

name: Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art
unique: A free encyclopedic museum with a strong Asian collection, European painting and the giant shuttlecocks on the lawn.
buzz: Free and world class, with a beautiful lawn and a good cafe. The shuttlecocks are the photo.

name: Union Station
unique: A 1914 Beaux Arts train station with a grand hall, a science center, a planetarium and a model train gallery.
buzz: The grand hall is the photo and the model trains are the kid draw. Free to walk through.

name: Arabia Steamboat Museum
unique: Cargo from a steamboat that sank in 1856, recovered intact from a cornfield, with tools, dishes, clothing and food still preserved.
buzz: The everyday objects are the fascinating part, and the recovery story is improbable. Good for kids.

name: Wonders of Wildlife
unique: A massive wildlife museum and aquarium with sharks, otters, a swamp, a cave and mounted animals from around the world.
buzz: Bigger and better than expected, with live animals and a real aquarium. Allow half a day.

name: Hermann Wine Trail
unique: A Missouri River town settled by German immigrants, with a brick main street and a cluster of wineries along the valley.
buzz: The wines are sweet and the town is charming. Book a designated driver or a shuttle.

name: Mark Twain Boyhood Home
unique: The house where Samuel Clemens grew up, with the whitewashed fence, the museum and the river town that became Tom Sawyer's St. Petersburg.
buzz: For readers it is a pilgrimage, and the town leans into it. The fence painting is a photo op for kids.

name: Table Rock Lake
unique: A clear Ozark lake with coves, marinas, swimming and bass fishing, next to the Branson strip but a world away.
buzz: The lake is the quiet alternative to the shows, with good swimming and rental boats.

name: Pappajohn Sculpture Park
unique: A 4.4 acre downtown park with 30 large outdoor sculptures, free and open at all hours, next to the art center.
buzz: The scale is surprising for Des Moines and the park is easy to walk. Free.

name: Greater Des Moines Botanical Garden
unique: A domed conservatory and outdoor gardens on the Des Moines River, with tropical plants, a bonsai collection and a cafe.
buzz: The dome is the winter escape and the river walk is pretty. Cheap and calm.

name: Living History Farms
unique: A 500 acre open air museum with an 1700s Ioway village, an 1850 farm, a 1900 farm and a small town, with interpreters in period dress.
buzz: The breadth of the three farms is the strength, and kids can help with chores. Allow three hours.

name: Czech Village
unique: A neighborhood of Czech bakeries, a butcher, a museum and a riverfront, with kolaches and a national Czech and Slovak museum.
buzz: The kolaches are the reason and the museum is worth an hour. The river walk is a bonus.

name: Brucemore
unique: A 1886 Queen Anne mansion with 26 acres of grounds, a carriage house and the story of the three families who owned it.
buzz: The house tour is personal and the gardens are free to walk. Check the event schedule.

name: Iowa Avenue Literary Walk
unique: A self guided walk through a UNESCO City of Literature, with bronze reliefs of writers and quotes set into the sidewalks.
buzz: A quiet hour for readers, and the used bookshops and Prairie Lights are the stops.

name: Amana Colonies
unique: Seven villages settled by German Pietists, with communal kitchens, woolen mills, furniture shops and family style restaurants.
buzz: The colonies are a good half day, with crafts and heavy German food. The woolen mill is the best stop.

name: Effigy Mounds National Monument
unique: Two hundred prehistoric mounds shaped like bears, birds and lines on bluffs above the Mississippi, with trails through the woods.
buzz: The bear mounds are subtle but the setting is beautiful. The bluff trail is a real hike.

name: Loess Hills
unique: A narrow band of wind deposited hills along the Missouri, with prairie ridges, sharp bluffs and a landscape found in only one other place on earth.
buzz: The ridges are best at sunrise and the prairie flowers peak in summer. Drive the back roads.

name: Fenelon Place Elevator
unique: The world's shortest and steepest scenic railway, a 296 foot funicular up the bluff to a view over the Mississippi and three states.
buzz: The ride is short and the view is the reward. A dollar or two, and a local institution.

name: Lewis and Clark Interpretive Center
unique: A museum on the Missouri telling the Corps of Discovery story, with a keelboat, a prairie garden and a view of the river.
buzz: The exhibits are well done and the river setting is the point. Good for kids studying the expedition.

name: Field Museum
unique: A natural history museum with SUE the T. rex, ancient Egyptian tombs, a man eating lion exhibit and a vast Native American collection.
buzz: The dinosaur and the Egypt gallery are the priorities, and the building itself is grand. Allow half a day.

name: Shedd Aquarium
unique: A 1930 aquarium on the lake with a Caribbean reef, belugas, otters and a Amazon flooded forest, plus a aquatic show.
buzz: The beluga and otter habitats are the favorites, and the building is beautiful. Book tickets ahead.

name: Museum of Science and Industry
unique: A huge science museum with a real U-boat, a coal mine, a 727 and a giant model train layout, in the 1893 World's Fair building.
buzz: The U-boat tour is the standout and the coal mine is a close second. Plan for half a day.

name: Lincoln Park Zoo
unique: A free zoo in the middle of the city with lions, apes, penguins and a farm, open every day of the year.
buzz: Free and genuinely good, which is rare for a city zoo. The penguin house is the kid favorite.

name: Millennium Park
unique: A downtown park with Cloud Gate, the Pritzker Pavilion, a fountain and a garden, on the old rail yards.
buzz: The Bean is the photo and the park is a good walk. Free and central.

name: Chicago Riverwalk
unique: A 1.25 mile promenade along the Chicago River with bars, kayak rentals, architecture tours and the bridges overhead.
buzz: The river level view of the architecture is the reason, and the bars are a good stop. Best at sunset.

name: Wrigley Field
unique: The second oldest ballpark in the majors, with the ivy covered walls, the manual scoreboard and the rooftop seats across the street.
buzz: The tour gets you into the dugout and the press box, and the history is the draw. Book ahead.

name: Pullman National Historical Park
unique: A planned industrial town built by the Pullman company, with the factory, the row houses and the story of the 1894 strike.
buzz: The architecture and the labor history together are the point. Free, with a visitor center.

name: Frank Lloyd Wright Home and Studio
unique: Wright's own home and studio, where he developed the Prairie style, with guided tours and a neighborhood full of his houses.
buzz: The studio tour is the best architecture hour in the Chicago area. Book ahead and walk the neighborhood after.

name: Galena Historic District
unique: A river town of brick storefronts, steep streets and 19th century houses, once a lead mining boomtown and now a weekend getaway.
buzz: The main street is polished and the houses are beautiful. Busy in fall.

name: The Children's Museum of Indianapolis
unique: The largest children's museum in the world, with a dinosaur hall, a carousel, a space station and a working water clock.
buzz: Overwhelming in a good way, with enough for a full day. The dinosaur exhibit is the star.

name: Indianapolis Motor Speedway Museum
unique: A museum of the 500 with winning cars, trophies and the bricks, plus a track tour on the speedway.
buzz: The winning cars and the track tour are the reasons. Book the tour with the museum.

name: Newfields
unique: An art museum and 152 acre campus with gardens, a lake, a greenhouse and a sculpture park.
buzz: The gardens and the art are both strong, and the campus is a good walk. Free on some days.

name: Conner Prairie
unique: A living history park with an 1836 village, a Lenape camp, a working farm and a balloon ride.
buzz: The interpreters are good and kids can try chores and crafts. Allow half a day.

name: Brown County State Park
unique: The largest state park in Indiana, with ridge trails, a fire tower, a lodge and some of the best fall color in the Midwest.
buzz: The fire tower view is the payoff and the trails are rolling. October is packed.

name: Indiana State Fair
unique: A big state fair with livestock shows, a midway, tractor pulls, fried food and the dairy bar.
buzz: The dairy bar and the livestock barns are the local picks. Go on a weekday.

name: University of Notre Dame
unique: A campus with the Golden Dome, the basilica, the grotto and the football stadium, all walkable around two lakes.
buzz: The basilica and the grotto are the quiet highlights, and game weekends are a scene. Free to walk.

name: French Lick Springs
unique: A historic mineral spring resort with a grand hotel, a casino, a spa and the Pluto mineral water that made it famous.
buzz: The hotel is a step back in time and the grounds are pretty. Worth a walk even if you are not staying.

name: Parke County Covered Bridge Festival
unique: A county with 31 covered bridges and a festival that fills them with craft fairs, food and traffic.
buzz: Pick a few bridges and drive the back roads, and go early to beat the crowds. The festival is the busiest week.

name: Cincinnati Museum Center
unique: Three museums in the Art Deco Union Terminal: natural history, Cincinnati history and a children's museum.
buzz: The building is worth the trip alone, and the history museum has a great model of the city.

name: Cincinnati Zoo
unique: The second oldest zoo in the country, with hippos, gorillas, a train and the Fiona the hippo story.
buzz: Well laid out and shady, with the hippo exhibit as the draw. Allow half a day.

name: Columbus Zoo and Aquarium
unique: A zoo and aquarium with polar bears, manatees, a water park and a golf course, on the Scioto River.
buzz: The manatee rescue and the polar bears are the highlights, and the water park makes it a full day.

name: Franklin Park Conservatory
unique: A glasshouse with biomes from rainforest to desert, plus a butterfly garden and a collection of Chihuly glass.
buzz: The Chihuly glass among the plants is the draw, and the butterfly house is a kid favorite.

name: Cleveland Museum of Art
unique: A free encyclopedic museum with Asian art, medieval armor, Impressionism and a sculpture garden.
buzz: Free and world class, with a beautiful building and a good cafe. One of the best museums in the country.

name: West Side Market
unique: A 1912 market hall with a vaulted ceiling, butcher stalls, pierogi stands and produce vendors under one roof.
buzz: The building is beautiful and the food is cheap. Go hungry and bring cash.

name: Great Lakes Science Center
unique: A science center on the lake with a NASA Glenn visitor center, a domed theater and hands on exhibits.
buzz: The NASA exhibits are the draw and the lakefront location is nice. Good for kids.

name: Toledo Museum of Art
unique: A free art museum with a strong glass collection, Old Masters and a sculpture garden, in a Greek Revival building.
buzz: The glass collection is the local specialty and the museum is free. A surprise for a mid sized city.

name: Henry Ford Museum
unique: A museum of American innovation with the Presidential limousine JFK was shot in, the Rosa Parks bus, a giant locomotive and rows of historic cars.
buzz: The bus and the limousine are the emotional artifacts, and the car collection is enormous. Allow three hours.

name: Greenfield Village
unique: A village of historic buildings moved from across the country, including Edison's lab, the Wright brothers' shop and a Model T ride.
buzz: The Model T ride and the Wright shop are the highlights, and the village is huge. Allow half a day.

name: Detroit Institute of Arts
unique: A encyclopedic museum with the Detroit Industry murals by Diego Rivera, a strong African American collection and a central courtyard.
buzz: The Rivera murals are worth the trip alone, and the collection is deep. Free for local residents on some days.

name: Motown Museum
unique: The modest house where Hitsville USA recorded the Supremes, the Temptations and Stevie Wonder, with the original studio and control room.
buzz: The studio is tiny and the guides sing, which makes it joyful. Book ahead, because tours sell out.

name: Frederik Meijer Gardens
unique: A 158 acre garden with a butterfly house, a Japanese garden, a children's garden and a large sculpture park.
buzz: The butterfly exhibit is the spring draw and the sculpture park is excellent. Allow half a day.

name: Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park
unique: Sixty thousand acres of old growth forest on Lake Superior, with waterfalls, a escarpment and backcountry campsites.
buzz: Remote and quiet, with real wilderness and Lake of the Clouds as the view. Bring bug spray.

name: Milwaukee Art Museum
unique: A museum with a winged addition by Calatrava that opens and closes over the lake, plus a strong American and folk art collection.
buzz: The wings opening is the photo, and the collection is solid. Check the schedule for the brise soleil.

name: Miller Brewery Tour
unique: A tour of the old Miller brewery with the caves, the brewhouse and a tasting at the end.
buzz: The caves and the history are the interesting parts, and the tasting is generous. Book ahead.

name: Wisconsin State Fair
unique: A state fair famous for cream puffs, cheese, livestock shows and a midway, eleven days in August.
buzz: The cream puffs are the ritual and the livestock barns are the real fair. Go on a weekday.

name: Olbrich Botanical Gardens
unique: Sixteen acres of gardens with a Thai pavilion, a rose garden, a prairie and a conservatory.
buzz: The Thai pavilion is the photo and the outdoor gardens are free. Quiet and pretty.

name: Cave of the Mounds
unique: A limestone cave with colorful mineral formations, a guided tour and a fossil dig outside.
buzz: The formations are colorful and the tour is easy. A good rainy day stop with kids.

name: Peninsula State Park
unique: A 3,700 acre park on Green Bay with a lighthouse, a beach, bike trails and a view of the Door County islands.
buzz: The Eagle Bluff lighthouse and the bike loop are the highlights. Book camping early in summer.

name: Circus World Museum
unique: The winter quarters of the Ringling brothers, with circus wagons, a big top and daily performances in summer.
buzz: The wagon collection is enormous and the shows are real. Good for kids and nostalgia.

name: Wingspread
unique: A late Frank Lloyd Wright house with a four winged plan around a central great hall, built for the Johnson wax family.
buzz: For Wright fans it is a major house, and the great hall is the showpiece. Tours by reservation.

name: Minneapolis Institute of Art
unique: A free encyclopedic museum with Asian art, African art, photography and a period room collection.
buzz: Free and excellent, with a good cafe and a strong Asian collection. A full afternoon.

name: Walker Art Center
unique: A contemporary art center with a sculpture garden across the street, including the Spoonbridge and Cherry.
buzz: The sculpture garden is free and the Spoonbridge is the photo. The museum is for contemporary tastes.

name: Guthrie Theater
unique: A major regional theater with three stages and a cantilevered lobby over the Mississippi, founded by Tyrone Guthrie.
buzz: The building and the river view are worth the visit, and the productions are strong. Rush tickets exist.

name: Minnehaha Falls
unique: A 53 foot waterfall in a city park, with trails down to the creek and a seafood shack at the top.
buzz: The falls are easy to reach and the park is lovely. The Sea Salt eatery is the local lunch.

name: Como Park Zoo and Conservatory
unique: A free zoo and conservatory with polar bears, gorillas, a Japanese garden and a carousel.
buzz: Free and genuinely good for families, with the conservatory as the winter escape.

name: Science Museum of Minnesota
unique: A science museum with a dinosaur hall, a Mississippi River exhibit, a omnitheater and a cell lab.
buzz: The river exhibit and the dinosaurs are the highlights. Good for a rainy day.

name: Split Rock Lighthouse
unique: A lighthouse on a cliff above Lake Superior, built after a 1905 storm wrecked a fleet, with keeper's quarters and a film.
buzz: The cliff setting is dramatic and the tour is good. Go on a clear day for the lake color.

name: Voyageurs National Park
unique: A water based national park of lakes and islands on the Canadian border, reached by boat, with loons, eagles and dark skies.
buzz: You need a boat or a tour, and that keeps it quiet. The fall colors and the northern lights are the reward.

name: Itasca State Park
unique: The headwaters of the Mississippi, where you can wade across the river, plus old growth pine and a lodge.
buzz: Walking across the Mississippi is the photo and the park is beautiful. The lodge is a good base.

name: Canal Park
unique: A lakefront district with a lift bridge, a maritime museum, a beach and a pier where ore boats pass through.
buzz: The lift bridge and the ships are the draw, and the lake walk is windy and beautiful.

name: Yankee Stadium Tour
customer: Baseball fans, families, visiting sports crowds
unique: The dugout, the press box and Monument Park in one walk, with a guide who has usually worked in the building since the old stadium came down.
buzz: Fans rate the guide stories above the memorabilia; weekend tours sell out and the field is off limits on game days.

name: Bronx Zoo
unique: 265 acres of the Bronx River valley holding Congo Gorilla Forest, a monorail over the Asian plains and a bison herd descended from the animals that started the American conservation movement.
buzz: The gorillas and tigers carry it; ride the Wild Asia monorail early and skip the indoor exhibits at midday when school groups fill them.

name: New York Botanical Garden
unique: A 250 acre Olmsted plan around the Haupt conservatory, with a patch of old growth forest that was never cut and a holiday train show that runs model trains past New York landmarks built out of bark.
buzz: Regulars insist on the conservatory plus the forest trail; the orchid show in spring is the busiest week of the year and needs a timed ticket.

name: Arthur Avenue Retail Market
customer: Food people, Italian American families, curious eaters
unique: The indoor market where Bronx Italian families still buy pasta by the pound, cigars are rolled in the back room and mozzarella is pulled in front of you.
buzz: Go on a weekday morning when the butchers are talking; Sunday after church is a crush and half the stalls are shut by three.

name: Woodlawn Cemetery
customer: History walkers, architecture people, jazz fans
unique: 400 acres of marble and granite where Duke Ellington, Herman Melville and Miles Davis lie under mausoleums designed by McKim, Mead and White.
buzz: The weekend trolley tour is the easy way in; the gate map is good enough to walk to Ellington and Melville yourself.

name: City Island Seafood Crawl
customer: Seafood people, boat watchers, city escapees
unique: A Long Island Sound fishing village inside the city limits: one avenue of clam shacks, boatyards and a small nautical museum, reached by a city bus.
buzz: Locals argue over which fried clam wins; the point is to walk the length of City Island Avenue and eat at two or three counters.

name: MoMA PS1
unique: A Romanesque revival school building in Long Island City where the raw third floor rooms and the summer courtyard music series take more risks than most Manhattan museums.
buzz: The sound installations and courtyard parties are the draw; check what is installed before going, since an empty floor is still a big walk.

name: Queens Night Market
unique: Sixty countries of cooking at stall prices in Flushing Meadows Corona Park under the Unisphere, with a cap that keeps most plates at six dollars or less.
buzz: Arrive at five before the lines form; the Trinidadian doubles and Colombian arepas are repeat picks, and half the stalls still want cash.

name: Louis Armstrong House Museum
customer: Jazz fans, history people, design lovers
unique: The modest Corona house where Armstrong lived for 28 years, kept as he left it, with his reel to reel tapes and the mirrored bathroom he built himself.
buzz: Visitors are surprised it is a row house on a working block; the guided tour is the only way in and the summer garden concerts are the local secret.

name: Ganesh Temple Canteen
company: Hindu Temple Society of North America
customer: South Asian families, students, cheap eat hunters
unique: The basement cafeteria of the first traditional Hindu temple in the country, where dosas and idli are cooked to order for a few dollars and lunch is part of the visit.
buzz: The line moves fast, the ghee dosa is the standing order, and the kitchen closes for a stretch in mid afternoon.

name: New World Mall Food Court
customer: Food crawlers, Flushing regulars, translators in training
unique: A basement food court in downtown Flushing with thirty stalls of Sichuan, Xi'an and northern Chinese cooking, most plates under twelve dollars and almost nothing translated.
buzz: Hand pulled noodles and cumin lamb skewers are the standards; go hungry, carry cash and a translation app, and avoid Saturday noon.

name: Museum of the Moving Image
unique: The only museum where you can dub a scene, play a working 1970s arcade and see the actual Muppets, all in a converted Astoria studio.
buzz: The Henson exhibition is what people come for and the arcade buys another hour; the weekend screenings are quietly excellent.

name: Rockaway Beach Surf Lesson
unique: The only city beach where surfing is legal, with a forgiving summer beach break and a subway station two blocks from the sand.
buzz: Beginners say the whitewater is gentler than expected and the lesson plus board package is the cheapest way into the water from New York.

name: Noguchi Museum
customer: Design people, art students, quiet seekers
unique: A quiet block of Long Island City where Noguchi turned a photo studio and a gas station into ten rooms of carved stone, paper light and a gravel garden he laid out himself.
buzz: People call it the most calming hour in the city; the garden café is worth staying for and the shop sells small editions of his lamps.

name: Staten Island Ferry
unique: The last free big boat ride in the country, passing the Statue of Liberty and Ellis Island with a beer and a hot dog cheaper than any museum ticket.
buzz: Stand on the right going out and the left coming back; if you are short of time, ride over and take the subway back from St George.

name: Snug Harbor Cultural Center
unique: A Greek revival retirement home for sailors turned 83 acre campus, with a Chinese scholar's garden, a botanic garden and a working lighthouse at the edge.
buzz: The Chinese garden is the surprise that brings locals back; the campus is larger than visitors expect, so pick two buildings and walk the rest.

name: Historic Richmond Town
customer: Families, school groups, local history people
unique: Thirty original buildings around the old county seat, with trade shops where a tinsmith and a carpenter work in front of you on weekends.
buzz: Living history weekends are the time to go; on a quiet weekday half the buildings are locked and the visit is over in an hour.

name: Jacques Marchais Museum of Tibetan Art
unique: A stone temple built into a Staten Island hillside by a self taught collector, with a terrace pond that looks lifted out of Ladakh.
buzz: Small, strange and peaceful; the terrace view is what people remember and several of the bronzes are genuinely old.

name: Alice Austen House
unique: The 17th century farmhouse where a Victorian photographer documented immigrant New York, now a museum of her glass plates with a lawn over the Narrows.
buzz: Photographers come for the archive and stay for the porch; it is a 20 minute walk from the ferry and pairs with the waterfront path.

name: Old Westbury Gardens
unique: A Charles II style manor with 200 acres of walled garden, allee and pond, built for an heir to the Phipps steel fortune and used as a set for Gatsby and The Age of Innocence.
buzz: The walled garden peaks in late May; the house tour is short and the grounds are where people spend the afternoon.

name: Sagamore Hill
unique: Theodore Roosevelt's shingle style house full of trophies, books and the rocking chair where he took calls, above a cove on Cold Spring Harbor.
buzz: The ranger led house tour is the only way inside and sells out; the trail down to the beach is short and usually empty.

name: Cradle of Aviation Museum
customer: Aviation people, families, rainy day crowds
unique: Hangars of Grumman fighters, a Lunar Module and the radar dome from Mitchell Field, telling how Long Island plants built the planes that won the Pacific.
buzz: Aviation people call it underrated; the cockpit exhibits and planetarium make it the reliable rainy day backup for families.

name: Jones Beach State Park
unique: Robert Moses built six miles of ocean beach with a brick water tower and a boardwalk designed to feel like an ocean liner, and it still works as a day out.
buzz: Arrive early in summer or the lots close; the west end is quieter, the east bathhouse has the food, and the boardwalk is flat enough for anyone.

name: Vanderbilt Museum and Planetarium
unique: A Spanish revival mansion on a Centerport bluff holding William Vanderbilt's natural history trophies and marine collection, plus a planetarium in the old garage court.
buzz: The house is odd and personal in a way that sticks; planetarium shows are cheap and sunset over Northport Bay is why people linger.

name: Montauk Point Lighthouse
unique: The oldest lighthouse in the state, commissioned by Washington, at the end of a 120 mile island, with 137 steps up and a view back along the whole south shore.
buzz: The climb is tighter than people expect and the wind at the point is real; pair it with the bluffs and lunch in the harbor.

name: Fire Island National Seashore
unique: A car free barrier island of boardwalk villages, a sunken forest of holly and sassafras behind the dunes, and a lighthouse at the west end.
buzz: Kismet and Ocean Beach are the busy villages, Watch Hill is the quiet one, and the deer will take your lunch if you leave it out.

name: Long Island Aquarium
unique: A river otter and penguin operation on the Peconic with a shark tank you can snorkel and a butterfly room, small enough to finish before the children wear out.
buzz: The ray touch tank and penguin encounter are the hits; the shark snorkel is the splurge and books weeks ahead in summer.

name: Big Duck
unique: A duck shaped shop built by a Riverhead duck farmer to sell Peking ducks, now a landmark with a small museum inside and a holiday light show in December.
buzz: A ten minute stop that everybody photographs; the shop inside still sells decades old duck memorabilia.

name: Parrish Art Museum
unique: Herzog and de Meuron's long barn of a building on the Water Mill fields, showing the painters who worked the light of the South Fork from Chase to today.
buzz: The building and the studio visits carry it; locals go Friday nights when admission is free and the galleries are quiet.

name: Splish Splash
unique: A 96 acre water park in the Pine Barrens with a half pipe slide, a lazy river and enough shade that a Long Island August afternoon is survivable.
buzz: Go on a weekday and split a cabana if you have a group; lockers and tube lines are the standard complaint in July.

name: Kykuit
unique: The Rockefeller estate above the Hudson with a six story view, a basement full of Picasso tapestries and Chinese ceramics, and a terraced garden by William Welles Bosworth.
buzz: The art tour is worth the extra ticket over the classic house tour; the coach from the visitor center is mandatory and the whole thing runs like a museum.

name: Playland Park
customer: Coaster people, families, art deco fans
unique: The oldest continuously operating amusement park in the country, an art deco seaside complex where the 1929 Dragon Coaster still runs through a wooden dragon mouth.
buzz: Coaster people come for the Dragon and the historical buildings; the ride lineup is small and the westchester beach next door is the calm alternative.

name: Untermyer Gardens
unique: A walled Persian garden and a rock and water feature built for a Gilded Age lawyer, largely forgotten for decades and now restored above the Hudson in Yonkers.
buzz: The walled garden is the reveal, and the view down to the Palisades is the second one; volunteers run free weekend tours.

name: Bear Mountain State Park
unique: The wooded hill above the Hudson where the Appalachian Trail crosses a zoo of native animals, a 1920s lodge and a stone tower with a view over the river bends.
buzz: The Perkins Tower drive is the easy win, the Major Welch trail is the real hike, and the lot fills by ten on fall weekends.

name: Edward Hopper House
unique: The clapboard house where Hopper was born and painted the light he spent his life chasing, with his easel and a garden that faces the same south light.
buzz: Small and personal, and the reason to come is seeing the rooms that appear in the paintings; the upstairs gallery shows young artists.

name: Hook Mountain
unique: A short climb to a traprock ridge above the Tappan Zee where turkey vultures ride the updraft and the Palisades sit across the water like a wall.
buzz: The loop from Rockland Lake is the standard route; the ridge is narrow with real drop offs and the parking lot is tiny on weekends.

name: Manitoga
customer: Design people, mid century fans, gardeners
unique: Industrial designer Russel Wright's house built into a quarry and a woodland garden he planted by hand, with a moss floor and a pool that reflects the hemlocks.
buzz: The house tour is the only way in and it is limited; designers leave talking about the window that frames a single tree.

name: Boscobel House and Gardens
customer: House tour people, gardeners, theater goers
unique: A Federal mansion moved brick by brick in the 1950s to a bluff above the Hudson, with period furniture and a rose garden that faces West Point across the river.
buzz: The view from the lawn is the best on the Hudson; the summer Shakespeare festival on the grounds is the local tradition.

name: Breakneck Ridge
customer: Hikers, trail runners, city day trippers
unique: A rock scramble straight up the Hudson Highlands from a train station platform, three false summits and a ridge walk with the river 900 feet below.
buzz: It is the most crowded hike in the region for a reason; go before eight, wear real shoes, and skip it when the rocks are wet.

name: Motorcyclepedia Museum
unique: Eighty five thousand square feet of motorcycles including a wall of police bikes, a circular room of Indians and a 1908 Harley, put together by a collector who never sold one.
buzz: People arrive expecting a small collection and stay three hours; the police motorcycle room is the surprise.

name: Brotherhood Winery
unique: The oldest continuously operating winery in the country, with tours through brick cellars dug by hand in the 1830s and a tasting room in the old press house.
buzz: The cellar tour is the reason to go; the wine is not why oenophiles come back and the holiday events fill the place.

name: Harriman State Park
unique: Forty seven thousand acres of lakes and ridge line where Seven Lakes Drive winds past swimming beaches, a stone tower and the remains of colonial iron works.
buzz: Lake Sebago is the swim, Anthony Wayne is the easy hike, and locals guard the quieter lakes; the park is bigger than the map suggests.

name: Walkway Over the Hudson
unique: A ruined 1889 railroad bridge rebuilt as a 1.28 mile pedestrian deck 212 feet above the Hudson, with a glass elevator down to the river trail.
buzz: Sunset is the time, the wind is constant, and the elevator on the Poughkeepsie side saves the stairs; it is fully accessible.

name: Home of Franklin D. Roosevelt
unique: Springwood, the Hudson river house where Roosevelt was born and ran a presidency, with his desk, his ship models and the grave where he and Eleanor are buried in the rose garden.
buzz: The house tour and the library are separate tickets; the grounds and the Valkill cottage next door are the quiet part most people miss.

name: Culinary Institute of America
customer: Food people, couples, parents visiting students
unique: Four student run restaurants where the people cooking your lunch are weeks away from graduating, on a campus that was a Jesuit seminary above the Hudson.
buzz: Reservations are essential for the American Bounty and Bocuse rooms; the prix fixe lunch is the bargain and the bread basket is famous.

name: Mohonk Mountain House
unique: A Victorian castle on a cliff above a glacial lake, with 85 miles of carriage roads, a rock scramble called the Labyrinth and a lemonade porch that has served guests since Grant.
buzz: Day passes need booking and are not cheap; the Labyrinth and Eagle Cliff are the hike, and the porch is worth a slow hour.

name: Shawangunk Ridge Climbing
unique: The Gunks: a quartz conglomerate cliff line with horizontal cracks so friendly that beginners lead their first routes here, plus carriage roads and a raptor migration in fall.
buzz: Guides say it is the best place in the east to learn to trad climb; the carriage roads are the backup when the cliffs are crowded.

name: Opus 40
unique: A six and a half acre bluestone sculpture built by one man over 37 years in a quarry he bought for the stone, with ramps and pools that you are allowed to walk on.
buzz: People call it the best unknown place in the Catskills; the founder fell to his death at the site and is buried under the sculpture.

name: Hudson River Maritime Museum
unique: A waterfront museum with a 1890s wooden tug, a working boat shop and the story of the ice harvest and brick barges that built the river economy.
buzz: Small and well made, and the lighthouse cruise and the tug are the reasons to check the schedule before driving over.

name: New York State Museum
customer: Families, history people, rainy day crowds
unique: A free state museum with a mastodon pulled from a Orange County bog, a full sized Adirondack lean to, and the largest collection of World Trade Center artifacts in the country.
buzz: The September 11 gallery is the reason many people come; the carousel and the mineral room keep children moving.

name: USS Slater
unique: The last destroyer escort still afloat, a 1944 ship built in Tampa that crossed the Atlantic and now sits in the Port of Albany with its guns, depth charges and crew quarters intact.
buzz: The volunteer guides are frequently former navy and will talk for an hour; the ship is tight and steep and not for strollers.

name: New York State Capitol Tour
company: New York State Office of General Services
customer: Architecture people, school groups, statehouse collectors
unique: A capitol built over 32 years without a dome, with a carved stone staircase that climbs four floors without support and a hall of governors that looks like a cathedral.
buzz: The Million Dollar Staircase is the thing to see; tours are free and run on the hour, and the observation deck is open in summer.

name: Troy Waterfront Farmers Market
