unique: A year round Saturday market under a brick riverside canopy where upstate farms sell cheese, cider and mushrooms and the knife sharpener works the crowd.
buzz: Locals say it is the best market in the capital region; get there by nine for the bread and stay for lunch from a stand.

name: Oakwood Cemetery
unique: A Victorian rural cemetery on a bluff above the Hudson holding Samuel Wilson, the meat packer behind Uncle Sam, along with Civil War generals and Tiffany windows in the chapel.
buzz: The Uncle Sam grave is the photo everyone takes; the self guided map at the gate points to the Earl Chapel, which is the real monument.

name: Saratoga Race Course
customer: Racing fans, groups, families on a picnic
unique: The oldest organized sporting venue in the country, where you can bring a cooler into the grandstand apron and watch the horses come down the stretch under the same 1860s trees.
buzz: The backyard picnic area is the local move; parking is a walk, the dress code is only in the clubhouse, and Travers week is chaos.

name: Saratoga Spa Mineral Springs
unique: A state park built around mineral springs where you can fill a bottle at a pavilion with water that tastes of iron and eggs, then take a carbonated bath in the 1935 Roosevelt Baths.
buzz: The taste is the story and everybody warns you; the Roosevelt Baths need booking and the park pools are the family alternative.

name: Saratoga Performing Arts Center
unique: An amphitheater in a state park where the New York City Ballet and Philadelphia Orchestra spend the summer and the lawn seats cost less than a city parking garage.
buzz: The lawn is the experience, with people carrying in full dinners and candles; the sound is better under the shell but the atmosphere is outside.

name: Buffalo AKG Art Museum
unique: A 1905 neoclassical gallery joined to a new SANAA building of glass bridges, holding one of the best modern collections in the country and a mirrored indoor bridge over a reflecting pool.
buzz: The new building is the draw but the Clyfford Still and Rothko rooms are what artists come for; the free first Friday is when Buffalo goes.

name: Martin House
unique: The prairie house Wright built for a Buffalo businessman, restored down to the art glass, with a pergola and conservatory that run the length of the block.
buzz: Guides say the two hour tour is worth it over the one hour; the restoration is the story as much as the design.

name: Buffalo RiverWorks Kayak Tour
unique: A paddle up the Buffalo River between grain elevators the size of cathedrals, through the canal terminus where the Erie Canal met the lake.
buzz: The scale of the silos from water level is what people talk about; the water is flat and the tour is beginner friendly.

name: Buffalo Central Terminal
unique: An art deco train station abandoned since 1979, with a 225 foot concourse, a tower you can climb and water damage that makes the tile work look like a Roman bath.
buzz: The volunteer tours are irregular and sell out; photographers call it the best interior in the city and the neighborhood around it is empty.

name: George Eastman Museum
customer: Photographers, film people, house tour fans
unique: The Kodak founder's 1905 mansion turned photography museum, with a working film preservation lab, a Technicolor camera and the world's oldest photography collection.
buzz: The house and the technology galleries are separate pleasures; the dryden theatre screenings are the local film school.

name: Susan B. Anthony House
unique: The brick row house where Anthony ran the suffrage campaign and was arrested for voting, with the parlor where she kept the movement's books and the desk she worked at.
buzz: The guides carry the story and the basement kitchen is the surprise; it is a small house and the tour is under an hour.

name: Rochester Public Market
unique: A shed market that has run since 1905, with butchers, a spice stall, Jamaican patties and a Saturday morning crowd that is the most mixed room in the city.
buzz: Go Saturday before ten; the garbage plate stand across the street is the other half of the ritual.

name: Lower Falls of the Genesee
unique: A 110 foot waterfall inside the city where the Genesee cuts a gorge through 400 million year old rock, reached by a path from Maplewood Park.
buzz: Locals treat it as a secret and warn about the unofficial trails; the official overlook is a five minute walk from the lot.

name: Erie Canal Museum
unique: A museum inside the 1850 weighlock building where canal boats were weighed, with a full canal boat cabin, the original locks and a room on the engineering that made New York the Empire State.
buzz: The building is the exhibit and the weighlock is the only one left; the upstairs gallery on the canal's labor history is what surprises people.

name: Ska nonh Great Law of Peace Center
unique: A center on the shore of Onondaga Lake interpreting the Haudenosaunee confederacy and the Great Law, on the site of a French mission and a salt works.
buzz: The lake itself is the point, since it was sacred ground and later the most polluted lake in the country; the exhibits are small and the guides carry it.

name: Dinosaur Bar-B-Que
unique: The original Syracuse barbecue joint, started as a motorcycle gang's fundraiser and now a brick riverside hall with a blues stage and brisket that people drive from Albany for.
buzz: Expect a wait on weekends and order the ribs and the salt potatoes; the live music is loud and the room is louder.

name: Fort Stanwix National Monument
customer: History families, rev war people, school groups
unique: A rebuilt timber fort in the middle of downtown Rome where the 1777 siege turned back the British and where the treaty that opened the west was signed.
buzz: The rangers fire the cannon in summer and the earthworks walk is short; the museum does a good job on the Oneida alliance.

name: F.X. Matt Brewing Tour
unique: A fourth generation family brewery in a brick complex where you walk past open fermentation tanks and end in the 1888 tavern for samples of Saranac and Utica Club.
buzz: The tour is short but the tasting room and the old brewery architecture carry it; book ahead for Saturdays.

name: Binghamton Carousel Circuit
unique: Six working 1920s carousels spread across the city parks, all free to ride, part of a bequest that required them to stay free forever.
buzz: Collectors come from other states to ride all six in an afternoon; the Recreation Park carousel is the biggest and the oldest.

name: Roberson Museum and Science Center
customer: Families, local history people, planetarium fans
unique: A 1904 mansion with a planetarium bolted on, holding a model railroad of the region, a natural history hall and the only public telescope in the area.
buzz: The holiday model train show is the local tradition; the rest of the year the mansion rooms and the planetarium are the draw.

name: Taughannock Falls State Park
unique: A 215 foot waterfall that drops into a rock amphitheater, taller than Niagara, with a flat gorge trail that takes you to the plunge pool.
buzz: The gorge trail is easy and the rim trail is the view; in winter the falls freeze and the trail becomes a ice walk.

name: Cornell Lab of Ornithology
unique: The research lab behind eBird and the Macaulay Library, with a viewing tower over Sapsucker Woods and a wall of screens playing recordings from every continent.
buzz: Birders call the sound lab the best free attraction in the state; the trails are flat and the tower is open year round.

name: Moosewood Restaurant
unique: The worker owned vegetarian restaurant that produced the best selling cookbook of its kind, still in a converted downtown Ithaca building with a menu that changes daily.
buzz: People arrive expecting a legend and get a busy casual room; the soups and the daily specials are the order, and the cookbook shelf is by the door.

name: Chautauqua Institution
unique: A gated Victorian village on a lake where the nine week summer program mixes daily lectures, a symphony, a ballet and a religion hall, all within walking distance of 19th century cottages.
buzz: The gate pass and parking are the hassle; once inside people describe it as summer camp for adults and stay for the amphitheater evening.

name: National Comedy Center
unique: A museum where you build a personal comedy profile at the door and the exhibits adapt to it, with Carlin's notebooks, a comedy club stage and a hologram room.
buzz: People expect a small town museum and get two hours of interactive exhibits; the adult only late nights are the local favorite.

name: Lucille Ball Desi Arnaz Museum
customer: TV people, families, I Love Lucy fans
unique: Lucille Ball's hometown museum with the actual Ricardo living room set, her costumes and a recreation of the chocolate factory wrapping line.
buzz: Fans love the costumes and the set; non fans are done in an hour, and the comedy center next door is the better value.

name: Ausable Chasm
unique: A sandstone gorge cut by the Ausable River with a mile of wooden walkways on the rim, a raft float through the inner chasm and a tube run down the side.
buzz: The raft through the gorge is the thing to book; the rim walk alone is fine but the water is the point and it is cold in June.

name: Point Au Roche State Park
unique: A peninsula of Lake Champlain shoreline with a shallow sand beach, a paved bike loop and a wetland boardwalk where the lake narrows toward Vermont.
buzz: Locals call it the quiet alternative to the city beach; the lake is shallow and warm by August and the bike path is flat.

name: Prospect Mountain Veterans Memorial Highway
unique: A five and a half mile road up a 2,030 foot peak with three pull offs, ending in a view of Lake George and the Adirondack high peaks on one side and Vermont on the other.
buzz: Sunset is the time and the road closes at dusk; the shuttle from the village in summer is easier than parking at the top.

name: Fort William Henry
unique: A rebuilt French and Indian War fort at the head of Lake George with musket and cannon firing, a stockade you can walk and a museum on the massacre that Cooper turned into a novel.
buzz: The live firing schedule is what children remember; the tour guides are in period dress and the lake view from the ramparts is the postcard.

name: Boldt Castle
unique: A six story granite and limestone castle on an island in the St. Lawrence, abandoned mid construction in 1904 when the builder's wife died, now reached only by boat.
buzz: The boat ride through the islands is half the trip; the upper floors were never finished and the story carries the tour.

name: Antique Boat Museum
unique: The largest collection of antique wooden runabouts in the country, in a riverside boatyard where you can row a skiff or ride in a 1930s launch.
buzz: Boat people call it a pilgrimage; the river cruise in a wooden launch is the add on worth paying for.

name: Sackets Harbor Battlefield
unique: The naval base that kept the American fleet on Lake Ontario during the War of 1812, with earthworks, a navy yard and a view across the harbor to the Canadian shore.
buzz: The hilltop earthworks are the walk; the reconstructed barracks and the summer reenactment are the reason to check the calendar.

name: Whiteface Veterans Memorial Highway
company: New York State Olympic Regional Development Authority
unique: An eight mile road that climbs to a parking lot at 4,500 feet, where a tunnel and elevator take you the last 300 feet to a summit view of the Adirondacks and Vermont.
buzz: The elevator through the mountain is the quirk; bring a jacket, since it is 20 degrees colder up top even in July.

name: Fort Ticonderoga
customer: Rev war people, families, history teachers
unique: The stone fort at the narrows between Lake George and Lake Champlain, taken by Ethan Allen's Green Mountain Boys and later by Burgoyne, with a garden and boat tours on the lake.
buzz: The fife and drum and the cannon demonstration run on a schedule; the hours between events are best spent on the walls and in the museum.

name: Cave of the Winds
unique: A wooden walkway rebuilt every spring that takes you to within 20 feet of Bridal Veil Falls, where the wind is 70 mph and the rain is going up.
buzz: The Hurricane Deck is the whole point and the poncho is useless; go early or late to avoid the tour bus hours.

name: Old Fort Niagara
unique: The oldest continuously occupied military site in North America, with a French castle from 1726, earthworks above Lake Ontario and a view of the Toronto skyline on a clear day.
buzz: The castle is small and the walls are the walk; the summer French and Indian War encampment is the day to come.

name: Harris Hill Glider Ride
customer: First time flyers, aviation people, gift buyers
unique: A sailplane ride off the ridge that hosted the first national soaring contest in 1930, where the engine is a tow plane and the silence after release is the attraction.
buzz: Riders say the 20 minute flight feels longer and the thermal over the Chemung valley is the ride; book a week out and expect weather cancellations.

name: National Soaring Museum
unique: The country's hang glider and sailplane archive on Harris Hill, with 50 gliders overhead and a workshop where you can watch a wooden wing being rebuilt.
buzz: Small but serious; combine it with a glider ride next door and the day makes sense.

name: Mark Twain Study
unique: The octagonal study where Twain wrote most of Huckleberry Finn, moved from his sister in law's hilltop farm to the Elmira College campus and kept as he left it.
buzz: It is a small wooden room and the visit is short, which is the point; the campus also has his grave in Woodlawn Cemetery nearby.

name: Harriet Tubman Home
customer: History people, students, civil rights pilgrims
unique: The brick house Tubman bought from William Seward, the home for aged people she ran next door, and the African Methodist Episcopal Zion church where her funeral was held.
buzz: The ranger tour ties the property to the underground railroad and her later life; the church across town is a separate stop on the same story.

name: Seward House Museum
customer: History people, house tour fans, students
unique: The Auburn home of Lincoln's secretary of state, with the desk where he wrote the Alaska purchase, a hidden staircase and a collection of Civil War flags.
buzz: The guided tour is the only way through and the guides know the Alaska story cold; the garden and the carriage house are included.

name: Merry-Go-Round Playhouse
unique: A professional musical theater in a 1930s carousel building in a state park, where Broadway actors do summer stock beside a lake.
buzz: Locals say the productions are better than a small city deserves; bring a picnic and arrive early for the park.

name: Sonnenberg Gardens and Mansion
unique: A Victorian mansion with nine formal gardens built for a banker and his wife, including a Japanese garden, a rock garden and a 1903 greenhouse range still in use.
buzz: The Japanese garden and the greenhouse are the highlights; the mansion is partly unrestored, which regulars prefer.

name: CMAC Summer Concert
unique: An open air amphitheater on the Canandaigua lakefront where the lawn slopes toward the stage and the sunset happens behind the audience.
buzz: The lawn is the value and the wine from the region is allowed in; the covered seats are for rain and the parking lot takes an hour to clear.

name: Canandaigua Lake Paddle
unique: A clear glacial lake below the Bristol Hills with a city beach at one end and a shoreline of docks, cottages and a few protected coves.
buzz: Morning is flat and empty and the lake gets choppy by afternoon; rentals are at the north end and the state park launch is quieter.

name: Stony Brook State Park
unique: A gorge of three waterfalls and stone stairs cut into the cliff, with a swimming area at the bottom and a trail that climbs beside the falls.
buzz: The gorge trail is closed in ice season; in summer the creek pools are the swimming and the stairs get slick.

name: New York State Festival of Balloons
unique: A small town balloon festival where 40 balloons launch at dawn and dusk from a field above the Genesee valley, with a night glow and no gate fee.
buzz: The 6am launch is the one and the wind decides everything; bring a blanket, coffee and patience, and expect to park in a farm field.

name: Conesus Lake
unique: The westernmost Finger Lake, ringed by cottages and a state park beach, with a July 3 ring of fire where every dock lights a flare at once.
buzz: The ring of fire is the local event of the year and the lake is packed that night; the rest of the summer it is quiet on weekdays.

name: Batavia Downs
unique: A half mile harness track where the horses come straight at you down the stretch and a two dollar bet lasts a whole evening.
buzz: Locals bring folding chairs to the apron and explain the betting to newcomers; the casino inside is louder than the track.

name: Holland Land Office Museum
unique: The stone land office where the Holland Land Company sold off western New York by the acre, with the survey maps and the strongbox that made Batavia the capital of the frontier.
buzz: Genealogists come for the deed records and find the building itself is the exhibit; it is small and staffed by volunteers.

name: Iroquois National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Ten thousand acres of marsh and hardwood between Lake Ontario and the Niagara escarpment, with an eagle nest, a driving loop and spring migration that fills the trees.
buzz: Birders time it for the first week of May; the observation deck at Cayuga Pool is where the photographers set up at dawn.

name: Allegany State Park
unique: Sixty five thousand acres of Allegheny plateau with two lakes, a stone casino built by the CCC and trails that run to the Pennsylvania line.
buzz: The Red House and Quaker areas are the two bases; the CCC casino is the rainy day building and the fall color is the peak season.

name: Griffis Sculpture Park
unique: Four hundred acres of hillside where a sculptor planted 250 steel figures among the trees, including a field of giant heads you can walk between.
buzz: People call it the strangest free art walk in the state; wear boots, since the trails are mown grass and the hills are real.

name: Ellicottville and Holiday Valley
unique: A one street village of bars and gear shops below a ski hill that runs 750 vertical feet, with a summer jazz festival and mountain coaster.
buzz: Buffalo and Toronto both claim it in winter; the bars on Washington Street are the apres scene and the mountain is beginner friendly.

name: The Wild Center
unique: A natural history museum of the Adirondacks with an elevated walkway through the treetops, otters, and a bog you can walk into without getting wet.
buzz: The Wild Walk canopy is the reason people drive three hours; the otter tank and the forest music installation are the sleepers.

name: Saranac Laboratory Museum
customer: Science people, history walkers, TB families
unique: The first laboratory in the country built for tuberculosis research, where the cure was studied and where the village of cure cottages outside grew up around it.
buzz: The docents tell the story of the patients who came for the air; the lab is small and the walking tour of the cure cottages is the better half.

name: Six Nations Iroquois Cultural Center
unique: A small museum in the Adirondack woods with a reconstructed longhouse, dugout canoes, beadwork and a collection put together by a Mohawk family over three generations.
buzz: Visitors are surprised by the quality of the collection and the personal tour; it is off the main road and worth the detour.

name: Adirondack Experience
unique: A campus museum on Blue Mountain Lake with a guideboat hall, a 19th century great camp, a logging exhibit you walk through and a working blacksmith.
buzz: The guideboat collection is the surprise and the camp buildings are the reason to give it three hours; the lake view from the porch is the rest.

name: Great Camp Sagamore
unique: Vanderbilt's 27 building Adirondack camp of log and twig work on a private lake, with a bowling alley and a guideboat fleet, reachable only by a long dirt road.
buzz: The guided tour is the only way in and people describe the scale as a national park lodge; stay overnight if you can, the rooms are original.

name: Blue Mountain Lake Paddle
unique: A deep clear lake under Blue Mountain with islands to land on, loon calls at dusk and a state campground on the shore.
buzz: The lake is quiet before nine and the wind picks up at noon; the islands are public and the mountain trail starts across the road.

name: Northeast Classic Car Museum
unique: A former lumber warehouse holding 160 cars from a 1908 Cadillac to muscle cars, arranged in period scenes with mannequins and garage signs.
buzz: Car people call it one of the best small collections in the east; the cars run and the volunteers will start one for you.

name: Rogers Environmental Education Center
unique: A wildlife education center on the Chenango River with a trout pond, a bird observation room and trails through old growth hemlock.
buzz: The bird feeders outside the window are the attraction in winter; it is free and the trails are flat enough for small children.

name: Bowman Lake State Park
unique: A spring fed lake in the hills with a sandy beach, a campground under tall pines and a nine hole disc golf course in the woods.
buzz: Locals come for the beach in July and the quiet in September; the lake is small and the hike around it takes an hour.

name: Cuba Cheese Shoppe
unique: A cheese shop in the town that supplied New York's cheese market for a century, with a cut to order counter, cheese curds and a viewing window into the plant.
buzz: The curds are the reason people detour and they sell out by afternoon; the shop is small and the sandwich counter is the local lunch.

name: Angelica Village
unique: A Genesee valley village of Greek revival and Italianate houses around a park with a civil war monument, largely unchanged since the 1830s and used as a film location.
buzz: Architecture people call it a time capsule; the antique shops and the inn make it a half day, and the drive through the valley is the point.

name: Palmer Opera House
customer: Theater people, local music fans, history buffs
unique: A restored 1903 opera house on the second floor of a main street block, with painted backdrops, wooden benches and a season of community theater and touring bands.
buzz: The room itself is the attraction and the acoustics are better than the seats; check the calendar before driving, it is not open daily.

name: Barnes Foundation
unique: Dr. Barnes collected 181 Renoirs, 69 Cezannes and 59 Matisses and hung them in ensembles meant to teach visual thinking, now in a Tod Williams building on the Parkway.
buzz: The hang is the lesson and people either love or fight it; book a timed ticket and give it three hours, the collection is denser than it looks.

name: Philadelphia's Magic Gardens
customer: Mosaic people, photographers, South Street wanderers
unique: Half a block of South Street tiled by Isaiah Zagar with bottles, mirrors, bicycle wheels and folk art, with a basement grotto you crawl through.
buzz: People come for a photo and stay for the story of the neighborhood; the outdoor lot needs a ticket and the surrounding alleys are free.

name: Italian Market
unique: Nine blocks of 9th Street where cheesemakers, butchers and tortilla factories still work behind open counters, with the Philadelphia side of the market running since the 1880s.
buzz: Go on a weekday morning and start at the top; the weekend crowd is a wall and the produce prices are the best in the city.

name: Andy Warhol Museum
unique: Seven floors holding 900 paintings, the Silver Clouds room and Warhol's time capsules, in the industrial building on the North Shore where he was born a few miles away.
buzz: The top floor films and the cloud room are the ones people remember; the permanent collection is so deep that a second visit is different.

name: Duquesne Incline
company: Society for the Preservation of the Duquesne Heights Incline
unique: A wooden 1877 funicular up Mount Washington, still run by hand by a operator in the upper station, ending at the three rivers view that defines the city.
buzz: Ride up at dusk and walk down the steps or take it back; the upper station has a small museum of the machinery and the fare is cash friendly.

name: Phipps Conservatory
unique: A Victorian glasshouse in Schenley Park with a tropical forest under glass, a butterfly room and a Center for Sustainable Landscapes that is one of the greenest buildings in the world.
buzz: The winter flower show is the local tradition and the summer butterfly room is the family draw; the glasshouse is hot in July.

name: Kennywood
unique: A trolley park from 1898 with three wooden coasters, a 1920s Noah's Ark walkthrough and the Thunderbolt, all on a bluff above the Monongahela.
buzz: Coaster people rank the Phantom's Revenge and the Jack Rabbit; the park is small enough that a day pass covers everything twice.

name: Lancaster Central Market
unique: The oldest continuously operating farmers market in the country, in a brick hall where Amish farm stands sell scrapple, chow chow and whoopie pies beside Lebanese and Jamaican counters.
buzz: Saturday is the crush and Tuesday is the locals; the smoked meats and the pretzels are the standing orders and cash is still normal.

name: Strasburg Rail Road
unique: The oldest short line railroad in the country, running a steam locomotive 45 minutes through Amish farm fields from a 1830s depot.
buzz: Book the open air car and sit on the left; children want the steam engine and the shop sells the wooden version for the ride home.

name: Amish Farm and House
customer: Families, first time visitors, school groups
unique: A 1805 farmhouse and working farm where a guide explains Amish schooling, barn raising and plain dress, with a bus tour into the back roads.
buzz: The house tour is better than the bus for understanding the religion; visitors say the guides answer the awkward questions honestly.

name: Harley-Davidson York Factory Tour
customer: Motorcycle people, engineers, families with teens
unique: The plant where every Harley frame and fuel tank is made and painted, walked on a catwalk above the assembly line with closed toe shoes required.
buzz: Riders call it a pilgrimage and non riders are surprised by the robots; tours fill weeks out and the plant shuts in some holiday weeks.

name: York Central Market
unique: A two story brick market house with a balcony of lunch counters, where York's German farm stands became Pennsylvania Dutch lunch stands over 130 years.
buzz: The pretzel and the chicken corn soup are the orders; it is smaller than Lancaster's and easier to actually shop.

name: Pennsylvania State Capitol
customer: Architecture people, school groups, statehouse collectors
unique: A Beaux Arts capitol Roosevelt called the handsomest in the nation, with a 272 foot dome, Moravian tiles and a limestone staircase modeled on the Paris opera.
buzz: The free tour is the only way into the rotunda and the House chamber; the tile work is what visitors photograph.

name: National Civil War Museum
unique: A hilltop museum that tells the war from both sides with a balance rare among Civil War sites, from the 1850s causes through reconstruction, with a large collection of soldiers' letters.
buzz: Visitors say it is the honest overview the battlefields do not give; the walk up the hill is steep and the view over Harrisburg is the bonus.

name: Broad Street Market
unique: Two brick market houses from the Civil War era, one of the oldest continuously operating markets in the country, with Pennsylvania Dutch stands and a growing row of Syrian and Vietnamese counters.
buzz: The stone building is the food hall and the brick building is the produce; go hungry and expect a line at the sandwich stands.

name: US Army Heritage and Education Center
unique: A free army museum with a mile long outdoor trail of reproduced fortifications from the French and Indian War to Vietnam, plus a research library of soldiers' letters.
buzz: The outdoor heritage trail is the surprise and you can walk inside a bunker and a trench; the indoor galleries are small and rotate.

name: Appalachian Trail Museum
unique: The only museum devoted to the Appalachian Trail, in an 1820s ironmaster's mansion where thru hikers still stop for a bunk, with packs, boots and journals from the trail.
buzz: Thru hikers sign the register and volunteers feed them; in June the porch is full of people who walked from Georgia.

name: Dorney Park
unique: A 1884 trolley park with a 1920s carousel, a steel hypercoaster and a water park on the same ticket, in the hills above Allentown.
buzz: The water park is the summer value and the coasters are the reason enthusiasts come; weekdays in June are empty enough to loop everything.

name: America on Wheels Museum
customer: Car and truck people, families, dads
unique: A transportation museum on the Lehigh River with a Mack truck gallery, a 1950s gas station and a rotating exhibit of cars you can walk around and under.
buzz: The truck room is what makes it different from every car museum; it is small and the admission is cheap enough for a rainy hour.

name: SteelStacks
unique: The Bethlehem Steel plant turned arts campus, where the blast furnaces stand lit at night above a lawn that hosts free summer concerts and a film series.
buzz: The furnaces at night are the photograph everyone takes; the free Levitt Pavilion shows are the local summer ritual.

name: National Museum of Industrial History
unique: A Smithsonian affiliate in a former Bethlehem Steel building, with a working steam engine, the only remaining screw propeller from the Titanic's sister ship and a silk loom you can run.
buzz: The volunteers start the engines and talk forever; the machine shop is the best part and children can operate several exhibits.

name: Crayola Experience
unique: The crayon factory's visitor center where children name and wrap their own crayon, mold wax and watch how a crayon is made, in the town where Crayola began.
buzz: Parents say three hours is the limit and the meltdown happens at the gift shop; buy tickets online and go at opening.

name: Steamtown National Historic Site
unique: A working rail yard in the old Lackawanna shops with a roundhouse, a turntable you can watch turn a locomotive and short steam excursions through the valley.
buzz: Train people spend all day and families do the roundhouse and the short ride; check the excursion schedule before going.

name: Lackawanna Coal Mine Tour
unique: A mine car drops you 300 feet into a anthracite seam where a former miner explains the work at a temperature of 53 degrees year round.
buzz: The guides are retired miners and the stories are the tour; bring a jacket and expect to duck, the seam is low.

name: Houdini Museum
customer: Magic fans, families, curious road trippers
unique: A magic museum and theater in a Scranton house where a working magician gives a tour of Houdini's handcuffs and escape trunks, then performs a show.
buzz: It is part museum and part vaudeville and children are the right audience; the tour and show run as one ticket.

name: Bushkill Falls
unique: Eight waterfalls on a privately owned gorge with boardwalks and stairs, the tallest dropping 100 feet, reached by a mile of trail in the Poconos.
buzz: The red trail covers everything and takes two hours; it is a paid attraction, which people either resent or appreciate for the upkeep.

name: Delaware Water Gap
unique: The river cuts through the Kittatinny Ridge at a notch you can climb above on the Appalachian Trail, with a beach, a canoe launch and a view of New Jersey from the top.
buzz: The Mount Tammany red dot trail is steep and crowded and the reward is the gap from above; the river beach is the easy alternative.

name: Pocono Raceway
unique: A triangle shaped superspeedway where you can camp inside the infield, watch three turns at once and see the cars come at you down the long front stretch.
buzz: The infield camping is the experience and the traffic afterwards is the warning; the July race is the big one.

name: Presque Isle State Park
company: Pennsylvania Department of Conservation and Natural Resources
unique: A seven mile sand spit curving into Lake Erie with eleven beaches, a flat multi use trail and a lagoon where migrating birds pile up in spring.
buzz: Sunsets over the bay side are the local ritual; the peninsula trail is flat and the beaches get crowded only in July.

name: Erie Maritime Museum
unique: The home port of the Brig Niagara, Perry's reconstructed flagship from the Battle of Lake Erie, with a museum on the 1813 battle and a winter shipyard you can watch.
buzz: Sailing on the Niagara is the splurge and books out; the museum alone explains why a freshwater lake had a naval war.

name: Waldameer Park
unique: A trolley era park with a 1908 carousel, a wooden coaster and a water park, free to enter so you can walk the midway without buying a ride wristband.
buzz: Locals love that admission is free and parking is cheap; the Ravine Flyer II is the coaster enthusiasts come for.

name: Mercer Museum
customer: Tool people, history fans, architecture students
unique: A concrete castle built to hold one man's collection of pre-industrial American tools, with a whaleboat hanging from the ceiling and a walkway that spirals up through six floors.
buzz: The building is the exhibit and people describe it as a cathedral of hand tools; allow two hours because every case has something strange.

name: Fonthill Castle
unique: Henry Mercer's concrete house with 44 rooms, 32 stairwells and a ceiling of Moravian tiles, built by hand with no architect and no plan.
buzz: The guided tour is the only way in and the stairs are steep; visitors say it feels like a medieval house built by a obsessive.

name: Valley Forge National Historical Park
unique: The winter camp where Washington's army survived 1777 with a reconstructed log city, earthworks you can walk and a 3,500 acre park with a bike trail through it.
buzz: The ranger talks and the Muhlenberg Brigade huts are the best part; the loop road is flat and the park is free, which surprises people.

name: Bryn Athyn Cathedral
company: General Church of the New Jerusalem
customer: Architecture people, stained glass fans, quiet seekers
unique: A Gothic cathedral built by hand in the 1910s by craftsmen who worked without straight lines, with glass made on the grounds and a hilltop view over the Pennypack valley.
buzz: Architects call the craftsmanship a century ahead of its time; the cathedral is free and the neighboring Glencairn Museum is the paid tour.

name: Brandywine River Museum
unique: A converted gristmill on the Brandywine holding three generations of Wyeth paintings, including the Olson House canvases and N.C. Wyeth's illustrations.
buzz: The top floor galleries with the Andrew Wyeth rooms are the reason to come; the mill windows look out on the river he painted.

name: Hawk Mountain Sanctuary
unique: The ridge where the modern raptor count began, with a lookout over the Kittatinny where hundreds of hawks and eagles pass on a good September day.
buzz: Volunteers with clickers will teach you to identify a bird on the wing; the North Lookout is a short steep walk and the trail system continues for miles.

name: Reading Pagoda
unique: A seven story Japanese pagoda built on a Pennsylvania mountain in 1908 by a manufacturer who never saw Japan, now a landmark above the city with a view of five counties.
buzz: It is a free oddity with a real view; the tower interior is closed most of the time and the hillside garden is where people sit.

name: Yuengling Brewery Tour
unique: America's oldest brewery, dug into a hillside where the cellars are 150 feet of hand cut sandstone and the tour ends with samples in a 19th century bottling house.
buzz: The cave cellars are the part people remember; tours are free but fill early and the tasting is short.

name: Pioneer Tunnel Coal Mine
unique: A narrow gauge mine train that carries you 1,800 feet into a working anthracite vein, then a steam locomotive ride on the surface along the old colliery.
buzz: The guides are former miners and the mine is cold; children like the train and adults like the stories about breaker boys.

name: Knoebels Amusement Resort
unique: A free admission park in the woods with three wood coasters, a 1913 carousel, a coal fired steam train and pierogies, all priced by the ride.
buzz: Enthusiasts rank Phoenix among the best wooden coasters in the world; families like that parking and admission are free and food is cheap.

name: Bloomsburg Fair
unique: The largest agricultural fair in the state, nine days of draft horse pulls, a mile of food stands and a grandstand concert series in a town of 15,000.
buzz: Locals take the week off; the livestock barns and the harness racing are the real fair and the midway is the noise around it.

name: Horseshoe Curve
unique: A 1.8 mile curve engineered in 1854 to lift the Pennsylvania Railroad over the Alleghenies, with a funicular up to a viewing park where 100 car freight trains still grind past.
buzz: Check the train schedule at the visitor center and time your visit; the funicular and the view of the curve from above are the whole experience.

name: Railroaders Memorial Museum
customer: Train people, families, labor history fans
unique: The old PRR master mechanics building holding a K4 steam locomotive, a cab you can climb into and the story of the Altoona shops that built and repaired the railroad.
buzz: The simulator and the cab are for children and the labor history galleries are for adults; combine it with Horseshoe Curve on one ticket.

name: Johnstown Flood Museum
unique: The 1889 flood that killed 2,200 people when a private dam gave way, told in the old Carnegie library with a relief map, survivor accounts and an Oscar winning film.
buzz: The film runs on a loop and still lands; visitors say the scale of the disaster is hard to hold until you see the map of the valley.

name: Johnstown Inclined Plane
unique: The steepest vehicular inclined plane in the world at 70 percent grade, built as an escape route after the flood and still carrying cars and people up the hill.
buzz: The ride is short and the view from the top over the Conemaugh valley is the point; the operator will explain the counterweight.

name: Flight 93 National Memorial
unique: A field in Somerset County where the fourth hijacked plane came down, marked by a white marble wall that follows the flight path and a tower of wind chimes with a bell for each passenger.
buzz: The walk from the visitor center to the wall is a quarter mile and the sound of the wind chimes is what people describe; it is quiet and free.

name: Laurel Hill State Park
unique: A CCC built lake and beach in the Laurel Highlands with a hemlock gorge trail and a spillway that freezes into ice climbs in winter.
buzz: The beach is the summer draw and the gorge trail is the walk; the ice climbing at the spillway is a local winter secret.

name: Penn's Cave
unique: The only all water cave tour in the country, a flat bottom boat through a limestone passage under a mountain and out the other side, with a wildlife park above.
buzz: The boat is the whole tour and children love it; the cave is 52 degrees and the wildlife park is a separate walk.

name: Berkey Creamery
unique: The university dairy that makes ice cream from its own herd and sells it in a plant on campus, with a viewing window over the production floor.
buzz: The lines run out the door on football weekends and the Peachy Paterno was renamed; the half gallon is the move if you are driving.

name: Little League World Series
unique: The world championship for 12 year olds, played on a hillside field where fans sit on the grass and teams from Japan, Venezuela and Texas stay in the same village.
buzz: Admission is free and the hill fills early; locals say the international teams and the Lamade Stadium atmosphere beat most professional games.

name: Millionaires' Row
unique: A street of lumber baron mansions from the 1880s and 1890s, some 40 rooms with ballrooms and Tiffany windows, when Williamsport was the lumber capital of the world.
buzz: The self guided walking tour brochure is at the visitor center; several houses are now law offices and one is a museum.

name: Pennsylvania Grand Canyon
unique: A 47 mile gorge of Pine Creek with two rim overlooks, a rail trail at the bottom and 800 foot rock walls that turn orange in October.
buzz: The west rim overlooks are the easy view and the Turkey Path is the steep way down; the canyon is at its best in the first week of October.

name: Pine Creek Rail Trail
unique: A 62 mile crushed stone trail down the floor of the Grand Canyon of Pennsylvania along Pine Creek, with shuttle services that drop you at the top.
buzz: The down hill run from Ansonia to Jersey Shore is the standard half day; the shuttle books out in fall and the trail is flat enough for hybrids.

name: Kinzua Bridge Skywalk
unique: A 301 foot tall railroad viaduct that a tornado tore down in 2003, now a glass floored observation deck at the edge of the wreckage with the twisted towers still standing in the valley.
buzz: The glass floor is the thrill and the fallen towers are the photo; the walk out is 600 feet and the valley is best in fall.

name: Eldred World War II Museum
unique: A volunteer museum in a small town with a room for each theater of the war, mannequins in original uniforms and a collection of home front ration books and letters.
buzz: Visitors say the personal donations make it better than the big museums; it is free will donation and the volunteers are often veterans.

name: Zippo/Case Museum
unique: The factory museum where the lighter that became a soldier's talisman is displayed with the case knives, including the prototypes and the lifetime guarantee repair bench.
buzz: Collectors come from overseas and the staff still repair any Zippo for free; the museum is free and takes an hour.

name: French Azilum
unique: A planned refuge for French aristocrats fleeing the revolution, built in the Pennsylvania wilderness in 1793, with the foundation of the house meant for Marie Antoinette.
buzz: The story is better than the remains and the volunteer guides tell it well; it is a quiet stop on a back road along the Susquehanna.

name: Polymath Park
unique: A hillside with three Frank Lloyd Wright houses, two of them moved here from elsewhere, that you can tour and then sleep in.
buzz: Wright people call it the only place to stay overnight in a Wright house in the east; tours need booking and the houses are small.

name: Idlewild Park
unique: A 1878 trolley park in the Laurel Highlands with Storybook Forest, a 1930s walk through nursery rhymes, and a wooden coaster in the woods.
buzz: Parents say Storybook Forest is the reason to come before children turn eight; the water park and the coaster extend the day.

name: Hersheypark
unique: A chocolate company's employee picnic ground turned 121 acre park with 15 coasters, a water park and a zoo, ringed by the smell of cocoa from the factory.
buzz: Candymonium and Skyrush are the coaster draws; buy tickets online, arrive at opening and use the preview night if you are staying over.

name: Hershey's Chocolate World
unique: A free visitor center with a singing animatronic ride through the chocolate making process, a factory viewing line and a create your own chocolate bar counter.
buzz: The ride is free and dated in a way people love; the lines for the custom bar are long and the parking is paid.

name: Museum of Fine Arts
customer: Art people, students, rainy day crowds
unique: A encyclopedic collection with the country's deepest holdings of Japanese prints, a whole Egyptian tomb chapel and Sargent's murals in the rotunda.
buzz: The Americas wing and the Impressionists are the usual route; the free hour at the end of the day is the local trick.

name: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum
customer: Art people, garden lovers, mystery readers
unique: A Venetian palace built around a flowering courtyard, with paintings hung where the founder left them and empty frames where the 1990 theft took thirteen works.
buzz: The courtyard is the first thing people mention and the empty frames the second; the new wing café is the quiet lunch.

name: Walden Pond
unique: The pond where Thoreau built his cabin, with a replica of the house, a trail around the shore and a beach where people still swim in water clear enough to see the bottom.
buzz: Go early in summer or the lot closes; the cabin site is a half mile walk and the far shore is quiet even on hot days.

name: Harvard Museum of Natural History
unique: The Blaschka glass flowers, 4,300 models made of glass in the 1880s so accurate that botanists still use them, plus a whale skeleton ceiling and a mineral gallery.
buzz: People come for the glass flowers and are surprised by the zoology galleries; the whole museum takes two hours and is good in any weather.

name: Adams National Historical Park
unique: Two presidential birthplaces and the mansion where four generations of Adamses lived, toured by trolley with a ranger who knows the family letters.
buzz: The trolley between the houses is part of the ticket and the library is the quiet highlight; the tour is ranger led and sells out in summer.

name: Blue Hills Reservation
unique: Seven thousand acres of rocky hills inside the Boston beltway, with a 635 foot summit tower, a ski area and trails that feel like New Hampshire.
buzz: The Skyline Trail is the real hike and takes most of a day; locals go on weekday evenings and the summit is a 30 minute climb from the reservation lot.

name: Peabody Essex Museum
customer: Art people, maritime history fans, families
unique: The oldest continuously operating museum in the country, with a Qing dynasty house moved from China, maritime paintings and a Yin Yu Tang courtyard you walk through.
buzz: The Chinese house is the reason people stay an extra hour; the maritime galleries are quieter than the witch museums down the street.

name: Crane Beach
unique: Four miles of barrier beach backed by dunes and a salt marsh, with a greenhead-free ocean side and a trail through the marsh to Ipswich Bay.
buzz: The parking fee is steep and the beach is worth it; the marsh trail at low tide is the quiet alternative when the lot fills.

name: Edaville Family Theme Park
customer: Families with small children, train people
unique: A narrow gauge railroad built to run through cranberry bogs, with a steam engine, a holiday lights season and rides scaled for children under ten.
buzz: The Christmas lights train is the tradition and the summer crowd is thin; parents say one visit a year is enough for older children.

name: Plymouth Long Beach
unique: A three mile sand spit that looks back at Plymouth's waterfront and out to the Gurnet lighthouse, with warm shallow water on the bay side.
buzz: Locals park at the town lot and walk on; the tip at the Gurnet is the walk and the beach is quieter than the Cape.

name: Cape Cod Rail Trail
unique: Twenty two paved miles of old railroad through cranberry bogs, cedar swamp and Cape villages, with bike rentals and a rail trail that reaches the National Seashore.
buzz: The Nickerson State Park stretch is the prettiest and the grade is gentle; rent at Dennis or Orleans and ride one way.

name: Cape Cod Potato Chip Factory Tour
unique: A self guided window tour over the fryers where small batches of kettle chips are cooked, with a sample bag at the end and the smell through the parking lot.
buzz: It is 15 minutes of windows and worth it with children; the shop sells flavors that never leave New England.

name: MASS MoCA
unique: A 19th century textile mill turned into the largest contemporary art museum in the country, with whole buildings given to single artists and a football field of light installations.
buzz: The Sol LeWitt wall drawings and the James Turrell rooms are the pilgrimage; some galleries are the size of a warehouse and the map matters.

name: Clark Art Institute
unique: A small jewel of a museum with 30 Renoirs, a Winslow Homer room and a reflecting pool by Tadao Ando set in 140 acres of meadow and trail.
buzz: People call it the perfect size for two hours; the Ando pools and the walk up Stone Hill are as memorable as the galleries.

name: Hancock Shaker Village
unique: A round stone barn and 20 Shaker buildings where a utopian community lived and worked, with gardens, a working farm and demonstrations of the furniture that shaped modern design.
buzz: The round barn is the architectural highlight and the craft demos are the reason to check the daily schedule; the village is bigger than it looks.

name: Eric Carle Museum of Picture Book Art
unique: The only museum in the country devoted to picture book art, founded by the author of The Very Hungry Caterpillar, with a gallery of original illustrations and a studio where children paint.
buzz: Adults without children love it as much as the children do; the studio and the reading library make it a two hour stop.

name: Smith College Museum of Art
unique: A college museum with a Degas, a Mondrian and a room of African textiles, free to the public and small enough to see before lunch.
buzz: Locals treat it as a free hour; the contemporary galleries rotate often and the print room is open by appointment.

name: Historic Deerfield
customer: History people, decorative arts fans, families
unique: A mile long street of 18th century houses from the 1704 raid, furnished with the chairs and textiles of the Connecticut valley, with a working farm and a tavern.
buzz: The guided house tours are the only way in and the decorative arts collection is serious; the street itself is free to walk.

name: Bridge of Flowers
unique: A 1908 trolley bridge planted end to end with flowers after the trolley stopped running, crossing the Deerfield River above glacial potholes.
buzz: The potholes below are as good as the bridge and both are free; peak bloom is July and the village has a glassblowing studio.

name: Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame
company: Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame
unique: Three floors of basketball history where you can shoot on a court, compare your hand to Shaq's and see the peach basket that started the game in Springfield in 1891.
buzz: The interactive court is what children remember and the enshrinement gallery is for fans; allow two hours and go on a weekday.

name: Springfield Armory National Historic Site
customer: Engineering people, military history fans, families
unique: The armory that made the rifles for every American war from 1794 to 1968, with a room of 1,000 muskets arranged like a pipe organ and the machine tools that invented interchangeable parts.
buzz: The gun collection is the show and the manufacturing story is the real history; rangers explain the machinery and the museum is free.

name: Dr. Seuss National Memorial Sculpture Garden
unique: Bronze Lorax, Horton and Cat in the Hat statues in a courtyard in Theodor Geisel's hometown, with a seated Geisel at his drawing board.
buzz: A free 20 minute stop that photographs well; the museum next door has the original drawings and is the paid companion.

name: Old Sturbridge Village
unique: Two hundred acres of a New England town rebuilt around a common, with a working farm, a tin shop, a printing office and interpreters who stay in character.
buzz: Allow four hours and check the daily schedule for the blacksmith and the farm; children like the animals and the stagecoach.

name: Worcester Art Museum
unique: A small encyclopedic museum with a Roman mosaic floor, the Higgins armor collection and an early Monet, in a 1898 building that is easy to see in two hours.
buzz: The armor and the mosaic are the surprises; locals go on the free first Sunday and the café is good.

name: Purgatory Chasm
unique: A quarter mile granite chasm with walls 70 feet high that you scramble through on boulders, formed by glacial meltwater and a popular local rite of passage.
buzz: The chasm floor is a boulder hop and not for sandals; the rim trail is the easy version and the park is free.

name: Aquinnah Cliffs
unique: Colored clay cliffs on the western tip of Martha's Vineyard, tribal land above a beach of red and white sand, with a lighthouse and a view to the Elizabeth Islands.
buzz: The cliffs are protected and you cannot climb them; the beach walk at low tide is the way and the sunset from the overlook is the photo.

name: Menemsha
customer: Harbor people, sunset chasers, seafood eaters
unique: A working fishing harbor on Martha's Vineyard where the catch is sold off the boat, the beach faces west and the sunset is a nightly event with people applauding.
buzz: Buy chowder and lobster from the shack and eat on the bulkhead; parking in the village is tight and the beach lot closes at sunset time.

name: New Bedford Whaling Museum
unique: The world's largest whaling museum, with half scale whale skeletons hanging over a full scale whaling ship, a scrimshaw collection and the logbooks of the voyages that made the city rich.
buzz: The skeleton room is the one people describe; the museum does not soften the industry and the harbor walk outside completes it.

name: Battleship Cove
unique: The most decorated American battleship of the Second World War, the USS Massachusetts, plus a destroyer and a submarine you can walk through, all tied up together.
buzz: Children can sleep on board with scout groups; the submarine is tight and the battleship guns are the photo.

name: Lizzie Borden House
customer: True crime people, history fans, ghost hunters
unique: The 1892 house where the Borden murders happened, now a bed and breakfast, with a tour that walks the rooms and lays out the evidence.
buzz: Guides present the case without pretending to solve it; overnight guests report things and the tour is more history than haunt.

name: Nantucket Whaling Museum
unique: A candle factory turned museum with a 46 foot sperm whale skeleton on the roof, a restored 1840s whaleship hold and the story of the island that lit America.
buzz: The roof walk with the skeleton and harbor view is the highlight; the museum is the best rainy day on the island.

name: Cisco Brewers
unique: A brewery, winery and distillery in a gray shingled barn outside town, with picnic tables, oyster shucking and live music on summer afternoons.
buzz: The outdoor scene is the point and the island prices are real; go early, the tasting room fills after three.

name: Newark Museum of Art
unique: A encyclopedic museum with one of the best Tibetan collections in the west, a Victorian ballroom and a planetarium, in a city most visitors skip.
buzz: The Tibetan galleries are the reason curators come; the Ballantine House next door is a separate tour and the planetarium is cheap.

name: Thomas Edison National Historical Park
unique: Edison's three story laboratory complex with 400,000 artifacts, a machine shop that could build anything and a recording studio where the first sound was captured.
buzz: The chemistry lab and the machine shop are the best preserved; the ranger tour of the main building is worth timing your visit for.

name: Liberty State Park
unique: The old Central Railroad terminal on the harbor with the Empty Sky memorial, a 30 acre lawn and the ferry dock for the Statue of Liberty.
buzz: The memorial and the skyline view are the draw; the ferry leaves from here and parking is far cheaper than Manhattan.

name: Loew's Jersey Theatre
customer: Movie palace fans, architecture people, film lovers
unique: A 3,200 seat 1929 movie palace with a ceiling of gilded stars and clouds, saved by volunteers and still showing classic films on 35mm.
buzz: The restoration is the story and volunteers run tours; film fans say the balcony seats are the best in the state.

name: Fort Lee Historic Park
unique: The bluff where Washington's army built a fort to block the Hudson, with reconstructed huts and a cliff edge view of the George Washington Bridge.
buzz: The view is the reason to stop and the history is the bonus; the cliff trail below is a separate walk with real exposure.

name: Tenafly Nature Center
unique: Four hundred acres of deciduous forest and a lake with a resident barred owl and a trail system that feels remote for being 15 minutes from the George Washington Bridge.
buzz: The owl and the pond are the easy wins with children; trails are flat and the center runs weekend programs.

name: Paterson Great Falls
unique: A 77 foot waterfall in the middle of a city where Alexander Hamilton planned the first industrial city, with raceways, mills and a hydroelectric plant still running.
buzz: The falls from the bridge are the photo and the ranger walk explains the engineering; the surrounding blocks are rough and the park is well patrolled.

name: Ringwood Manor
customer: House tour people, history fans, gardeners
unique: A 51 room ironmaster's mansion in the Ramapo hills with period rooms, a walled garden and the forges and mines that armed the Revolution nearby.
buzz: The house tour is the only way in and the guides know the families; the state park trails behind it are free and quiet.

name: Morristown National Historical Park
customer: History families, hikers, rev war people
unique: The winter encampment where the Continental Army survived 1779, with Washington's Ford Mansion, reconstructed log huts and 27 miles of trails through Jockey Hollow.
buzz: The huts and the Wick House are the walk and the mansion tour is separate; the park is the first national historical park in the country.

name: Historic Speedwell
unique: The ironworks village where Samuel Morse demonstrated the telegraph in 1838, with the original factory building, a wheelwright shop and a working letterpress.
buzz: The telegraph story is the hook and the volunteers demonstrate it; the site is small and best combined with Jockey Hollow.

name: Duke Farms
unique: A 2,700 acre estate with nine lakes, a 1909 conservatory, a hay barn cafe and miles of paved paths where bicycles are free to borrow.
buzz: The free bike borrow and the orchid range are the local secret; it is the former Doris Duke estate and the trails are flat.

name: Leonard J. Buck Garden
unique: A rock garden built into a wooded ravine with a stream, ponds and paths that switchback through alpine plants, hidden behind a suburban office park.
buzz: Gardeners call it the best small garden in the state; spring is the peak and the paths are steep and narrow.

name: Watchung Reservation
unique: Two thousand acres of forest with a lake, a nature center and the Deserted Village of Feltville, an 1840s mill town abandoned and still standing in the woods.
buzz: The deserted village is the strange draw and the lake trail is the easy walk; the nature center has live animals for children.

name: Miller-Cory House
unique: A 1740 farmhouse where volunteers cook over the open hearth and work the garden with 18th century tools on Sunday afternoons.
buzz: The open hearth cooking is the reason to time a visit; it is run by volunteers and small enough to feel like a neighbor's house.

name: Thomas Edison Center at Menlo Park
company: Thomas Alva Edison Memorial Tower Corporation
customer: Science people, families, local history fans
unique: A 131 foot Art Deco tower of Edison's light bulb on the site of his Menlo Park lab, with a small museum of phonographs and early bulbs.
buzz: The tower is visible from the highway and the museum is one room; locals bring visiting engineers and the ranger talk is good.

name: Delaware and Raritan Canal State Park
unique: Seventy miles of towpath along an 1830s canal, flat and gravel, with a mule drawn boat at Griggstown and herons the whole way.
buzz: The Princeton to Kingston stretch is the standard ride; the path is flat and shaded and the canal is stocked with fish.

name: Red Mill Museum Village
unique: A red painted gristmill on the South Branch with a limestone quarry, a one room schoolhouse and a mule drawn canal boat, all in a village of 2,700 people.
buzz: The mill and the quarry are the tour and the bridge over the river is the photograph; check hours before driving, it is seasonal.

name: Delaware River Tubing
unique: A three mile float down the Delaware between wooded New Jersey and Pennsylvania banks, with small rapids, rope swings and a bus back to the start.
buzz: Bring water shoes and a dry bag; the river is shallow in August and the weekend crowds are loud by noon.

name: WheatonArts
unique: The Museum of American Glass with 7,000 pieces, a working glass studio where you can watch a gather and blow, and a folk art center on a wooded campus.
buzz: Glassblowing demos run all day and the paperweight collection is the surprise; in April the glass festival fills the grounds.

name: East Point Lighthouse
unique: A brick 1849 lighthouse at the mouth of the Maurice River, surrounded by marsh and one of the best shorebird staging areas on the Delaware Bay.
buzz: In May the horseshoe crabs and red knots draw birders from other countries; the lighthouse opens on select weekends and the road is gravel.

name: Red Bank Battlefield
unique: The bluff above the Delaware where a 1777 fort held off a Hessian attack, with earthworks, the Whitall House and a view across to Philadelphia International.
buzz: The archaeology dig that found soldiers' remains made news; the park is free and the river path is a good evening walk.

name: William Heritage Winery
unique: A family fruit farm that turned to wine, with a tasting room over the vineyard and peach and apple orchards that pick in summer.
buzz: The dry riesling and the cider are the orders; the deck is the reason to come on a fall afternoon.

name: Cowtown Rodeo
unique: The oldest weekly professional rodeo in the country, running Saturday nights in a South Jersey field with bull riding, barrel racing and a calf scramble for children.
buzz: Locals bring blankets to the bleachers and first timers are surprised by how fast the night goes; the funnel cake stand is the tradition.

name: Fort Mott State Park
unique: An 1890s harbor defense fort on the Delaware with concrete batteries you can walk through, a ferry to a island fort and a river beach.
buzz: The batteries are open and dark and children love them; the ferry to Pea Patch Island and Fort Delaware runs in summer.

name: Battleship New Jersey
unique: The most decorated battleship in American history, with a 16 inch gun turret you can climb inside, a guided engine room tour and the captain's cabin.
buzz: The turret climb is the thing people remember; the engine room tour costs extra and is worth it, and the deck view of Philadelphia is free.

name: Adventure Aquarium
unique: A shark tunnel you walk under, a hippo exhibit with underwater viewing and a touch tank of stingrays, on the Camden waterfront across from Philadelphia.
buzz: The hippos and the shark tunnel are the hits; tickets are cheaper online and the garage is the easiest parking.

name: Cape May Lighthouse
unique: A 1859 brick tower with 199 steps and a view over the Cape May point where two bays meet, inside a state park that is a major migration stop.
buzz: The climb is worth the view and the fall hawk watch at the park is a separate draw; the beach below is free.

name: Twin Lights
unique: Twin granite towers on the Navesink Highlands with a museum in one and a view of the Atlantic and New York Harbor from the other.
buzz: The view from the north tower is the best on the Jersey shore; the museum covers the Marconi wireless station that once stood here.

name: Island Beach State Park
unique: Ten miles of undeveloped barrier beach with dunes, a maritime forest and no boardwalk, between the ocean and Barnegat Bay.
buzz: The park closes when the lot fills, usually by nine in summer; the bay side is calm for children and the trails are empty in September.

name: Batsto Village
unique: A bog iron and glassmaking village in the Pine Barrens with a mansion, a sawmill, a gristmill and worker cottages, abandoned when the iron ran out.
buzz: The village is free to walk and the mansion tour is cheap; the pond and the pine woods make it a good half day.

name: Wadsworth Atheneum
unique: The oldest public art museum in the country, with a castle facade, a Hudson River School collection, the first Picasso bought by an American museum and a baroque cabinet of curiosities.
buzz: The Morgan and the Hudson River rooms are the local favorites; the museum is quiet on weekday mornings and the café is in the old sculpture court.

name: Harriet Beecher Stowe Center
unique: The Victorian cottage where Stowe wrote after Uncle Tom's Cabin, kept with her desk, her paintings and a tour that connects the book to the present rather than treating it as a relic.
buzz: The guides are trained to run a conversation, not a lecture, and visitors say it is the most useful history tour in the city; Mark Twain's house is next door.

name: Elizabeth Park Rose Garden
unique: The oldest municipal rose garden in the country, with 15,000 bushes in a formal arbor and a pond, free and open at dawn.
buzz: Peak bloom is the third week of June and locals come before work; the park is safe and the greenhouses are open in winter.

name: Bushnell Park Carousel
unique: A 1914 Stein and Goldstein carousel with 48 hand carved horses and a Wurlitzer organ, still turning in a glass pavilion in the middle of downtown.
buzz: A two dollar ride that adults take without children; the park around it is the oldest public park in the country.

name: Yale University Art Gallery
unique: The oldest college art museum in the western hemisphere, with a Van Gogh, a Trumbull revolution cycle and a room of African art, all free.
buzz: The Trumbull paintings and the modern galleries are the route; it is free and rarely crowded on weekday afternoons.

name: Yale Center for British Art
unique: Louis Kahn's last building, a four story box of oak, linen and concrete holding the largest collection of British art outside Britain, including Constable and Turner.
buzz: The building is as good as the paintings and the long gallery on the top floor is the place to sit; admission is free.

name: Grove Street Cemetery
customer: History walkers, architecture fans, Yale visitors
unique: The first chartered cemetery in the country, laid out in family plots on a grid with an Egyptian revival gate, holding Eli Whitney, Noah Webster and Lyman Beecher.
buzz: The gate and the Whitney monument are the landmarks; it is a quiet walk between Yale and the Hill and free maps are at the entrance.

name: East Rock Park
unique: A traprock ridge with a carriage road to a soldiers' monument and a cliff view over New Haven harbor, plus a trail down to the Mill River.
buzz: The summit is a 20 minute walk and the view of the city and Long Island Sound is the payoff; the road is closed to cars in winter.

name: Peabody Museum
unique: A natural history museum with a brontosaurus mount that helped start the dinosaur craze, a great hall of mammals and an Egyptian collection, reopened after a major renovation.
buzz: The dinosaur hall is the reason children ask to return; admission is free and the new galleries are brighter than the old ones.

name: Weir Farm National Historical Park
unique: The farm where American impressionist J. Alden Weir painted for 40 years, with his studio, a pond and a trail where the park supplies easels and paint.
buzz: Artists can borrow supplies and paint on the grounds; the studio tour is short and the property is the only national park devoted to painting.

name: Maritime Aquarium
unique: A aquarium built in a 19th century ironworks on the Norwalk River, with a shark tank, seals and a research vessel that takes people out on Long Island Sound.
buzz: The touch tanks and the seal feeding are the hits; the harbor cruise is the add on and the building itself is a nice piece of industrial reuse.

name: Beardsley Zoo
unique: The state's only zoo, with a New England farmyard, a carousel and animals from the Americas, in a park designed by Frederick Law Olmsted's firm.
buzz: The farmyard and the tigers are the route with small children; it is small enough to finish in two hours and the parking is free.

name: Sherwood Island State Park
unique: The first state park in Connecticut, 238 acres of beach and salt marsh on Long Island Sound with a nature center and a September 11 memorial garden.
buzz: The beach is wide and the parking is the only cost; the marsh boardwalk is quiet and good for birds at low tide.

name: Mystic Aquarium
unique: A beluga whale habitat, a penguin pavilion and a touch tank of sharks, next to Mystic Seaport so a family can do both in a day.
buzz: The belugas and the sea lion show are the draw; buy the combined ticket with the seaport and arrive at opening.

name: Ocean Beach Park
unique: A half mile of beach with a 1940s boardwalk, a carousel, a bandshell and a bathhouse that still looks like a seaside postcard.
buzz: The boardwalk and the ice cream stand are the tradition; parking is the cost and the beach is calm and shallow.

name: Harkness Memorial State Park
unique: A 42 room Roman renaissance mansion on a Long Island Sound point with a formal garden, a pergola and a lawn that runs to the water.
buzz: The gardens and the mansion terrace are the photo backdrop; the house is only open on tour dates and the beach is rocky.

name: Eugene O'Neill Theater Center
unique: The campus where new American plays and musicals are workshopped before Broadway, with a barn theater, a mansion and readings that cost a fraction of a city ticket.
buzz: Audiences see shows in development and are asked for feedback; the summer season is short and the grounds are open to walk.

name: Lime Rock Park
unique: A 1.5 mile road course in the Berkshire foothills where spectators can walk the paddock, sit on the hill at the uphill and watch vintage cars race without a grandstand ticket.
buzz: The Labor Day vintage festival is the weekend to go; the track is small, the access is unmatched and the loudest cars are the point.

name: Kent Falls State Park
unique: A quarter mile of cascades dropping 250 feet over marble ledges, with a trail alongside and a covered bridge at the bottom.
buzz: The climb is short and steep and the upper pools are the quiet part; in spring the water is loud and in August it is a trickle.

name: American Mural Project
customer: Art people, families, labor history fans
unique: The largest indoor collaborative mural in the country, 120 feet long and five stories high, filling a former textile mill with painted tributes to American workers.
buzz: Visitors are unprepared for the scale; you can walk into parts of the mural and the mill building is part of the exhibit.

name: White Memorial Conservation Center
unique: Four thousand acres of woods, ponds and boardwalks around a small nature museum with live owls and a working weather station.
buzz: The boardwalk and the owls are good with children; the trails are flat and the museum is small enough for an hour.

name: Nathan Hale Homestead
unique: The Hale family farmhouse where the 21 year old schoolteacher who said he had only one life to give grew up, with period rooms and a heritage breed farm.
buzz: The house tour ties the famous last words to a real family; the grounds and the farmers market in summer are free.

name: Stafford Motor Speedway
unique: A half mile oval that runs Friday night short track racing under lights, with modifieds, late models and a grandstand where you can see the whole track.
buzz: Friday night races are cheap and loud and the modified division is the local obsession; bring a jacket, the hill is cold after dark.

name: Mansfield Drive-In
unique: A three screen drive-in in the woods where you tune the radio, sit on the tailgate and watch two features for the price of one.
buzz: The snack bar is cash only and the double features are the deal; arrive early for a good spot and bring bug spray.

name: Roseland Cottage
unique: A Gothic revival summer cottage painted bubblegum pink, with original 1850s wallpaper, a boxwood parterre garden and a bowling alley in the carriage house.
buzz: The color and the bowling alley are the surprises; the tour is short and the garden is free to walk.

name: Air Line Trail
unique: A 50 mile gravel rail trail on the old Air Line route, crossing stone arch bridges and a gorge on the Natchaug River.
buzz: The Thompson to Putnam section and the Willimantic bridge are the highlights; the surface is gravel and better on a hybrid than a road bike.

name: Thompson Speedway Motorsports Park
unique: A five eighths mile oval plus a road course on the same property, one of the oldest closed circuit tracks in New England, with open track days for street cars.
buzz: The road course track days are the way in for drivers; the oval races are cheap and the grandstand is old school.

name: Connecticut River Museum
customer: Boat people, history families, river walkers
unique: A museum in a 1878 steamboat warehouse on the river, with a working shipyard, a 1906 schooner and the story of the Connecticut's shipbuilding trade.
buzz: The schooner sails in summer and the museum is small; combine it with the Essex steam train across town.

name: Hammonasset Beach State Park
unique: Two miles of beach on Long Island Sound with a boardwalk, a campground in the pines and the Meigs Point nature center at the eastern end.
buzz: The park is huge and the west beach is the family side; the nature center has live animals and the campground books early.

name: Devil's Hopyard State Park
unique: Eighty foot Chapman Falls drops into a pothole marked gorge on the Eightmile River, with trails through hemlock and a legend about the devil that the park does not endorse.
buzz: The falls are a five minute walk and the orange trail climbs above them; it is small and popular on summer weekends.

name: RISD Museum
unique: A design school museum with a 12th century French chapel, a Mesopotamian lion, Gorham silver and a room of student work, all in a block of College Hill.
buzz: The decorative arts and the costume galleries are quietly excellent; the museum is free on Sundays and students use it as a study hall.

name: Benefit Street Mile of History
unique: A mile of original colonial and federal houses on College Hill, with the First Baptist Church in America at one end and a burial ground where Roger Williams is remembered.
buzz: The street itself is free and the best architecture walk in the state; the Athenaeum and the John Brown House are the paid stops.

name: The Breakers
customer: House tour people, architecture fans, families
unique: The Vanderbilt summer cottage of 70 rooms, with a great hall of Caen limestone, a dining room that took a year to carve and a cliff walk terrace over the Atlantic.
buzz: The audio tour is better than the guided one for the details; buy the multi house ticket if you are doing two or three.

name: Ocean Drive
unique: Ten miles of coastal road past Gilded Age cottages, rocky coves, Brenton Point and the entrance to the Cliff Walk, with the ocean on one side and stone walls on the other.
buzz: Drive it at sunset and stop at Brenton Point; cyclists do the loop in summer and the road is narrow in places.

name: Watch Hill Carousel
unique: A flying horse carousel built in 1879 hanging from chains rather than mounted on a frame, still turning beside a Rhode Island beach.
buzz: Collectors say it is one of the oldest in the country; the ride is two dollars and the beach and lighthouse are a short walk.

name: Misquamicut State Beach
unique: A wide barrier beach with real surf, a boardwalk of food stands and the Atlantic on one side and a salt pond on the other.
buzz: It is the busiest beach in the state and the surf is the draw; arrive before nine or park in the private lots across the road.

name: Blithewold Mansion
unique: A 45 room summer mansion on Narragansett Bay with a 10 acre arboretum, a giant sequoia and a bamboo grove, all on a lawn that runs to the water.
buzz: Gardeners come for the rare trees and the spring bulb show; the house tour is short and the grounds are the reason to stay.

name: Herreshoff Marine Museum
customer: Sailors, boat builders, America's Cup fans
unique: The boatyard where Captain Nat Herreshoff built six America's Cup defenders, with a model room, the catamarans of 1988 and a working waterfront.
buzz: Sailing people treat it as a shrine and non sailors are converted by the model room; the restored boats are in the water in summer.

name: Bristol Fourth of July Parade
unique: The oldest continuous Fourth of July celebration in the country, a morning parade down Hope Street past colonial houses with the nation's oldest flag still flying.
buzz: Locals claim their spot the night before; parking is impossible and the walk from the edge of town is part of the ritual.

name: Goddard Memorial State Park
unique: Nearly 500 acres on Greenwich Bay with a beach, a bridle path, a picnic grove and one of the few public polo fields in New England.
buzz: The beach is calm and shallow and the park is quiet on weekdays; the polo matches in summer are free to watch.

name: Nathanael Greene Homestead
customer: Rev war people, history families, locals
unique: The Georgian house Washington's most trusted general built and left to go to war, with period rooms and a forge site on the grounds.
buzz: The volunteers know Greene's campaigns in detail; it is small and only open seasonally, so call before driving.

name: Conimicut Point Park
unique: A sandbar point at the mouth of the Providence River with a view of the Conimicut lighthouse and the bay traffic, a favorite for sitting in the car at dusk.
buzz: Locals come for the sunset and the fishing; the tide comes in fast across the point and there is no lifeguard.

name: Church Street Marketplace
unique: Four blocks of brick street closed to cars, with a farmers market, buskers, a used bookstore and the lake at the bottom of the hill.
buzz: The summer festival and the winter lights are the two seasons; locals walk it fast and visitors should take the side streets to the lake.

name: Burlington Bike Path
unique: A paved eight mile path along Lake Champlain with beaches, a skate park, a fishing pier and a view of the Adirondacks across the water.
buzz: The north beach and the causeway are the stops; the path is flat and the lake is swimmable in July and August.

name: Vermont State House
customer: Statehouse collectors, school groups, history people
unique: A granite capitol with a gold leaf dome and a cedar statue of Ceres on top, in a town of 8,000 that is the smallest state capital in the country.
buzz: Tours are free and the Representatives Hall is the room to see; the farmers market on the lawn in summer is the local ritual.

name: Cabot Creamery
unique: A farmer owned dairy cooperative with a visitor center over the cheese plant, a tasting counter and the world's best selling cheddar made a few feet away.
buzz: The tasting is generous and the tour is short; the shop sells a 10 year cheddar you cannot get at home.

name: Mount Philo
unique: The first state park in Vermont, a 968 foot peak with a road and a trail to a summit view of Lake Champlain and the Adirondacks.
buzz: The hike is 45 minutes and the view is the best effort to reward ratio in the state; the road is narrow and the lot fills on fall weekends.

name: Rokeby Museum
customer: History people, students, abolition history fans
unique: A Quaker farm that was a stop on the Underground Railroad, with four generations of family letters, a stone barn and a trail through the fields.
