buzz: The letters are the exhibit and the guides read them aloud; it is small and the story is specific and local.

name: Bennington Battle Monument
customer: History people, families, state monument collectors
unique: A 306 foot stone obelisk, the tallest structure in Vermont, with an elevator to an observation deck over three states and the site of the 1777 battle.
buzz: The elevator is a surprise in a 19th century monument; the view from the top and the museum at the base are both quick.

name: Hildene
unique: Robert Todd Lincoln's 24 room Georgian mansion with the original 1908 Aeolian organ, formal gardens and a working goat dairy on 400 acres.
buzz: The organ plays on a schedule and the goat dairy is the family draw; the view of the Taconic and Green mountains is the postcard.

name: Hogback Mountain
unique: A roadside pull off at 2,400 feet on Route 9 with a long view into the Green Mountains and a trail along the ridge.
buzz: The first week of October is the reason to come; the pull off is small and the trail is a gentle walk along the top.

name: Marlboro Music Festival
customer: Chamber music people, students, summer visitors
unique: A summer chamber music school where established players and young musicians rehearse together in a barn and perform programs they chose the week before.
buzz: Audiences say the rehearsals are as good as the concerts and some are open; tickets are cheap for the quality and the barn is unheated.

name: Killington
unique: The biggest vertical drop in the east and the longest season, with 155 trails across six peaks and a gondola that runs in summer for leaf peepers.
buzz: Skiers argue about the crowds but agree on the terrain; midweek in March is the locals' window and the access road is a long drive from anywhere.

name: Vermont Marble Museum
unique: A museum in a working marble company town, with the world's largest marble exhibit, a quarry overlook and the tomb of a company president cut into a block of stone.
buzz: The carving demos and the quarry view are the highlights; the town itself is built of marble and the museum is a labor of local pride.

name: Trapp Family Lodge
customer: Sound of Music fans, cross country skiers, families
unique: The Austrian lodge the von Trapp family built after fleeing Europe, with a meadow, a beer hall, cross country ski trails and a weekly history talk by a family member.
buzz: The story is the draw and the trails are excellent; the visit is free if you are eating or skiing and the family talks book out.

name: Smugglers' Notch
unique: A family ski mountain in a notch where boulders pinch the road and the trails run through birch and hemlock, with a summer water park and zip line.
buzz: Parents like the ski school and the slope side lodging; the notch road is closed in winter and the drive around is long.

name: Snow Farm Vineyard
unique: A vineyard on a Lake Champlain island with a tasting room in a barn and free summer concerts on the lawn overlooking the water and the Adirondacks.
buzz: The Thursday concerts are the local summer tradition; the wine is cold climate and the view beats it.

name: Lake Champlain Islands Bike Loop
unique: A flat loop across the islands of Lake Champlain on quiet roads, with orchards, a ferry crossing and water on both sides most of the way.
buzz: The islands are flat and the traffic is light; the apple orchards in September and the ferry back to New York are the local route.

name: Great Vermont Corn Maze
unique: A 24 acre corn maze cut with a different design each year, plus a smaller maze for children and a cow train, on a working Vermont farm.
buzz: Adults get lost for two hours and children do the small maze; wear closed shoes and go early, the field is hot in September.

name: Silvio O. Conte National Wildlife Refuge
unique: The Nulhegan Basin division, 26,000 acres of boreal forest and bog in the Northeast Kingdom where moose, black bear and spruce grouse live and the Connecticut River begins.
buzz: Birders come for spruce grouse and gray jay; the driving loop is gravel and the trails are flat and buggy in June.

name: Mount Washington Auto Road
unique: A 7.6 mile road climbing 4,618 feet to the summit of the highest peak in the northeast, where the weather is measured in hurricane force and the view runs to Canada.
buzz: The drive is narrow with no guardrails and the summit is 30 degrees colder; check the summit forecast, they close the road for wind.

name: Santa's Village
unique: A 1950s Christmas theme park in the White Mountains with a reindeer herd, a train through the woods and a bakery that sells gingerbread all summer.
buzz: Parents call it the cleanest small park they have visited; children under eight are the right age and the reindeer are real.

name: Flume Gorge
unique: A boardwalk through a 90 foot granite chasm with waterfalls on both walls, discovered in 1808 and still the most visited natural site in the White Mountains.
buzz: The boardwalk is steep in places and the loop takes 90 minutes; go before nine to beat the tour buses.

name: Clark's Bears
unique: A 1928 family park with a steam train that climbs a trestle, a water blaster boat ride and trained bears performing in a ring, run by the same family for four generations.
buzz: The train and the bear show are the tradition and both feel like 1965 in a good way; teenagers may be bored and small children are not.

name: Lost River Gorge
unique: A boardwalk and boulder cave route through a gorge where the river disappears underground, with crawl spaces named after what they do to your knees.
buzz: Children love the caves and adults find the boardwalk sections slick; wear shoes that can get wet and skip the caves if you are claustrophobic.

name: Hampton Beach Boardwalk
unique: A old fashioned seaside strip of fried dough, arcades, a bandshell and a wide sand beach, with the state's biggest free summer fireworks on Wednesdays.
buzz: It is loud and crowded and that is the point; parking is the hassle and the north beach is quieter.

name: Fuller Gardens
unique: A formal rose garden and Japanese garden behind a 1900s summer estate, a mile from the ocean in a town of 4,500.
buzz: Rose people come in late June and the Japanese garden is the quiet corner; it is small and the admission is modest.

name: Castle in the Clouds
customer: House tour people, hikers, leaf peepers
unique: A 1914 Arts and Crafts mansion on a mountain above Lake Winnipesaukee, with a working farm, carriage roads and a waterfall trail on 5,000 acres.
buzz: The view from the terrace is the reason to come and the trails are the surprise; the house tour is timed and the drive up is steep.

name: MS Mount Washington
unique: A 230 foot excursion boat that circles Lake Winnipesaukee past 365 islands, with a view of the Ossipee and Belknap ranges from the top deck.
buzz: The Sunday brunch cruise is the local tradition and the top deck is worth the wind; the lake is 20 miles long and the trip covers a fraction.

name: Gunstock Mountain
unique: A ski hill with a view of Lake Winnipesaukee from every run, plus a summer adventure park with a mountain coaster and an aerial treetop course.
buzz: Families like the smaller scale and the lake view; the terrain is not steep and the lodge is old but the snowmaking is serious.

name: Conway Scenic Railroad
unique: A 1870s railroad running steam and diesel excursions through Crawford Notch, with a climb up the Frankenstein Trestle and a view of Mount Washington.
buzz: The Notch train is the scenic one and the valley train is the short one; book the dome car for fall and sit on the left going up.

name: Story Land
unique: A nursery rhyme theme park in the White Mountains with a wooden coaster, a pirate ship and a pumpkin coach, scaled for small children and shaded by real trees.
buzz: Parents say it is the right size for a first park and the lines are short before noon; teenagers will be bored by two.

name: Diana's Baths
unique: A series of ledge pools and small waterfalls on Lucy Brook where the water has cut potholes into the granite, a half mile walk from the road.
buzz: The lower falls are crowded and the upper pools are quieter; the rocks are slippery and the water is cold even in August.

name: Mount Monadnock
unique: A bare granite summit above the treeline with a 100 mile view, reached by a 1.8 mile trail that is one of the most climbed mountains in the world.
buzz: The White Dot trail is steep and exposed and the summit is windy; start early, the parking lot fills by nine on weekends.

name: Keene Pumpkin Festival
unique: A downtown festival where thousands of carved jack o'lanterns are stacked into towers and lit at once, a record setting attempt that started as a local fundraiser.
buzz: The towers at dusk are the spectacle; the event has had crowd troubles in the past and now runs with tighter security and shuttles.

name: Madame Sherri Forest
company: Society for the Protection of New Hampshire Forests
unique: The stone staircase and foundations of a costume designer's castle in the woods, with a trail to a swimming pond and an old quarry.
buzz: The staircase is the photograph everyone takes; the trail is short and the pond is a local swimming hole in summer.

name: Currier Museum of Art
unique: A small museum with a Wyeth, a Picasso and a Monet, plus tours of two Frank Lloyd Wright houses a few miles away.
buzz: The Wright house tour is the reason to book ahead; the museum itself is calm and the collection is better than a city this size suggests.

name: Milford Drive-In
unique: A two screen drive-in in the woods north of Nashua, with a playground under the screen and double features that run past midnight.
buzz: Cash only at the snack bar and the early show fills; bring a battery radio if your car stereo is not great.

name: McAuliffe-Shepard Discovery Center
unique: A planetarium and science center named for the teacher who died on Challenger and the first American in space, with a Mercury capsule and a full dome theater.
buzz: The planetarium shows are the draw and the exhibits are best for ages six to twelve; the building is next to the state technical college.

name: Canterbury Shaker Village
unique: Twenty five original Shaker buildings on a hilltop, with a meetinghouse, a laundry, gardens and demonstrations of the inventions the community patented.
buzz: The guides are excellent and the village is quiet; the Shaker furniture and the round barn are the highlights.

name: Woodman Institute Museum
unique: Four buildings on a Dover block holding a mineral collection, a taxidermy hall, a colonial garrison house and a 1675 settler's home with a bullet hole in the door.
buzz: The garrison house and the odd collections are the charm; it is volunteer run and feels like a museum from 1950.

name: Children's Museum of New Hampshire
unique: A hands on museum in a 1904 armory with a working post office, a lobster boat and a maker space where children build and test things.
buzz: Parents say the age range is two to eight and the maker space is the reason older siblings agree to come; it is quiet on weekday afternoons.

name: Saint-Gaudens National Historical Park
unique: The sculptor's home and studio with the original plaster of the Shaw memorial, a colonnade he built for his casts and a garden that looks across the Connecticut River.
buzz: Sculpture people call it a pilgrimage and the outdoor casts are the reason; the summer concert series on the lawn is the local event.

name: Mount Sunapee
unique: A ski mountain inside a state park with a view of Lake Sunapee from the summit and a beginner area that is genuinely separate from the expert runs.
buzz: Families like the layout and the lodge; the summit chair is the scenic ride in fall and the state beach is across the road.

name: Fort at No. 4
customer: History families, rev war people, school groups
unique: A reconstructed palisade fort and village on the Connecticut River where settlers held out during King George's War, with period gardens and livestock.
buzz: The reenactment weekends are the time to go; on ordinary days the fort is quiet and the guides have time to talk.

name: Museum L-A
customer: Labor history people, local families, students
unique: A museum in a former shoe shop telling the story of the mills that drew French Canadian, Greek and Somali workers to Lewiston, with the machines still threaded.
buzz: The oral histories are the exhibit and the volunteers are often former mill workers; it is small and personal.

name: Lost Valley
unique: A community ski hill with night skiing, a tiny vertical and a lodge that has not changed much since the 1960s, 30 minutes from Portland.
buzz: Locals learn here and the night sessions are cheap; experts will be bored in an hour.

name: Maine Potato Blossom Festival
unique: A week of potato themed events in the county that grows most of the country's potatoes, with a parade, a mash potato wrestling match and fields of blossoms in July.
buzz: The parade and the food stands are the tradition; it is a real county fair atmosphere with almost no tourists.

name: Acadian Village
unique: A collection of 19th century Acadian houses and barns moved to a site on the St. John River, with guides who speak the French of the upper valley.
buzz: Visitors from Louisiana and France come for the genealogy; the village is quiet and the river view is the setting.

name: Sugarloaf
unique: The largest ski area in the east by vertical, with above treeline terrain, a snowfields bowl and a drive that ends in the middle of nowhere.
buzz: Skiers come for the steeps and the lack of crowds midweek; the access road is long and the wind holds lifts.

name: Maine Huts and Trails
unique: A chain of off grid lodges connected by 80 miles of trail through the Carrabassett valley, with bunk rooms, wood heat and meals cooked by a hutmaster.
buzz: People ski hut to hut in winter and hike in summer; the huts are comfortable and the booking system fills months ahead.

name: Colby College Museum of Art
unique: A college museum with the Alex Katz collection, a Whistler room and a wing by Frederick Fisher, free and better than most city museums of its size.
buzz: Art people make the drive from Portland for the Katz and the American galleries; the museum is free and the campus is walkable.

name: Old Fort Western
customer: History families, rev war people, school groups
unique: The oldest surviving wooden fort in New England, a storehouse and garrison on the Kennebec built for the French and Indian War, with the original timbers.
buzz: The guides are in period dress and the storehouse is the best building; it is small and the river setting is the rest.

name: Coastal Maine Botanical Gardens
unique: Three hundred acres of gardens on a tidal saltwater frontage, with five huge wooden trolls hidden in the woods, a children's garden and a rhododendron trail.
buzz: The trolls are why families come and the gardens are why gardeners return; allow three hours and wear walking shoes.

name: Boothbay Railway Village
unique: A village of moved and restored buildings around a narrow gauge steam railroad, with a Model T ride and a collection of antique automobiles.
buzz: The steam train ride is short and the village is the charm; good with children under ten and quiet in September.

name: Sunday River
unique: Eight connected peaks with a lift system that spreads crowds, wide groomers and a resort base that makes a week easy without a car.
buzz: Families like the variety and the snowmaking; experts prefer Sugarloaf and the base area is a long walk from some lodging.

name: Maine Mineral and Gem Museum
unique: A world class mineral collection in a Bethel storefront, including the largest meteorite found in the state and a walk in gem vault.
buzz: Rockhounds call it a hidden gem and the fluorescent mineral room is the surprise; children like the gold panning.

name: Cole Land Transportation Museum
unique: A hangar of Maine snowplows, logging trucks, fire engines and a 1920s bus, put together by a truck dealer who bought back the state's working vehicles.
buzz: The snowplow and logging equipment are the local history; the military hall next door is separate and free.

name: Hudson Museum
unique: A university anthropology museum with a strong Wabanaki collection, birchbark canoes and baskets, free and open to the public.
buzz: The Wabanaki baskets and the Penobscot canoe are the highlights; it is small and the staff are helpful.

name: Maine Maritime Museum
unique: A shipyard museum on the Kennebec where a 19th century shipbuilding yard is preserved, with a working wooden boat shop and cruises on the river.
buzz: The boat shop and the yard are the real thing and the river cruise is the add on; children like the lobstering exhibit.

name: Popham Beach State Park
company: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands
unique: A sand spit that shifts with the tide, with a view of two islands and the remains of Fort Popham at one end, near the site of the 1607 Popham colony.
buzz: At low tide you can walk to Fox Island and the currents at the river mouth are dangerous; the beach is wide and rarely packed.

name: Moosehead Lake
unique: The largest lake in Maine, 40 miles long, ringed by unbroken forest where moose come down to the road at dusk and the steamboat Katahdin still runs.
buzz: The drive along the eastern shore at dusk is the moose route; fly fishing for brook trout and the float plane rides are the local specialties.

name: Kennebec River Rafting
customer: Groups, families with teens, adventure seekers
unique: Class IV and V whitewater on a dam controlled river, with a 12 foot drop at Magic Falls and a calmer float below for the second half.
buzz: Outfitters say the autumn release weekends are the biggest water; the river is cold and the trip runs rain or shine.

name: Cutler Coast
company: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands
unique: A bold coast of volcanic headlands and spruce forest where the trail runs along the cliff edge to coves you can only reach on foot.
buzz: The bold coast loop is the best coastal hike in the state and the fog is part of it; the trail is rough and the parking is a small lot on a dirt road.

name: Machias Wild Blueberry Festival
unique: A church run festival in the blueberry capital of the world, with a pie eating contest, a blueberry pancake breakfast and a parade through a town of 2,000.
buzz: The pies and the breakfast are the reason to come; it is small, genuine and the drive is long enough to keep it that way.

name: Marginal Way
unique: A mile and a quarter of paved footpath along the top of the sea wall between Ogunquit beach and Perkins Cove, with granite benches and rose bushes.
buzz: It is the most walkable mile on the Maine coast and busy on summer mornings; the cove at the south end has the lobster shack.

name: Nubble Lighthouse
unique: A lighthouse on a rocky island just offshore, connected to the mainland by nothing, with a keeper's house and a view of Cape Neddick.
buzz: The classic photo is from Sohier Park at sunset and the island is not open to the public; parking is limited in summer.

name: Portland Museum of Art
unique: A museum with the Winslow Homer studio collection, a Pei wing and a strong Maine painting collection, in a downtown block a few steps from the water.
buzz: The Homer galleries are the reason to come and the Wyeths are the local favorite; the free Friday evening is packed.

name: Portland Head Light
unique: Washington's first lighthouse, on a headland above the entrance to Portland harbor, with the keeper's house and a park of gun emplacements around it.
buzz: The park is free and the view of the lighthouse from the beach below is the photograph; the museum in the keeper's house is small.

name: Fort Knox
company: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands
unique: A granite fort on the Penobscot with casemates, a dry moat and a view of the Penobscot Narrows Bridge, never finished and never fired a shot in anger.
buzz: The fort is dark and open to roam and children love it; the bridge observatory next door is the add on.

name: Belfast Harbor
unique: A working waterfront with a footbridge, a farmers market, a boatyard and a rail trail along the bay, in a town that rebuilt itself around its harbor.
buzz: The coop and the harbor walk are the local ritual; the town is quieter than Camden and the sailing school takes beginners.

name: Lily Bay State Park
company: Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands
unique: A sandy beach and campground on the east shore of Moosehead Lake, with a view of Katahdin across the water and canoe rentals at the dock.
buzz: The beach is the best on the lake and the campground books early; the water is cold and the sunsets are the reason to stay.

name: Katahdin Cruises
unique: The SS Katahdin, a 1914 steamboat still running on Moosehead Lake, with a route past islands and a view of Katahdin from the water.
buzz: The boat is the attraction and the crew points out moose on the shore; the afternoon trip is the quieter one.

name: Bombay Hook National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Sixteen thousand acres of tidal salt marsh and impoundments on the Delaware Bay where hundreds of thousands of shorebirds stop in May and eagles nest within sight of the road.
buzz: The auto tour loop is the way in and the observation tower at Raymond Pool is where the photographers set up; bring bug spray in summer.

name: Air Mobility Command Museum
unique: A hangar of C-5s, C-141s and a C-47 restored as a D-Day aircraft, plus the only B-17 in Delaware, free and walk around open.
buzz: Volunteers are often retired loadmasters and will open cockpits; the C-5 is the size people cannot get over.

name: Dover Motor Speedway
unique: A mile concrete oval known as the Monster Mile, with banking that lets you see the whole field from the frontstretch and a campground that becomes a small city.
buzz: Fans say the concrete makes the racing better and the traffic easier than the big tracks; the September race is the traditional weekend.

name: Hagley Museum
unique: The du Pont gunpowder works on the Brandywine, with water powered mills you walk through, a powder yard demonstration that shakes the valley and the family mansion.
buzz: The explosion demonstration is the reason children agree to the museum; the walk along the raceway is beautiful and mostly shaded.

name: Delaware Art Museum
unique: The largest collection of Pre-Raphaelite art in the country outside Britain, in a bank building on a wooded park, with a strong Howard Pyle illustration collection.
buzz: The Pre-Raphaelites are the surprise and the American illustration galleries the local pride; it is a two hour museum and free on Sundays.

name: Bethany Beach Boardwalk
unique: A quiet half mile boardwalk with a bandstand, a totem pole and a beach that is calmer than Rehoboth's, in a town that bans alcohol on the sand.
buzz: Families choose it for the calm water and the quiet; the boardwalk is a walk, not a carnival, and parking is free but tight.

name: Delaware Seashore State Park
unique: A barrier beach between the ocean and Rehoboth Bay, with a surfing beach on the inlet side, a fishing pier and a campground under the bridge.
buzz: The inlet is where the surf is consistent and the bay side is flat for kayaks; the bridge traffic in summer is the local joke.

name: Great Falls Tavern
unique: The Potomac pouring over a quarter mile of rock ledges at the fall line, with a 1831 tavern, a canal boat, a mule drawn ride and a cliff trail above the gorge.
buzz: The Billy Goat Trail is the real hike and the section A scramble is the local test; go early, the lot fills by nine on weekends.

name: Glen Echo Park
unique: A 1891 trolley park and Chautauqua that became an arts center, with a 1921 carousel, a Spanish ballroom with swing dances and a glass studio.
buzz: The Saturday night swing dance in the ballroom is the local institution; the art studios are open to walk through and the carousel is two dollars.

name: US Naval Academy
unique: The yard where every American naval officer is trained, with a chapel crypt holding John Paul Jones, a 1906 chapel dome and a museum of ship models.
buzz: The guided tour is free and walks you past the midshipmen, who are still in formation; visitors need a government ID and the museum is separate.

name: Sandy Point State Park
unique: A bay beach under the Chesapeake Bay Bridge with calm water, a fishing pier and a view of the bridge towers from the sand.
buzz: The beach is the easy swim for children and the bridge view at sunset is the photograph; the lot fills early on summer weekends.

name: B&O Ellicott City Station
unique: The oldest railroad station in the country, built 1831 on the B&O's first line, with a turntable, a freight house and a model of the Patapsco valley line.
buzz: The building and the turntable are the reason to come; the town around it floods in heavy rain and the hill is steep.

name: Merriweather Post Pavilion
unique: A pavilion in the woods of Symphony Woods where the lawn slopes into the trees and the summer lineup runs from the symphony to indie rock.
buzz: The lawn is the reason people go and the sound is better than most amphitheaters; parking is a walk and the shows run late.

name: Catoctin Mountain Park
unique: A wooded mountain park built around a CCC camp, with trails to a waterfall and a vista, and Camp David hidden in the next hollow.
buzz: The Cunningham Falls and the Blue Blazes trail are the walks; the park is quiet on weekdays and the presidential retreat is off limits.

name: National Museum of Civil War Medicine
company: National Museum of Civil War Medicine
unique: The story of battlefield medicine in a downtown Frederick building, from amputation tables to the letterman stretcher and the sanitary commission, with a second site at Antietam.
buzz: Nurses and doctors find it fascinating and children find it grim; the guides do not sanitize the surgery.

name: Elk Neck State Park
unique: A peninsula between the Elk and Susquehanna rivers with a bay beach, bluffs, a lighthouse and a campground in the woods.
buzz: The Turkey Point lighthouse trail is the walk and the beach is calm for children; the park is a halfway stop between Baltimore and Philadelphia.

name: Chesapeake City
unique: A canal town split by the Chesapeake and Delaware Canal, with a high bridge over the cut, a waterfront of 19th century houses and ships passing at eye level.
buzz: People stop to watch the ships from the bridge and stay for lunch; the town is small, the canal museum is free and the walk is flat.

name: Chesapeake Bay Maritime Museum
unique: A waterfront campus of skipjacks, a lighthouse moved from the bay, a working boatyard and the Hooper Strait screw pile light, with crabbing demonstrations.
buzz: The lighthouse and the skipjack are the highlights and the boatyard is where the work happens; children like the tonging and crab picking.

name: Oxford Bellevue Ferry
unique: The oldest privately operated ferry in the country, a small boat that carries cars and bicycles across the Tred Avon between two colonial towns.
buzz: The crossing is ten minutes and the point is the ride; cyclists use it to loop the Talbot county back roads.

name: Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Thirty thousand acres of marsh and open water where the largest breeding population of bald eagles on the east coast nests and thousands of Canada geese winter.
buzz: The wildlife drive at dawn is the experience and the eagle nest is visible from the road; bring bug spray and a scope.

name: Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad Visitor Center
company: National Park Service and Maryland State Parks
customer: History people, students, civil rights pilgrims
unique: A visitor center in the marsh landscape Tubman grew up in, telling her story through the places she worked and fled, with a driving tour to the sites.
buzz: The building and the landscape carry the story and rangers lead walks; the driving tour takes a half day and the roads are flat and empty.

name: Calvert Cliffs State Park
unique: A mile and a half walk through woods to a beach below 30 million year old cliffs where shark teeth and shells wash out of the sand.
buzz: Children find teeth within minutes and the walk back is uphill; collecting is allowed from the beach but not the cliffs.

name: Calvert Marine Museum
unique: A museum with river otters, a fossil hall of Miocene whales and a lighthouse, plus a boatyard where a skipjack is restored.
buzz: The otters are the family draw and the fossil hall is serious; the drum point lighthouse is the photograph.

name: Western Maryland Scenic Railroad
unique: A steam locomotive climb from Cumberland to Frostburg over the Allegheny divide, through a horseshoe curve and the 914 foot Brush Tunnel.
buzz: The dome car and the open air car are the seats to book; the Frostburg stop is 90 minutes and the return is the same route.

name: C&O Canal Cumberland
unique: Mile zero of the 184 mile canal towpath, where the canal climbs from Cumberland into the Potomac valley through a lock house and a stone aqueduct.
buzz: Cyclists ride the whole towpath in two days; the first ten miles from Cumberland are flat and shaded and the Paw Paw tunnel is the highlight.

name: Deep Creek Lake State Park
unique: A 3,900 acre lake in the Allegheny mountains with a swimming beach, boat rentals and a ski area at one end, ringed by state forest.
buzz: Summer is the lake and winter is Wisp ski area; the state park beach is the cheap way in and the rental houses fill a year ahead.

name: Swallow Falls State Park
unique: A gorge walk past Muddy Creek Falls, the tallest in the state, under hemlocks that are among the oldest east of the Mississippi.
buzz: The loop is a mile and the falls are the reward; the hemlock canopy keeps it cool in summer and icy in winter.

name: Historic St. Mary's City
unique: The site of Maryland's first capital, with a reconstructed 17th century inn, a tobacco plantation and an ongoing dig that has found the original statehouse.
buzz: The archaeology is the story and the guides are often students; the living history and the ship reconstruction make it a full half day.

name: Point Lookout State Park
unique: A point where the Potomac meets the Chesapeake, with a Civil War prison camp cemetery, a lighthouse and a beach on the bay.
buzz: The prison history is grim and the markers are quiet; the fishing pier and campground are why locals come back.

name: Smith Island
unique: A marshy island of watermen's villages reachable only by boat, where the layer cake is a local invention and golf carts are the main transport.
buzz: The cake is the reason many come and the island is quiet and flat; the ferry takes 45 minutes and the last boat back is early.

name: National Gallery of Art
unique: A free national collection with the only Leonardo in the Americas, a Calder mobile in the rotunda and an East Building by I.M. Pei that is as good as anything hanging in it.
buzz: The West Building for old masters and the East for modern; the sculpture garden in summer and the moving walkway between buildings are the local route.

name: National Museum of African American History and Culture
unique: A bronze and glass corona on the Mall that takes you from the slave trade in the basement to music and sports on the top floors, with Emmett Till's casket and a slave ship timber.
buzz: The history galleries below ground are the reason to reserve a pass; people say three hours is not enough and the top floors are the relief after the descent.

name: National Museum of American History
unique: The flag that inspired the anthem, Julia Child's kitchen, the Greensboro lunch counter and Dorothy's ruby slippers in one free building on the Mall.
buzz: The Star Spangled Banner room is the quiet moment and the transportation hall is for children; the building is easier to enter than the newer museums.

name: Ford's Theatre
unique: The working theater where Lincoln was shot, with the presidential box preserved and a museum in the basement, still staging plays at night.
buzz: The ranger talk in the box is worth waiting for and the Petersen House across the street is included; timed tickets go fast in spring.

name: Lincoln Memorial at Dawn
unique: The marble chamber above the reflecting pool, where the Gettysburg Address is carved on one wall and the view back to the Capitol lines up with the sunrise.
buzz: Go before seven and you will have the steps almost alone; the chamber under the memorial and the view from the back are the parts people miss.

name: Eastern Market
unique: A brick market house from 1873 where butchers and a blueberry buckwheat stand still work the hall, with a weekend flea market and a crab cake counter outside.
buzz: The market hall is best on Saturday morning and the flea is behind it; the blueberry pancakes at Market Lunch are the standing order.

name: Maine Avenue Fish Market
unique: The oldest continuously operating open air fish market in the country, a row of barges on the Washington Channel selling crabs, oysters and fried fish to order.
buzz: The crabs are sold by the dozen and the fried shrimp box is the cheap lunch; it is outdoors, cash friendly and best at lunchtime.

name: US National Arboretum
unique: Four hundred and forty six acres inside the city with the National Bonsai and Penjing Museum, a grove of state trees and the columns of the old Capitol standing in a meadow.
buzz: The bonsai museum is the surprise and free; the Capitol columns are the photograph and the azalea collection peaks in late April.

name: Rock Creek Park
unique: Eighteen hundred acres of wooded valley through the middle of the city, with a creek, a mill, a planetarium and a trail network that connects to the Potomac.
buzz: Locals run the trail on weekday mornings and the Peirce Mill grinding days are the family draw; the parkway closes to cars on weekends in summer.

name: Theodore Roosevelt Island
unique: A wooded island in the Potomac reached by a footbridge, with a memorial plaza to Roosevelt in a clearing and trails through swamp and upland forest.
buzz: The island feels nothing like the city and the memorial is usually empty; the boardwalk on the north end is the birding spot.

name: Kenilworth Aquatic Gardens
unique: The only national park devoted to aquatic plants, with ponds of lotus and water lilies on the Anacostia and a boardwalk through a tidal marsh.
buzz: The lotus bloom in July is the event and photographers arrive at dawn; the park is in a quiet part of the city and feels overlooked.

name: 9:30 Club
unique: A 1,200 capacity club that has broken more bands than any room its size in the country, with a balcony that puts you almost on the stage.
buzz: The sound is consistently good and the sightlines from the balcony are the secret; shows sell out and doors are early.

name: Georgetown C&O Canal
unique: A cobblestone towpath along the canal from Georgetown to Great Falls, with lock houses, a mule drawn boat and herons in the middle of the city.
buzz: The first three miles from Georgetown are flat and shaded and the mule boat runs Wednesday to Sunday; the path is gravel and busy on weekends.

name: The Cloisters
customer: Medieval art people, gardeners, architecture fans
unique: A museum assembled from European monasteries and cloisters on a cliff in Fort Tryon Park, with the Unicorn Tapestries and a garden of medieval plants.
buzz: The building and the view of the Hudson are half the experience; the unicorn room is the reason art people make the trip uptown.

name: Morgan Library and Museum
unique: J.P. Morgan's private library, with a Gutenberg Bible, the original manuscript of A Christmas Carol and a McKim building that feels like a Renaissance study.
buzz: The East Room and the study are the rooms people remember; the rotating exhibitions pull manuscripts that rarely travel.

name: The Strand Bookstore
unique: Eighteen miles of books in a 1930s building at Broadway and 12th, with a rare book room on the third floor and dollar carts on the sidewalk.
buzz: Book people call the rare room a museum and the crowds are part of the experience; go on a weekday morning.

name: Grand Central Terminal
unique: A Beaux Arts cathedral of transit with a painted zodiac ceiling, a whispering gallery and a hidden platform once used for presidents.
buzz: The Oyster Bar and the whispering arch are the easy stops; the official tour gets you into the Vanderbilt room and the catwalks.

name: McSorley's Old Ale House
unique: The oldest continuously operating tavern in the city, with sawdust on the floor, two beers on offer and a room that has not changed since the last century.
buzz: Order the ale and skip the menu; it is crowded and cash only and the history is the point.

name: Russ and Daughters
unique: A Lower East Side appetizing shop that has smoked its own salmon since 1914, with a counter of herring and a bagel sandwich that is the neighborhood's standard.
buzz: The line moves and the ordering system confuses first timers; get a number, order the super heebster and eat it on the street.

name: Houston Museum of Natural Science
unique: A paleontology hall with 60 mounted skeletons, a butterfly rainforest, a gem vault and a planetarium, all in a building on the edge of Hermann Park.
buzz: The paleo hall and the Cockrell butterfly center are the two stops everyone makes; the museum is enormous and the add on exhibits cost extra.

name: Buffalo Bayou Park
unique: A 160 acre linear park along the bayou with a cistern you can tour, a kayak launch, a dog park and a skyline view from the water.
buzz: The Buffalo Bayou Park Cistern tours sell out and the bat bridge at dusk is the local spectacle; the trails are flat and shaded in parts.

name: Project Row Houses
unique: A block of restored shotgun houses in the Third Ward turned into artist installations and community programs, one of the earliest and most copied social practice projects in the country.
buzz: Visitors say the art is only part of it and the neighborhood context is the point; check which houses are open before going.

name: Rothko Chapel
unique: An octagonal chapel holding 14 Rothko canvases painted for the space, with a Broken Obelisk by Barnett Newman in the reflecting pool outside.
buzz: People describe the light changing through the day and the room as intentionally dim; it is free and asks for silence.

name: Perot Museum of Nature and Science
unique: A cube of concrete and glass with a glass escalator that climbs five floors past a T. rex skeleton, a earthquake simulator and an engineering hall.
buzz: The paleontology hall and the sports science exhibit are the hits; the museum is best for ages five to fourteen and gets crowded on school holidays.

name: Dallas Arboretum
unique: Sixty six acres on the shore of White Rock Lake, with a trial garden of 3,000 plants, a prairie and a children's adventure garden.
buzz: The spring tulips and the fall pumpkin village are the two seasons; the view across the lake to the Dallas skyline is the photograph.

name: Texas Theatre
unique: The 1931 movie palace where Lee Harvey Oswald was arrested, now a repertory cinema with a bar and a programming mix of cult films and new releases.
buzz: The balcony and the art deco lobby are the atmosphere; the November 22 programming is the local history lesson.

name: Kimbell Art Museum
unique: Louis Kahn's vaulted concrete galleries holding a small but flawless collection, with a Michelangelo, a Caravaggio and a Piano pavilion next door.
buzz: Architects come for the light in the vaults and art people for the quality; it is small enough for two hours and rarely crowded.

name: Modern Art Museum of Fort Worth
company: Modern Art Museum of Fort Worth
unique: Five glass pavilions floating on a reflecting pool by Tadao Ando, holding a collection from Warhol to Richter and a film program in the auditorium.
buzz: The building and the reflection pool are as good as the art; the café overlooks the water and is a destination on its own.

name: Billy Bob's Texas
unique: A honky tonk the size of a airplane hangar in the Stockyards, with a bull riding arena, 30 bars and a stage that has hosted everyone from Willie Nelson to the Rolling Stones.
buzz: The bull riding before the show is the warm up and the dance floor is enormous; it is a tourist version of a honky tonk and still fun.

name: San Antonio Missions
unique: Four Spanish colonial missions along the San Antonio River, with a working acequia, stone churches and the country's only UNESCO site that is also a living parish.
buzz: Mission San Jose is the largest and the aqueduct walk behind it is the surprise; the bike trail connects all four and the Alamo is the fifth.

name: Mi Tierra Cafe y Panaderia
unique: A Market Square institution open around the clock since 1941, with a bakery counter, a mariachi trio and a ceiling of painted panels and Christmas lights.
buzz: The pan dulce and the breakfast plates are the orders; it is loud, brightly lit and the wait at midnight is part of the experience.

name: San Antonio Museum of Art
unique: A 1884 brewery turned museum holding Latin American art, Greek vases and Asian ceramics, with a river walk extension along the back.
buzz: The Latin American collection is the reason curators visit; the building's brew house bones are visible and the river terrace is free.

name: Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center
unique: The national wildflower research center with a demonstration meadow, a limestone garden and a tower that looks over the Hill Country.
buzz: The spring bluebonnets are the peak and the center is quiet the rest of the year; the children's garden and the trails are the family route.

name: Continental Club
unique: A small South Congress club with a neon sign and a stage that has held Stevie Ray Vaughan, the Resentments and most of Austin's working musicians.
buzz: Locals say the early show is the real one and the late show is for the tourists; the room is small and the sound is loud.

name: McKinney Falls State Park
unique: Two waterfalls on Onion Creek inside the Austin city limits, with limestone ledges to swim from and trails through juniper and oak.
buzz: The upper falls are the swim and the lower falls are the photograph; the park is small and the lot fills by ten on summer weekends.

name: Hueco Tanks State Park
unique: A granite maze of boulders and tinajas with hundreds of prehistoric pictographs, and some of the best bouldering in the country.
buzz: The rock art tours are ranger led and limited and the climbing is world class; the park caps visitors and the desert heat is serious.

name: Franklin Mountains State Park
unique: The largest urban park in the country, 37 square miles of desert mountain inside El Paso, with a road to a 5,700 foot overlook of two countries and three states.
buzz: The McKelligon Canyon road and the ridge trail are the easy wins; the park is dry and exposed and the border view is the reason to drive up.

name: El Paso Mission Trail
unique: Three Spanish missions along the Rio Grande, including Ysleta, the oldest parish in Texas, with adobe walls, painted ceilings and a cemetery of wooden crosses.
buzz: The missions are active parishes and visitors are welcome at services; the drive between them follows the river and the border fence.

name: Santa Ana National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Two thousand acres of subtropical thorn forest on the Rio Grande where green jays, chachalacas and a dozen species found nowhere else in the country live.
buzz: Birders come from around the world in winter and the hawk tower is the lookout; the tram is seasonal and the trails are flat and hot.

name: Estero Llano Grande State Park
unique: A wetland and thorn scrub park on the flyway with a boardwalk, a feeding station and a recorded 350 species, including the rare hook billed kite in summer.
buzz: The feeding station is where the photographers sit and the rangers keep a daily list; it is the easiest birding in the valley for beginners.

name: Quinta Mazatlan
unique: A 1930s adobe mansion and its thorn forest garden, now an urban birding center with a canopy walk and a courtyard café.
buzz: The house and the birds are the combination; it is small and the staff point out what is at the feeders that morning.

name: USS Lexington
unique: A World War II carrier on the bay with a hangar deck of aircraft, a flight simulator and a maze of passages you can climb through.
buzz: The engine room and the bridge are the tours people remember; the ship is hot in summer and the passages are narrow.

name: Padre Island National Seashore
unique: Sixty miles of undeveloped barrier island with four wheel drive access, sea turtle releases in summer and the wreck of a Spanish ship in the dunes.
buzz: The drive down the beach is the adventure and the further you go the emptier it gets; check tide tables and do not take a car that cannot handle sand.

name: Texas State Aquarium
unique: A Gulf of Mexico aquarium with a dolphin bay, a shark exhibit and a splash park, on the ship channel next to the Lexington.
buzz: The dolphins and the touch tanks are the family draw; the splash park is the summer reason to stay and the combo ticket with the ship saves money.

name: The Strand
unique: A street of cast iron fronted Victorian buildings from the cotton boom, with a tall ship, an oil rig museum and a working harbor at one end.
buzz: The architecture is the reason to walk and the Mardi Gras and Dickens events fill it; the shops are mixed and the pier is the family stop.

name: Moody Gardens
customer: Families, tour groups, rainy day crowds
unique: Three glass pyramids on the bay holding a rainforest, an aquarium and a discovery museum, with a paddlewheel boat and a ropes course outside.
buzz: The penguins and the rainforest are the hits; the ticket pricing is confusing and the combo pass is the way to do it.

name: Galveston Island State Park
unique: Two thousand acres of beach and salt marsh on the west end of the island, with a kayak trail through the bay side and a beach that is never crowded.
buzz: The bay side is calm and good for beginners and the beach side has real surf; the park is quiet compared with the seawall.

name: Buddy Holly Center
unique: The glasses, the Fender Stratocaster and the tour van of the Lubbock kid who wrote the songs the Beatles covered, in a depot building downtown.
buzz: Music people say it is small but the artifacts are real; the West Texas Walk of Fame and the statue are across the street.

name: National Ranching Heritage Center
customer: History families, ranch people, school groups
unique: A 19 acre outdoor museum of 50 relocated ranch buildings from a 1780s Spanish compound to a 1930s bunkhouse, with longhorn cattle and a windmill collection.
buzz: The buildings are original and the scale is the surprise; it is free and the signage explains how each structure worked.

name: Prairie Dog Town
unique: A colony of prairie dogs in a city park with a viewing wall and a tunnel, started when a road crew spared the animals in the 1930s.
buzz: Children love it and the story is local legend; a 20 minute stop with a bag of unsalted peanuts.

name: Point Reyes National Seashore
unique: A fog wrapped peninsula where the San Andreas fault runs under a dairy ranch, elephant seals haul out at Chimney Rock and a 1870 lighthouse sits below the cliffs.
buzz: The lighthouse stairs are closed when the wind is up and the road to the point is long; the cypress tunnel and the elk at Tomales Point are the other stops.

name: Muir Woods
unique: Old growth coast redwoods within 30 minutes of the Golden Gate Bridge, with a boardwalk loop through trees that were standing before Columbus.
buzz: Parking requires a reservation and the main loop is crowded by ten; the Dipsea and Bootjack trails are the escape and the fog keeps it cool.

name: Angel Island
unique: An island in the bay with an immigration station known as the Ellis Island of the west, Civil War barracks and a five mile loop with views of the city and Marin.
buzz: The immigration museum is the emotional stop and the bike loop is the fun; the ferry books out and the island has no cars.

name: Mount Diablo State Park
unique: A 3,849 foot peak where you can see more of the state than from any other summit, with a stone visitor center and fire lookout from the 1930s.
buzz: Cyclists climb it as a rite of passage and the view from the summit on a clear day reaches the Sierra; the road is narrow and the heat is real in summer.

name: Rosie the Riveter WWII Home Front
unique: The shipyards where 90,000 workers built 747 ships in four years, with a museum, a preserved child care center and a waterfront walk past the dry docks.
buzz: The ranger talks and the oral histories are the reason to come; the walk along the bay to the Ford plant is the part most people miss.

name: Black Diamond Mines
unique: A coal and sand mining district in the East Bay hills with a cemetery of Welsh miners, a rose garden and a sand mine you can tour underground.
buzz: The sand mine tour is the reason to book ahead and the hike to the cemetery is short; the park is hot and exposed in summer.

name: Castello di Amorosa
unique: A 13th century style Tuscan castle built from scratch on a Napa hillside, with a torture chamber, a chapel and a barrel room painted by Italian fresco artists.
buzz: People call it Disney for adults; the wine is secondary to the tour and reservations are required on weekends.

name: Oxbow Public Market
unique: A market hall on the Napa River with a oyster bar, a spice shop, a butcher and a taco counter, where locals eat between wine appointments.
buzz: The oysters and the ice cream are the standard stops; it is smaller than the Ferry Building and easier to park.

name: Bothe-Napa Valley State Park
unique: The only state park in the Napa Valley, with redwood groves, a creek and trails up to a ridge, plus a swimming pool in summer.
buzz: It is the quiet alternative to the wineries and the campsites book early; the Ritchey Creek trail is the walk.

name: California State Railroad Museum
unique: The largest collection of restored locomotives in the country, in a 100,000 square foot building on the old Central Pacific shops, with a cab forward and a dining car you can walk through.
buzz: The roundhouse and the sleeper car are the highlights and the weekend excursion train is the add on; children can climb on several cars.

name: Sutter's Fort
customer: History families, school groups, gold rush fans
unique: The adobe fort where John Sutter ran a trading post and where the Donner Party survivors were brought, with rooms furnished as workshops and a cannon on the wall.
buzz: The living history weekends are the time to go and the fort is small; the gold discovery at Coloma is 50 miles away and the story continues there.

name: Crocker Art Museum
unique: A Victorian mansion gallery with a bowling alley in the basement, joined to a modern wing holding California art and a strong works on paper collection.
buzz: The original mansion rooms and the drawing collection are the reason to come; the newer wing hosts the big traveling shows.

name: Channel Islands National Park
unique: Five islands off the coast with endemic foxes, sea caves you can kayak into and a isolation that feels nothing like Southern California.
buzz: The ferry from Ventura takes an hour and books out; Scorpion Ranch on Santa Cruz is the easy day and the sea caves at Santa Cruz are the snorkel.

name: Santa Barbara Mission
unique: The tenth of the California missions and the only one with twin bell towers, with a cemetery, a lavanderia and a museum of Chumash and mission life.
buzz: The gardens and the facade are the photograph and the museum is frank about the mission system; the rose garden across the street is free.

name: Stearns Wharf
unique: The oldest working wooden wharf in California, with a sea center, fish and chips stands and a view back at the mountains and the red tile roofs.
buzz: The sea center touch tanks are good with children and the sunset from the end is the local ritual; parking on the pier is expensive.

name: Hearst Castle
customer: House tour people, art fans, families
unique: William Randolph Hearst's hilltop estate with a Roman pool, a private zoo's remains and a main house full of European ceilings and Spanish choir stalls.
buzz: The grand rooms tour is the standard and the upstairs tour is for repeat visitors; the bus ride up is 15 minutes and the views are half the show.

name: Morro Bay
unique: A 576 foot volcanic plug at the mouth of an estuary where sea otters raft in the channel and a dozen charter boats run fishing trips.
buzz: The otters in the harbor and the hike around the rock are the two things to do; the estuary is a bird sanctuary and kayak rentals are at the dock.

name: Oceano Dunes
unique: The only state park in California where you can drive on the beach and camp in the dunes, with five miles of sand and a riding area for ATVs.
buzz: The dune camping is the experience and the wind is relentless; check the closures for snowy plover nesting and air down your tires.

name: Buck Owens Crystal Palace
unique: Buck Owens' club and museum in Bakersfield, with his red silver sparkle guitar, a restaurant and live country music in the room that kept the Bakersfield sound alive.
buzz: The museum cases are free to browse and the shows are the draw; the food is better than a club restaurant needs to be.

name: Kern River Rafting
customer: Groups, families with teens, adventure seekers
unique: Class III and IV rapids on the river that flows out of the Sierra south of Sequoia, with a gorge section and a calmer lower run for first timers.
buzz: Outfitters say May and June are the biggest water and the lower river is the family trip; the water is cold and the canyon is hot.

name: Tule Elk State Reserve
unique: A preserve where a herd of tule elk survives on the valley floor, with a viewing platform and a fence line you can drive along.
buzz: The elk are visible most mornings and the reserve is a short detour from Interstate 5; bring binoculars and go early.

name: Forestiere Underground Gardens
unique: Ten acres of underground rooms, courtyards and fruit trees dug by one Sicilian immigrant with hand tools over 40 years to escape the valley heat.
buzz: Visitors are astonished it exists; the tour is the only way in and the temperature stays in the 70s while Fresno bakes outside.

name: Fresno County Blossom Trail
unique: A self guided drive through orchards in bloom, with farm stands selling oranges and almonds and a map that changes with what is flowering.
buzz: The bloom window is short and weather dependent; locals check the county blossom report before driving and go on a weekday.

name: Meux Home Museum
customer: House tour people, local history fans
unique: A Victorian house built by a Confederate surgeon who moved to Fresno, with original furniture, a carriage house and a garden in the middle of downtown.
buzz: The volunteers know the family and the house is a step back into 1890s Fresno; it is small and only open afternoons.

name: Emerald Bay
unique: A glacier carved bay on Lake Tahoe with the only island in the lake, a 1929 stone castle on the shore and turquoise water clear to 60 feet.
buzz: The overlook on the highway is the postcard and the Vikingsholm trail down is steep; the castle tour is worth timing and the parking is limited.

name: Apple Hill
unique: A loop of apple farms in the Sierra foothills where you pick your own, buy cider doughnuts and watch trees turn, 45 minutes from Sacramento.
buzz: October weekends are a traffic jam and the pie sells out; go on a weekday and start at the top of the loop.

name: Marshall Gold Discovery State Historic Park
unique: The sawmill site where gold was found in 1848, with a replica mill, a mine tunnel, a blacksmith and a chance to pan for gold in the American River.
buzz: Panning is the reason children agree to the history; the park is shaded and the museum explains how the discovery changed the state.

name: Columbia State Historic Park
customer: History families, school groups, gold rush fans
unique: A gold rush town preserved as a living park, with a working stagecoach, a candy store in a brick 1850s building and shopkeepers in period dress.
buzz: The stagecoach ride and the panning are the family draws; the town is small and the summer heat is serious.

name: Railtown 1897
unique: A working roundhouse and steam shop where the locomotives that appeared in dozens of westerns are still maintained, with weekend steam excursions.
buzz: The roundhouse is the best part and the train ride runs on weekends; film fans come for the movie train history.

name: Don Pedro Lake
unique: A foothill reservoir with 160 miles of shoreline, a swim beach and a campground, warm enough for water sports by June.
buzz: The lake is the summer cooling off spot for the gold country; the water level drops late in the season and the wind comes up in the afternoon.

name: Chautauqua Park
unique: The Flatirons rise straight out of a 1898 Chautauqua campus, with a dining hall, a ranger cottage and trails that climb into the rock in 20 minutes.
buzz: The First and Second Flatiron trails are the local workout and the lawn is a picnic spot; parking fills by nine on weekends and the shuttle runs in summer.

name: Celestial Seasonings Tea Tour
unique: A walk through the tea factory past the mint room, where the smell is so strong visitors are warned, ending in a tasting room of every blend.
buzz: The mint room is the story everyone tells and the tasting is generous; the tour is free and requires a reservation.

name: Fiske Planetarium
unique: One of the largest planetariums in the country, with a dome 60 feet across and student led shows that include live tours of the current sky.
buzz: The live star talks are better than the recorded shows and the laser nights are the student tradition; check the schedule before driving.

name: Denver Art Museum
unique: Daniel Libeskind's angular steel building and a collection of Native American, Latin American and western art, including the finest collection of Indigenous art in the country.
buzz: The Indigenous arts galleries are the reason curators visit and the architecture is the family puzzle; the building is confusing and the map helps.

name: Denver Botanic Gardens
unique: Twenty four acres with a Japanese garden, a tropical conservatory and a Rocky Mountain alpine collection that grows plants from above treeline.
buzz: The Japanese garden and the conservatory are the winter stops; the summer concert series on the lawn is the local date night.

name: Molly Brown House Museum
unique: The 1889 Capitol Hill house of the Titanic survivor and suffragist, restored with period rooms and a tour that separates the myth from the life.
buzz: The guides are good at cutting through the Unsinkable Molly Brown legend; the house is small and the tour runs on the hour.

name: Breckenridge Ski Resort
unique: Five peaks above a preserved gold rush main street, with above treeline bowls, a high speed gondola and a town you can walk at the base.
buzz: The high alpine terrain is the draw and the altitude is real; the town is lively and the lift lines on peak weekends are the complaint.

name: Country Boy Mine
customer: Families, history kids, gold rush fans
unique: A real gold mine tunnel you walk into with a hard hat, and a hillside of ore chutes and buildings above Breckenridge, with gold panning at the end.
buzz: The underground tour is short and cool and the panning keeps children busy; it is the best rainy day activity in town.

name: Iowa Hill Trail
unique: A short trail through the remains of a hydraulic gold mining operation, with sluice cuts, a miner's cabin and a view over the town.
buzz: Locals use it as an easy evening walk and the signs explain what the ditches were for; it is free and takes an hour.

name: Vail Mountain
unique: The back bowls that changed American skiing, 5,300 acres across seven miles, with a village at the base built to look like a Tyrolean town.
buzz: Skiers come for the back bowls and the powder days; the front side gets tracked out fast and the village is expensive.

name: Betty Ford Alpine Gardens
unique: The highest botanical garden in the country at 8,200 feet, with rock gardens of alpine plants from around the world and a waterfall below the ski slopes.
buzz: Gardeners call it a miracle of microclimate and it is free; the peak is late June and the paths are steep.

name: Beaver Creek
unique: A resort built around a pedestrian village and a bird sanctuary, with groomed cruisers, a downhill race course and cookie time at the base each afternoon.
buzz: Families like the easy layout and the ski school; experts find it tame compared with Vail and the village is quiet at night.

name: Maroon Bells
unique: Two maroon striped peaks reflected in a glacial lake at the end of the most photographed road in Colorado, with trails into the Elk Mountains.
buzz: The lake at dawn is the photograph and the shuttle is mandatory in summer; the parking reservation system catches people out.

name: Aspen Art Museum
unique: A free museum in a Shigeru Ban building with a woven wood screen, a rooftop sculpture garden and a glass elevator that opens onto views of Aspen Mountain.
buzz: The roof deck and the building are worth the stop even if the exhibition is between shows; admission is free and it is a one hour visit.

name: Ashcroft Ghost Town
unique: A silver boom town of 2,000 people reduced to a handful of cabins in a meadow at the end of a dirt road, with the hotel and saloon still standing.
buzz: The setting under Castle Peak is the reason to come and the buildings are unrestored; the road is rough and the site is free.

name: Glenwood Hot Springs
unique: The world's largest mineral hot springs pool, a block long and fed by a Yampah spring at 122 degrees, with the Colorado River running past the wall.
buzz: The pool is the family side and the smaller therapy pool is quieter; it is busiest in ski season and the water is body temperature.

name: Hanging Lake
unique: A travertine lake hanging above Glenwood Canyon, with turquoise water, fallen logs and a waterfall, reached by a steep mile of switchbacks.
buzz: The permit system limits the crowd and the trail is steep and rocky; no swimming and the shuttle from Glenwood is the way in.

name: Glenwood Caverns
unique: A cave system inside Iron Mountain reached by a gondola, with formations lit in color and a cliffside coaster and swing on top.
buzz: The cave tour is the reason to come and the rides are the surprise; the combo ticket is the way to do both.

name: Colorado National Monument
unique: Red sandstone canyons and monoliths above the Grand Valley, with a 23 mile rim road, tunnel and trailheads that drop into the canyon.
buzz: The rim rock drive at sunset is the experience and the Monument Canyon trail is the hike; the road is narrow with cyclists.

name: Museum of the West
unique: A regional museum with Ute baskets, a taxidermy hall and a courtyard of pioneer cabins and farm equipment behind the main building.
buzz: The Ute collection is the serious part and the outdoor village is good with children; it is small and the staff are local experts.

name: Powderhorn Mountain
unique: A small ski hill on the Grand Mesa with a view into the Colorado National Monument, lift tickets half the price of the destination resorts and no lift lines.
buzz: Locals call it the best value in the state and the terrain is modest; the drive up the mesa can be snowy and the lodge is basic.

name: Crested Butte
unique: A ski mountain above a preserved Victorian mining town, with extreme terrain and a July wildflower bloom that draws botanists from other countries.
buzz: Skiers come for the steeps and the town is the reason to stay; the wildflower festival in July books a year out.

name: Taylor Reservoir
unique: A high reservoir below the Elk Mountains where the Taylor River runs out and rainbow trout stack up, ringed by forest service campgrounds.
buzz: Fishermen come for the tailwater below the dam and the jeep roads into the mountains are the local adventure; the water is cold and the wind picks up.

name: Curecanti National Recreation Area
unique: Three reservoirs in the Gunnison River gorge, with a 5.5 mile trail to the Morrow Point boat tour and osprey nests on the canyon walls.
buzz: The Morrow Point boat tour through the gorge is the hidden gem and it runs on a schedule; the lakes are windy in the afternoon.

name: Zapata Falls
unique: A short climb to a slot where the Zapata Creek drops into a cave behind the rock, with the Great Sand Dunes spread out below the trail.
buzz: The last stretch is a wade through cold water and the payoff is a waterfall inside a cave; the road is rough for low cars.

name: Colorado Gators Reptile Park
unique: A tilapia farm that became an alligator rescue in the San Luis Valley, with 200 gators in geothermal water and a chance to hold a small one.
buzz: People cannot believe alligators live in Colorado; the staff are rescuing animals and the feeding shows are the reason to check times.

name: Royal Gorge Bridge
unique: The highest suspension bridge in the country over the Arkansas River, with a gondola, a zip line and a skycoaster above a 1,000 foot gorge.
buzz: The bridge walk is the free thrill and the add ons cost extra; the park was rebuilt after a 2013 fire and the views are the point.

name: Skyline Drive
unique: A one way road along the crest of a dinosaur fossil ridge, with drops on both sides and a view of the Arkansas valley and the Sangre de Cristo range.
buzz: Locals take visitors up at sunset and the road is narrow and one way; dinosaur tracks were found along the ridge.

name: Mollie Kathleen Gold Mine
unique: A original gold mine cage drops you 1,000 feet underground into tunnels where ore cars, drills and stopes are still in place, guided by miners.
buzz: The cage ride is the thrill and the guides are retired miners; it is cold underground and the tour is the only way in.

name: Cripple Creek Heritage Center
unique: A free museum above the gold camp explaining the 1890s rush, the labor war and the open pit mine that swallowed part of the town.
buzz: The view from the deck and the film are the quick history lesson; it pairs with the Mollie Kathleen mine down the road.

name: Natural History Museum of Utah
unique: A copper clad building above the valley with a dinosaur wall of 60 skeletons, a Great Salt Lake exhibit and a gallery on the Fremont and Ancestral Puebloan cultures.
buzz: The dinosaur hall and the native voices gallery are the two reasons to come; the building's design and the terrace view of the Wasatch are the bonus.

name: Red Butte Garden
unique: A hundred acres in the foothills with a water conservation garden, a children's garden and a summer concert series in the amphitheater.
buzz: The water wise garden is the local lesson and the concerts sell out; the upper trails are steep and the view over the city is the rest.

name: Snowbird
unique: A steep resort at the top of Little Cottonwood Canyon with a tram to 11,000 feet, 500 inches of snow in a good year and a summer ride to a ridge walk.
buzz: Skiers say the terrain is as serious as anywhere in the country and the canyon closes for avalanches; the tram runs year round.

name: Bridal Veil Falls
unique: A 607 foot double cataract at the mouth of Provo Canyon, with a paved trail to the base and a pool that freezes into a blue cone in winter.
buzz: The walk is short and paved and the falls are visible from the road; the ice climb in winter is a local spectacle.

name: Museum of Ancient Life
unique: One of the largest dinosaur museums in the world, with 60 mounted skeletons, a working paleontology lab and a walk through the eras of life.
buzz: Children who are serious about dinosaurs will want three hours; the lab where fossils are prepared is the part adults linger at.

name: Timpanogos Cave
unique: Three connected caves full of helicitites and anthodites at the end of a steep 1.5 mile trail, with a view down the canyon the whole way.
buzz: The hike is the hard part and the cave tour is the reward; tickets sell out and the trail is hot and exposed.

name: Cedar Breaks
unique: A natural amphitheater at 10,000 feet with hoodoos in pink and orange limestone, less visited than Bryce and just as strange.
buzz: The rim trail at sunset is the photograph and the altitude is real; the road closes with snow from November to May.

name: Brian Head
unique: The highest base elevation of any resort in the state, with a long beginner run and red rock views from the lifts.
buzz: Families like the price and the lack of crowds; the terrain is modest and the drive from Las Vegas is four hours.

name: Parowan Gap
customer: Rock art people, road trippers, photographers
unique: A wind cut gap in the rock covered with hundreds of petroglyphs, including a calendar spiral that marks the solstice.
buzz: Archaeologists argue about the meanings and the site is free and unguarded; the drive is a short detour off Interstate 15.

name: The Wave
unique: A sandstone formation of red and pink swirls in Coyote Buttes North, reachable only by a six mile round trip hike and a permit that thousands apply for daily.
buzz: The lottery is the hard part and the navigation is the second; people who get in describe it as the best rock in the southwest.

name: Coral Pink Sand Dunes
unique: Pink sand dunes between red cliffs where a slot canyon funnels wind into ripples, with an ATV riding area and a closed preserve for a rare beetle.
buzz: Sandboarding down the big dune is the family fun and the ATV rental is at the entrance; the sand is hot in summer and the wind is constant.

name: Best Friends Animal Sanctuary
unique: The largest no kill animal sanctuary in the country, in Angel Canyon, with tours of the dog, cat and horse areas and volunteer shifts you can book.
buzz: Visitors say the tour is moving and the canyon setting is beautiful; you cannot adopt on a whim but you can walk dogs for a morning.

name: Valley of the Gods
unique: A 17 mile dirt road through red monoliths and mesas that look like Monument Valley without the fees or the crowds.
buzz: The drive is the attraction and the camping is free; the road is graded but rough after rain and there are no services.

name: Natural Bridges National Monument
unique: Three natural stone bridges in a canyon with a loop road and trails underneath, plus a dark sky designation and Ancestral Puebloan ruins on the mesa.
buzz: The Owachomo bridge at sunset is the photograph and the canyon hike is quiet; the park is remote and the nearest town is 40 minutes away.

name: Goosenecks
unique: The San Juan River loops through a 1,000 foot deep meander three times in a mile, one of the most dramatic incised meanders in the world.
buzz: The overlook is a short walk and the scale is hard to photograph; it is a 15 minute stop that people remember longer than expected.

name: Heber Valley Railroad
unique: A heritage railroad along Deer Creek Reservoir into Provo Canyon, with a steam engine on some weekends and a murder mystery train at night.
buzz: The canyon view from the open car is the reason to ride; the themed trains sell out and the ride is 90 minutes.

name: Wasatch Mountain State Park
unique: Twenty three thousand acres in the Wasatch foothills with a golf course, a reservoir and trails that climb into aspen, 20 minutes from Park City.
buzz: Locals use it for camping and fall color and the golf is cheap; the trails are shared with bikes and horses.

name: Dinosaur National Monument
unique: A quarry wall with 1,500 dinosaur bones still embedded in the rock, inside a building built over the dig, plus canyons where the Green and Yampa rivers meet.
buzz: The quarry wall is the thing people come for and it is better than any mounted skeleton; the river rafting through the canyon is the local secret.

name: Utah Field House of Natural History
unique: A museum with a garden of full size dinosaur sculptures, a walk through time hall and a fossil prep lab, next to the road into the monument.
buzz: The outdoor dinosaur garden is the photograph and the inside is a good rainy day stop; it takes 90 minutes.

name: Red Fleet State Park
unique: A reservoir with a dinosaur trackway on the shore and a hike to tracks left by a three toed dinosaur 200 million years ago.
buzz: The trackway hike is the reason to come and the water is warm enough to swim in summer; the reservoir levels drop late in the season.

name: Canyonlands: Island in the Sky
unique: A mesa between the Green and Colorado rivers with overlooks into a canyon system the size of a small state, including Mesa Arch at sunrise.
buzz: Mesa Arch is the photograph and the Grand View Point trail is the walk; the park is 40 minutes from Moab and far emptier than Arches.

name: Dead Horse Point
unique: A promontory 2,000 feet above a gooseneck of the Colorado with a view into Canyonlands, where cowboys once corralled wild horses on a neck of land.
buzz: Sunrise from the point is the classic and the mountain bike trail along the rim is a classic ride; the park is quieter than the national parks.

name: Colorado River Rafting from Moab
unique: A float through the red rock canyon below Moab with Class II and III rapids, a beach lunch and a view of arches and petroglyphs from the water.
buzz: The full day Fisher Towers section is the standard and the water is warm in summer; book ahead for holidays and bring sunscreen.

name: Snow Canyon
unique: Red and white sandstone formations with lava tubes, petrified sand dunes and a slot canyon, 15 minutes from St. George and often overlooked for Zion.
buzz: The Petrified Dunes trail and the lava tube are the local favorites; summer heat is brutal and the park is best at sunrise.

name: Tuacahn Amphitheatre
unique: A outdoor amphitheater in a red rock canyon where Broadway musicals use the cliff as a backdrop and mist the stage in summer heat.
buzz: The setting is the reason people go and the productions are better than expected; bring a cushion and expect a long walk from parking.

name: Utah Olympic Park
unique: The ski jumping and bobsled venue from the 2002 Games, with a museum, a zip line and a summer bobsled ride down the track.
buzz: The bobsled ride is the thrill and the ski jump elevator is the view; the museum is small but the athletes training are real.

name: High West Distillery
unique: A distillery on a historic ranch with a saloon and a barrel room, making rye whiskey at altitude in a state that used to ban the stuff.
buzz: The tasting is generous and the food is better than a distillery needs; the original Park City location is smaller and harder to park at.

name: Lagoon Amusement Park
unique: A 1886 resort with a wooden coaster, a pioneer village of moved buildings and a lagoon, still family owned and still a Utah summer ritual.
buzz: The wooden coaster and the pioneer village are the reasons locals defend it; the park is dated in places and the water park costs extra.

name: Great Salt Lake Shorelands Preserve
unique: A boardwalk through wetland and upland where the Great Salt Lake's brine flies and shrimp feed millions of migrating birds, with a visitor center and tower.
buzz: Birders come in spring and fall and the boardwalk is flat; the lake levels have dropped and the shoreline has moved.

name: Topaz Museum
customer: History people, students, civil rights pilgrims
unique: A museum in Delta telling the story of the 11,000 Japanese Americans imprisoned at Topaz during the war, with barracks, artifacts and an art school that flourished behind barbed wire.
buzz: Visitors say it is one of the most important small museums in the country; the site itself is 16 miles out of town and marked by a monument.

name: Georgia O'Keeffe Museum
unique: The largest collection of O'Keeffe's work in the world, from the Lake George flowers to the Ghost Ranch bones, in a adobe block a few steps from the plaza.
buzz: The paintings and her studio objects together explain how she saw the landscape; the museum is small and the timed ticket keeps it calm.

name: Canyon Road
unique: A half mile of adobe houses turned into more than 80 galleries, from cowboy painters to contemporary installations, with sculpture courtyards open to the street.
buzz: The Friday night openings in summer are the social event and the side streets have the smaller galleries; most places welcome browsers.

name: Santa Fe Farmers Market
unique: A covered market in the Railyard where northern New Mexico farms sell chile, apples, goat cheese and dried corn, with a breakfast counter inside.
buzz: Locals come at eight for the chile and the breakfast burritos; the Railyard around it has galleries and a cinema for the rest of the morning.

name: Indian Pueblo Cultural Center
unique: A museum owned by the 19 pueblos, with a gallery for each, a courtyard for dances and a restaurant serving pueblo food, on Route 66.
buzz: The dance schedule on weekends is the reason to check ahead; the restaurant's pueblo oven bread and blue corn enchiladas are the local recommendation.

name: Old Town Albuquerque
unique: The adobe plaza founded in 1706, with the San Felipe de Neri church, a row of shops under portales and a bandstand where mariachi plays on weekends.
buzz: It is touristy and small and the church and the plaza are worth the walk; the rattlesnake museum and the candy shop are the family stops.

name: Organ Mountains Desert Peaks
unique: A national monument of jagged granite peaks above the Rio Grande valley, with trails into the Organ Mountains and a desert of lava and petroglyphs.
buzz: The Dripping Springs trail is the local hike and the peaks glow at sunset; the desert sections are exposed and the heat is serious in summer.

name: Mesilla Plaza
unique: The adobe plaza that was briefly the Confederate capital of Arizona, with the Basilica of San Albino, a double eagle on the wall and a cantina where Billy the Kid was jailed.
buzz: The plaza is small and the history is dense; the restaurants around it serve some of the best New Mexican food in the state.

name: New Mexico Farm and Ranch Museum
unique: A working farm and museum with dairy cows, sheep, a greenhouse and exhibits on how irrigation and cattle changed the desert.
buzz: Children like the animals and adults like the machinery; it is cheap and the demonstrations on weekends are the reason to time a visit.

name: Bandelier National Monument
unique: Ancestral Puebloan homes carved into soft volcanic tuff, with ladders into cavates and a trail along the canyon wall above a creek.
buzz: The Main Loop and Alcove House are the standard route and the ladders are the fun; the shuttle from White Rock runs in summer.

name: Valles Caldera
unique: A 13 mile wide volcanic caldera with grassy valleys and forested rims, where elk herds graze and the Jemez River rises from springs.
buzz: The elk in the valley at dusk are the reason to come and the preserve is quiet; the dirt roads close with snow and the backcountry needs a permit.

name: Walatowa Visitor Center
unique: A visitor center at the entrance to Jemez Pueblo with a small museum of pueblo history and access to Red Rock canyon, where the pueblo's story is told by its own people.
buzz: The center is the only way to learn about the pueblo without intruding; photography rules are strict and the red rock formations are the draw.

name: Ghost Ranch
unique: The red and yellow cliffs where Georgia O'Keeffe painted for decades, now a retreat and education center with trails, a museum and guided tours to her house.
buzz: The landscape is the attraction and the tour to O'Keeffe's house needs booking; the trails are open and the light changes all afternoon.

name: El Santuario de Chimayo
