unique: A small adobe chapel built around a pit of earth said to heal, visited by hundreds of thousands of pilgrims each year, especially during Holy Week.
buzz: People describe the room of crutches and the quiet; it is an active church and visitors should be respectful, especially during services.

name: Echo Amphitheater
unique: A natural stone bowl above the road where the echo comes back clearly, with a short trail to the base of the cliff.
buzz: It is a ten minute stop on the drive to Ghost Ranch and people shout into it; the picnic tables and the red rock are the rest.

name: Rio Grande Gorge Bridge
unique: The seventh highest bridge in the country, 650 feet above the Rio Grande, with a walkway on both sides and a view of the gorge that opens under your feet.
buzz: The west side rest area has the vendors and the view; the bridge walk is free and the wind is strong enough to hold you up.

name: Taos Ski Valley
unique: A steep European style mountain with hike to terrain and chutes, in a high desert valley where the snow is dry and the sun is usually out.
buzz: Experts rate the steeps with anything in Colorado and the base area is small; the drive from Taos is 20 minutes and the altitude is 9,200 feet.

name: Pecos National Historical Park
unique: The ruins of a 17th century mission church beside the remains of a pueblo that traded with the plains, on the route of the Santa Fe Trail.
buzz: The church walls and the reconstructed kiva are the walk and the ranger talks explain the Pueblo Revolt; the park is quiet and free.

name: Las Vegas Plaza
unique: A plaza ringed by 900 historic buildings from the Santa Fe Trail boom, including a hotel where Doc Holliday and Billy the Kid drank, largely unrestored.
buzz: Architecture people call it the best preserved Victorian town in the southwest and it is nearly empty; some buildings are fragile.

name: City of Rocks State Park
unique: A field of volcanic rock columns standing like a city skyline, with campsites tucked between the pillars and a botanical garden of desert plants.
buzz: The camping between the rocks is the experience and the night sky is dark; the park is exposed and hot in summer.

name: Silver City Historic District
unique: A copper mining town in a canyon with a brick downtown, the Big Ditch that carries the creek under the street and a museum of the mining wars.
buzz: The town is the base for the Gila wilderness and the historic district is a good hour; the university and the bike trail keep it alive.

name: Three Rivers Petroglyph Site
unique: More than 21,000 petroglyphs on a ridge of basalt boulders, one of the largest rock art sites in the southwest, with a trail through the middle.
buzz: The density is what surprises people and the trail is short; the site is exposed and the nearest town is 20 minutes away.

name: Oliver Lee Memorial State Park
unique: A ranch house and campground at the mouth of Dog Canyon on the west face of the Sacramento Mountains, with a trail into a cool canyon and desert views.
buzz: The canyon trail is the hike and the campground has shade; it is a quiet base for White Sands 30 minutes away.

name: Sitting Bull Falls
unique: A 150 foot waterfall in a desert canyon with a pool you can swim in, reached by a 40 mile drive through the Chihuahuan desert.
buzz: The waterfall in the desert is the surprise and the pool is cold; the road is remote and the area can close for flooding.

name: Red Rock Park
unique: Red sandstone cliffs and a box canyon just outside Gallup, with trails to petroglyphs and an amphitheater that hosts the intertribal ceremonial in August.
buzz: The August ceremonial is the reason to time a visit and the trails are quiet otherwise; the park is a short drive off Interstate 40.

name: Zuni Pueblo
unique: The largest pueblo in the state, known for inlay jewelry and fetish carving, with a mission church whose murals were painted by Zuni artists in the 1970s.
buzz: The mural church is the highlight and tours are led by tribal members; photography is restricted and the pueblo asks visitors to check in first.

name: El Malpais National Monument
unique: A lava field with ice caves, a sandstone arch and a 17 mile lava tube, on a high plateau where the flows are up to 100,000 years old.
buzz: The lava tube needs a permit and a headlamp and the ice cave is a short walk; the landscape is black and strange and the trails are unmarked in places.

name: Acoma Sky City
unique: One of the oldest continuously inhabited places in the country, a mesa top village 367 feet above the desert with adobe houses, a mission church and a view of the lava country.
buzz: The tour is led by Acoma guides and photography requires a permit; visitors say the church and the story of the 1599 massacre stay with them.

name: Bottomless Lakes State Park
unique: A chain of sinkhole lakes in the desert, formed when groundwater dissolved the limestone, with a swimming beach and a dive training area.
buzz: The water is clear and cold and the diving platforms are the local training spot; the lakes are small and the park is quiet outside summer.

name: Bradbury Science Museum
unique: A free museum on the Manhattan Project and the lab that grew from it, with a replica of the first atomic bombs, a supercomputer and a defense gallery.
buzz: The history gallery is frank about the bomb and the science exhibits are hands on; it is the best explanation of Los Alamos anywhere.

name: Capulin Volcano
unique: A symmetrical cinder cone with a road spiraling to the rim and a trail around the crater, looking out over a field of older volcanoes and three states.
buzz: The drive up is the attraction and the rim trail is a mile; the view from the top on a clear day reaches Colorado and Oklahoma.

name: National Automobile Museum
unique: Two hundred cars from the Harrah collection, arranged in streetscapes from 1900s to the 1950s, including the 1907 Thomas Flyer that won the New York to Paris race.
buzz: The street scenes are what make it different from a parking lot of cars; the Thomas Flyer and the Cadillac V16 are the two people photograph.

name: Nevada Museum of Art
unique: A museum with a roof deck of giant letters spelling out a landscape essay, plus a strong collection on the Great Basin and the environment.
buzz: The rooftop sculpture and the view of the Sierra are the reason to go up; the galleries are small and the building is the surprise.

name: Great Reno Balloon Race
unique: A free balloon festival where 100 balloons launch at dawn from a park inside the city, with a glow show before sunrise and a teddy bear drop for children.
buzz: The 5am glow is the photograph and the dawn patrol is worth the alarm; traffic is heavy and the parking shuttle is the way in.

name: Pyramid Lake
unique: A desert lake with tufa towers and a hot spring, home to the Lahontan cutthroat trout that can reach 20 pounds, on Paiute land.
buzz: Anglers come for the trout and the tufa formations at sunrise are the photograph; the lake is tribal land and requires a permit.

name: Virginia City
unique: A silver boom town on a mountainside with a wooden main street, saloons, a opera house and the mine that produced the Comstock Lode.
buzz: The board sidewalks and the old bars are the atmosphere; it is touristy in summer and the mine tours are the serious history.

name: Virginia and Truckee Railroad
unique: A restored steam railroad that climbs from Virginia City down toward the Carson River, on the grade that carried Comstock silver to the mills.
buzz: The open car and the tunnel are the fun and the commentary explains the mining; the ride is short enough for small children.

name: Fourth Ward School Museum
unique: A four story 1876 schoolhouse with original desks and chalkboards, built for 1,000 students when Virginia City was one of the richest towns in America.
buzz: The building is the exhibit and the classrooms are intact; the top floor view of the town and the mountains is the bonus.

name: National Cowboy Poetry Gathering
customer: Poetry people, ranchers, folk music fans
unique: A week of cowboy poetry, music and storytelling in a Nevada cow town, with workshops, dances and performers who still work cattle.
buzz: People arrive from ranches across the west and the late night sessions in the bars are the real festival; book lodging months ahead.

name: California Trail Interpretive Center
customer: History families, road trippers, school groups
unique: A free center on the emigrant trail where 250,000 people crossed the desert, with wagons, diaries and a walk to the ruts still visible in the sagebrush.
buzz: The diaries are the exhibit and the trail ruts outside are the real thing; it is the best stop on Interstate 80 between Salt Lake and Reno.

name: Lamoille Canyon
unique: A glacier carved canyon in the Ruby Mountains with 12 miles of road, waterfalls and trailheads into alpine lakes, called the Switzerland of Nevada.
buzz: The drive to the road end and the hike to Lamoille Lake are the standard; the canyon is snowed in from November to June.

name: Eureka Opera House
customer: History people, music fans, road trippers
unique: A restored 1880 opera house in a silver mining town of 500 people, with painted scenery, a horseshoe balcony and a season of concerts and plays.
buzz: The room is the attraction and the acoustics are good; call ahead, it is not open every day.

name: Eureka Sentinel Museum
unique: The old Sentinel newspaper office with its press, type cases and a wall of 19th century issues still in place, in a town of brick buildings from the silver boom.
buzz: The press and the type are the reason to stop and the museum is free; the whole town is a half hour walk.

name: Stokes Castle
unique: A three story stone tower built by a silver baron as a summer home, abandoned after a few months and now standing over the Reese River valley.
buzz: The story is better than the ruin and the view down the valley is the reason to climb the short hill; it is a ten minute stop.

name: Austin Historic District
unique: A silver boom town climbing a canyon wall on the Loneliest Road, with a church, a castle and brick ruins stacked above the highway.
buzz: The drive through town is the attraction and the grid of streets is steep; it is a good leg stretch on Highway 50.

name: Buckaroo Hall of Fame
customer: Cowboy culture people, road trippers, families
unique: A small hall in the Winnemucca convention center honoring the Great Basin buckaroos, with saddles, spurs, braided rawhide and portraits of working hands.
buzz: The gear is beautiful and the stories are local; it is free and takes 30 minutes, a good stop on Interstate 80.

name: Black Rock Desert
unique: A dry lakebed so flat and empty that land speed records and a temporary city are built on it, with hot springs and a canyon at the edges.
buzz: The playa in summer is brutal and the solitude is the point; check conditions, since rain turns the surface to impassable mud.

name: Lahontan State Recreation Area
unique: A desert reservoir on the Carson River with sandy beaches, cottonwood groves and good fishing for walleye and catfish.
buzz: The beaches are the summer swim and the river inlet is the fishing spot; the water level varies a lot year to year.

name: Churchill County Museum
customer: Local history people, families, school groups
unique: A museum with a reconstructed 1900s main street, a Pony Express exhibit and a basement of mining and ranching equipment.
buzz: The street scene is the reason to bring children and the Pony Express room is the history; it is small and volunteer run.

name: Fort Churchill State Historic Park
unique: Adobe ruins of a Civil War era army post on the Carson River, built to protect the emigrant road, with a cemetery and a cottonwood campground.
buzz: The adobe walls and the river walk are the visit and the campground is green and quiet; it is a good stop between Reno and Las Vegas.

name: Dayton State Park
unique: The site of Nevada's first gold discovery, with a five stamp mill, a tunnel and tailings you can walk among on the Carson River.
buzz: The mill is the reason to stop and the town of Dayton has a old main street; it is a short visit and the park is small.

name: Hawthorne Ordnance Museum
customer: Military history people, road trippers, families
unique: A museum of artillery, bombs and ammunition from the naval depot that stored munitions here for decades, with rows of shells and a atomic cannon shell.
buzz: The scale of the collection is what people remember and the volunteers are veterans; it is free and takes an hour.

name: Walker Lake
unique: A desert lake below the Wassuk Range where the water has receded for decades and the shoreline is a study in alkali and abandoned piers.
buzz: Photographers come for the emptiness and the mountains; the lake is too salty for most fish now and the shore is stark.

name: Cathedral Gorge State Park
unique: Soft bentonite clay eroded into cathedral spires and slot canyons, with trails through the spires and a campground at the edge.
buzz: The slot canyon trail is the walk and the spires glow at sunset; the clay is slippery when wet and the park is remote.

name: Pioche Boot Hill
unique: A hillside cemetery where the graves outnumber the living town several times over, with wooden markers and the story of a silver camp that killed its men faster than it buried them.
buzz: The handwritten grave markers and the view over town are the reason to climb; the town below has a restored opera house and a mile long main street.

name: Gold Point Ghost Town
customer: Ghost town hunters, photographers, road trippers
unique: A silver camp of 30 surviving buildings kept up by a handful of residents, with a saloon and a general store you can walk into.
buzz: The caretakers live on site and will talk about the town; the road in is gravel and the nearest gas is 30 miles away.

name: Nevada State Railroad Museum
unique: A collection of Virginia and Truckee locomotives including the Inyo, a 1875 4-4-0 that pulled the first train to Carson City, with weekend rides.
buzz: The roundhouse and the restored cars are the reason to come; the ride is short but the collection is serious.

name: Kit Carson Trail
company: Carson City Convention and Visitors Bureau
unique: A walking tour of the state capital's Victorian houses and the governor's mansion, with a audio guide and a cemetery where the city's founders are buried.
buzz: The self guided map is free at the visitors center and the October ghost walk is the local tradition; most of the trail is flat.

name: Nevada State Museum
unique: A museum in the old Carson City mint building, with a working coin press, a Nevada history hall and a full skeleton of an ichthyosaur found in the state.
buzz: The mint press and the ichthyosaur are the two things people remember; the building itself is the oldest mint still standing west of the Mississippi.

name: Little A'Le'Inn
unique: A diner and motel on the Extraterrestrial Highway at the edge of Area 51, with alien murals, a gift shop and a burger named after the nearby base.
buzz: The owner tells the stories and the walls are covered in visitor tags; it is a long empty drive and the diner is the only thing for 50 miles.

name: National Historic Trails Interpretive Center
customer: History families, road trippers, school groups
unique: A free center where the Oregon, California, Mormon and Pony Express trails all crossed the North Platte, with covered wagons you can climb into and a simulated river crossing.
buzz: The wagon and the crossing simulation are what children remember; the diaries and the maps are the adult version and the view of Casper Mountain is the setting.

name: Independence Rock
unique: A granite dome the emigrants called the Register of the Desert, covered in carved names, where wagon trains aimed to arrive by July 4 to make the mountains before snow.
buzz: The names on the rock are the thing and the climb is short; it is a good leg stretch on Highway 220 and the ruts are nearby.

name: Fort Caspar
unique: A reconstructed 1860s military post and emigrant crossing on the Oregon Trail, with a ferry replica and a museum of the telegraph line.
buzz: The rebuilt buildings and the wagon ruts are the visit and the summer demonstrations bring it alive; it is small and the river setting is pleasant.

name: Wyoming Territorial Prison
customer: History people, families, true crime fans
unique: A stone territorial prison where Butch Cassidy served time, with cell blocks, a broom factory and a warden's house, on a bluff above Laramie.
buzz: The cell block and the stories of the inmates are the tour; it is small and the self guided map lets you move at your own pace.

name: University of Wyoming Geological Museum
unique: A free museum with a Apatosaurus skeleton, a wall of Wyoming fossils and a mastodon, in a university building that has been collecting since the 1880s.
buzz: The dinosaur hall is the family stop and the fossil collection is serious; it is free and takes an hour.

name: Sinks Canyon
unique: A river that disappears into a limestone cave and reappears a quarter mile down the canyon, with a viewing bridge and trout you can feed at the rise.
buzz: The disappearing river is the story and the trout at the rise are a hit with children; the canyon trails climb above the road.

name: South Pass City
customer: History families, ghost town hunters, road trippers
unique: A gold camp of 30 original buildings at the crossing of the Oregon Trail, where Wyoming gave women the vote in 1869 and the first woman justice of the peace was elected.
buzz: The restored buildings and the Esther Hobart Morris story are the history; the drive over South Pass is half the visit.

name: Riverton Museum
unique: A small museum on the Wind River with Arapaho and Shoshone beadwork, a pioneer kitchen and a room on the oil boom that changed the town.
buzz: The Native collection and the local stories are the reason to stop; it is volunteer run and the staff will talk.

name: King's Saddlery
unique: A saddlery and rope shop with a museum of braided rawhide and horsehair hitches behind the sales floor, run by a family that still makes tack for working ranches.
buzz: The museum cases are free and the workmanship is museum grade; the shop sells ropes and hats and the staff will explain what you are looking at.

name: Trail End State Historic Site
customer: House tour people, history fans, families
unique: A 1913 Flemish revival mansion built by a cattle baron and later a governor, with original furniture and a view over Sheridan.
buzz: The house is unrestored in the best way and the guides know the family; the tour runs on the hour and is short.

name: Bighorn Canyon
unique: A canyon 1,000 feet deep where the Bighorn River runs between Wyoming and Montana, with wild horses on the uplands and a lake for fishing and boating.
buzz: The drive along the rim and the boat up the canyon are the two ways to see it; the park is quiet and the wild horses are a bonus.

name: Medicine Wheel
unique: A 80 foot stone wheel at 9,600 feet on the Bighorn range, aligned with the summer solstice and considered sacred by several tribes, reached by a 1.5 mile walk.
buzz: The walk is the pilgrimage and the wheel is roped off for protection; visitors are asked to treat it as a church and the altitude is serious.

name: Hot Springs State Park
unique: A free state bathhouse with water at 104 degrees, a travertine terrace above the Bighorn River and a buffalo herd in the park.
buzz: The free bathhouse is the local institution and the state park is free; the commercial pools next door have slides and quieter hours.

name: Wyoming Dinosaur Center
unique: A museum with a 106 foot Supersaurus and a dig site on a nearby mesa where visitors can join a real excavation for a day.
buzz: The dig program is the reason people come from other states and the mounted skeletons are the rainy day version; book the dig weeks ahead.

name: Ten Sleep Canyon
unique: A limestone canyon with hundreds of sport climbing routes on both walls, and a road that switchbacks 2,000 feet up to the Bighorn plateau.
buzz: Climbers call it one of the best limestone destinations in the country and the drive is the scenic route; the canyon is hot in summer and the rock is sharp.

name: Washakie Museum
unique: A museum on the Bighorn Basin with a mammoth skeleton found nearby, Native beadwork and a room on the German POW camp that was here in the war.
buzz: The mammoth and the POW story are the surprises; it is small and the staff are proud of the local finds.

name: Jim Gatchell Memorial Museum
unique: A drugstore owner's collection of frontier weapons, saddles and Lakota artifacts, with a room on the Johnson County War and the cattle barons' invasion.
buzz: The Johnson County War exhibit is the reason history people stop and the collection is bigger than the building suggests; it takes 90 minutes.

name: Cloud Peak Wilderness
unique: A quarter million acres of roadless Bighorn high country with 13,000 foot peaks, glacial lakes and cutthroat trout, reached by trails from West Tensleep.
buzz: Backpackers say it is the emptiest big wilderness in the lower 48 and the weather turns fast; the trails are unmarked in places.

name: Fort Bridger
customer: History families, trail people, school groups
unique: A fur trading post turned army fort on the Oregon Trail, with original stone buildings, a museum and a Labor Day rendezvous with mountain men and buckskinners.
buzz: The rendezvous weekend is the time to go and the stone buildings are the real thing; the site is quiet otherwise and the grounds are free to walk.

name: Bear River State Park
unique: A small state park with a herd of bison and elk you can see from the road, and a river walk, on the edge of Evanston.
buzz: The bison are the reason to stop and the park is free; it is a good break on Interstate 80 with children.

name: Fossil Butte National Monument
unique: A butte of ancient lakebed where 50 million year old fish are quarried out whole, with a visitor center of prepared specimens and a quarry trail you can hike.
buzz: The fish fossils are astounding and the quarry trail is short; the park is remote and the preparation lab is where people linger.

name: Intermittent Spring
unique: A spring that flows heavily for several minutes and then stops, probably because of a natural siphon in the mountain, reached by a mile and a half trail.
buzz: The timing is unpredictable and that is the fun; scientists have studied it and locals take visitors up in summer.

name: Flaming Gorge
company: National Park Service and Bureau of Reclamation
unique: A red rock canyon flooded into a 91 mile reservoir with trophy lake trout and a dam you can tour, on the Green River above the Colorado.
buzz: Anglers come for the big lake trout and the canyon drive on the Sheep Creek loop is the scenery; the water is cold and the wind is strong.

name: White Mountain Petroglyphs
customer: Rock art people, road trippers, photographers
unique: A sandstone cliff covered with petroglyphs of bison, elk and human figures, some a thousand years old, reached by a short walk on a dirt road.
buzz: The figures are large and clear and the site is unguarded; the drive is 15 miles of gravel and the wind never stops.

name: Wyoming Pioneer Memorial Museum
unique: A museum on the state fairgrounds with a pioneer cabin, a one room school and the saddles and brands of the ranches that settled the Platte valley.
buzz: The buildings out back are the charm and it is free; the state fair in August fills the grounds.

name: Guernsey State Park
unique: A reservoir with CCC built stone picnic shelters and a castle-like museum, and the Register Cliff where emigrants carved their names on the Oregon Trail.
buzz: The CCC stonework is the reason architecture people stop and the lake is the summer swim; Register Cliff is a short drive away.

name: Fort Laramie
customer: History families, trail people, school groups
unique: The fur trading post and army fort that anchored the Oregon Trail, with 20 original buildings, Officers' Row and the treaty grounds where the 1851 council was held.
buzz: The ranger tours and the restored barracks are the visit; it is free and the scale is bigger than people expect on the high plains.

name: Campbell County Rockpile Museum
customer: Local history people, energy workers, families
unique: A museum of the coal and oil boom that built Gillette, with a coal camp kitchen, a rail car and a room on the homesteaders who came before.
buzz: The energy history is unusually honest about the booms and busts; it is free and the staff are local.

name: Virginia City
customer: Ghost town hunters, history families, photographers
unique: A gold rush town of 300 original buildings, including the first newspaper office and a opera house, preserved as a state historic site with board sidewalks.
buzz: The buildings are unrestored and the town is quiet compared with the Wyoming version; the live theater in summer is the local tradition.

name: Lewis and Clark Caverns
unique: The largest cave system in the northwest, with a guided tour through limestone passages and a view over the Jefferson River valley from the entrance.
buzz: The tour is two hours with a lot of stairs and the cave is 48 degrees; the view from the top is the reward before you go in.

name: A Carousel for Missoula
unique: A hand carved carousel built by 1,000 volunteers over four years, with 38 horses, a dragon chariot and a band organ, in a glass pavilion by the river.
buzz: The story of the volunteers is on the walls and the ride is two dollars; children pick the dragon and adults look at the carving.

name: Smokejumper Visitor Center
unique: The base where the smokejumpers train, with a loft of parachutes, a plane you can walk through and a film on jumping into fires.
buzz: The plane and the gear are the exhibits and the jumpers are often there training; it is free and the tour is short.

name: Rattlesnake Wilderness
unique: A roadless area that starts at the edge of Missoula, with a creek trail into alpine lakes and enough climb to feel remote in an hour.
buzz: Locals run it after work and the lake is a half day; the trail is shared with mountain bikes on some sections.

name: Giant Springs State Park
unique: One of the largest freshwater springs in the country, pouring 156 million gallons a day into the Missouri, with a trout hatchery and a riverwalk.
buzz: The spring pool and the rainbow trout are the stops and it is free; the River's Edge Trail continues for miles along the Missouri.

name: C.M. Russell Museum
customer: Western art people, history fans, families
unique: The largest collection of Charles Russell's paintings and sculpture, plus his log studio and the cabin where he worked, in his hometown.
buzz: The studio and the watercolors are the reason art people come; the museum explains how a cowboy became the west's painter.

name: Lewis and Clark Interpretive Center
unique: A center on the portage the expedition made around the Great Falls, with a full size canoe, interactive exhibits and trails to the river overlooks.
buzz: The portage story is the part of the expedition people do not know and the center tells it well; the trails outside are free.

name: Pictograph Cave State Park
unique: Three rock shelters with painted figures up to 2,000 years old, excavated in the 1930s, on a rim above the Yellowstone valley.
buzz: The pictographs are faint and the story is the archaeology; the loop trail is short and the view of Billings is the bonus.

name: ZooMontana
unique: A small zoo focused on northern climates, with grizzly bears, wolves and a sensory garden, on the Yellowstone River rimrocks.
buzz: The grizzlies and the wolves are the reason to come and the zoo is small enough for two hours; it is good with young children.

name: Moss Mansion
customer: House tour people, history fans, families
unique: A 1903 sandstone mansion built by a cattle and banking family, with original furnishings, a ballroom and a staircase that curves three stories.
buzz: The woodwork and the family story are the tour; the October ghost tours are the local tradition.

name: Whitefish Mountain Resort
unique: A locals' mountain above Whitefish with tree skiing, a long groomer from the summit and a view into Glacier National Park from the top.
buzz: Skiers like the lack of crowds and the tree runs; the summit is windy and the base lodge is dated in a good way.

name: Flathead Lake
unique: The largest natural freshwater lake west of the Mississippi, 28 miles long with orchards along the east shore and islands you can camp on.
buzz: The cherries in July and the water in August are the two seasons; the lake is deep and cold and the wind comes up in the afternoon.

name: Lake Como
unique: A mountain lake at the end of a valley in the Bitterroots, with a beach, a campground and trails up to a waterfall and a ridge.
buzz: The lake is the easy family swim and the waterfall trail is the hike; the road is gravel for the last stretch.

name: St. Mary Peak
unique: A 9,351 foot peak in the Bitterroot range with a fire lookout on top and a view into Idaho, reached by a steep trail from the valley.
buzz: Hikers call it the best day hike in the Bitterroots and the lookout volunteer will show you the map; the trail is long and exposed.

name: Daly Mansion
customer: House tour people, gardeners, history fans
unique: A 50 room Georgian revival mansion built by a copper king, with original furnishings, a carriage house and 46 acres of lawns and gardens.
buzz: The house is enormous and the family story is the tour; the grounds are free and the summer concerts are the local event.

name: Kootenai Falls
unique: One of the largest free flowing waterfalls in the northwest, where the Kootenai drops through a gorge, with a swinging bridge over the river to the far side.
buzz: The swinging bridge is the thrill and the falls are the photograph; the trail is steep in places and the river is not for swimming.

name: Ross Creek Cedars
unique: A grove of western red cedars up to 12 feet across and 1,000 years old, with a flat loop trail through the trunks in the Cabinet Mountains.
buzz: The scale of the trees is the surprise and the trail is easy; the road in is gravel and the grove is quiet even in August.

name: Libby Dam
unique: A concrete dam 422 feet high on the Kootenai with a visitor center, a tour inside the powerhouse and a reservoir that runs 90 miles into Canada.
buzz: The tour into the dam is the reason to stop and the lake is beautiful; it is free and the guides explain the flood control.

name: Museum of the Plains Indian
unique: A museum of Plains Indian beadwork, quillwork and clothing from the Blackfeet, Crow and Sioux, with a diorama hall built in the 1940s.
buzz: The beadwork is museum grade and the collection is unexpected for a small town; the annual Indian Days powwow in July fills Browning.

name: Two Medicine Lake
unique: A glacial lake below Rising Wolf Mountain with a 1913 chalet, a boat shuttle and trails to twin waterfalls and a pass into the backcountry.
buzz: The boat across the lake and the hike to Upper Two Medicine is the quiet alternative to the Going-to-the-Sun crowds; the water is cold and the wind is real.

name: Bannack State Park
unique: Montana's first territorial capital, a gold camp of 60 original buildings along a creek, abandoned when the gold ran out and kept as a state park.
buzz: The buildings are unrestored and you can walk into most of them; the July ghost walk and the living history weekends are the local events.

name: Clark Canyon Reservoir
unique: A reservoir on the Beaverhead where Lewis and Clark camped, with trophy rainbow trout and a campground on the shore below the Tendoy Mountains.
buzz: Fishermen come for the big rainbows below the dam and the lake is quiet; the wind makes afternoon boating a chore.

name: Old Montana Prison
customer: History people, true crime fans, families
unique: A territorial prison with cell blocks, a dungeon and a walled yard, plus a complex of car museums and a doll museum on the same ticket.
buzz: The cell blocks and the stories of the 1959 riot are the tour; the car collection next door is the surprise for people who came for the prison.

name: Grant-Kohrs Ranch
customer: History families, ranch people, school groups
unique: A working cattle ranch that was the center of the open range era, with the original bunkhouse, blacksmith shop and a herd of cattle and horses.
buzz: The rangers run the ranch with horses and the bunkhouse tour is the reason to come; it is free and the scale is bigger than a museum.

name: Red Lodge Mountain
unique: A ski hill above a historic coal town with long groomers, tree skiing and a view of the Beartooth range, at half the price of the destination resorts.
buzz: Locals like the price and the lack of lines; the mountain is modest and the town is the reason to stay overnight.

name: Boise Art Museum
unique: A museum in Julia Davis Park with a strong collection of American art and a sculpture garden, next to the zoo and the state historical museum.
buzz: The sculpture garden and the rotating contemporary shows are the draw; it is small enough for an hour and the park is the rest of the afternoon.

name: Idaho State Capitol
unique: A sandstone capitol with a marble dome covered in native copper, and a law library in the basement that looks like a Victorian club.
buzz: The dome and the original chambers are the tour and it is free; the basement library is the room people photograph.

name: Bogus Basin
unique: A nonprofit ski area 16 miles from downtown Boise with night skiing, 2,600 acres and a summer mountain bike park.
buzz: Locals ski after work and the price is the reason; the terrain is gentle and the road up can be snowy.

name: Tubbs Hill
unique: A forested peninsula on Lake Coeur d'Alene with a loop trail, granite cliffs and swimming coves, a short walk from downtown.
buzz: The loop is the local after work walk and the coves are the summer swim; the trail is rocky and the lake is cold.

name: Silverwood Theme Park
unique: A theme park and water park in the Idaho panhandle with a wooden coaster, a steam train and a 1915 carousel, plus a Boulder Beach water park.
buzz: The train and the coaster are the family standards; it is smaller than a California park and the lines are shorter in June.

name: Cataldo Mission
unique: The oldest standing building in Idaho, a church built by Jesuit missionaries and the Coeur d'Alene people with hand hewn timber and painted walls.
buzz: The church and the story of the mission are the tour; the grounds are quiet and the old cataldo town site is a short walk.

name: Musical Instrument Museum
unique: A museum where the headphones switch to the music of whatever gallery you stand in, from a Steinway to a Tibetan trumpet, with instruments from every country.
buzz: People plan two hours and stay four; the mechanical instrument gallery and the artist gallery with Prince's and Clapton's instruments are the two stops.

name: Desert Botanical Garden
unique: Fifty thousand desert plants from around the world on 140 acres in Papago Park, with a butterfly pavilion and a trail through a sonoran desert that looks planted but is wild.
buzz: The cactus and succulent collection is the reason gardeners come and the butterfly exhibit runs in spring; summer heat limits the visit to early morning.

name: Heard Museum
unique: The best collection of Native American art in the country, with a room of katsina dolls, contemporary Indigenous painting and a courtyard of pueblo jewelry makers.
buzz: The katsina gallery and the board of trustees' collection are the highlights; the museum is frank about the boarding schools and the jewelry market is real.

name: Saguaro National Park
unique: Two districts of saguaro forest around Tucson, with a scenic loop drive, petroglyphs and trails through cactus that can live 150 years.
buzz: The west district at sunset is the photograph and the east district has the loop drive; go early or late, the midday heat is dangerous.

name: Pima Air and Space Museum
unique: One of the largest aircraft collections in the country, with 400 planes across 80 acres, including a SR-71 and a B-29, plus a tram tour of the bone yard.
buzz: The outdoor storage rows are the reason enthusiasts come and the tram saves walking; the hangars are hot in summer.

name: Mission San Xavier del Bac
unique: The white desert mission on the Tohono O'odham reservation, with painted interior walls, carved doors and a restoration that has lasted decades.
buzz: The interior is the surprise and the fry bread stand outside is the local lunch; it is an active church, so visitors should respect services.

name: Grand Canyon Skywalk
unique: A glass horseshoe suspended 4,000 feet above the Colorado on the Hualapai reservation, reached by a dirt road and a shuttle from the west rim.
buzz: The view is real and the pricing is confusing, with packages for the skywalk, the ranch and the boat; cameras are not allowed on the glass.

name: Oatman
unique: A gold camp on Route 66 where wild burros walk the main street, with a wooden sidewalk, a saloon and a gunfight show for tourists.
buzz: The burros are the reason children love it and the drive over the Black Mountains is the scenic route; the town is tiny and the shows are corny on purpose.

name: London Bridge
unique: The 1831 London Bridge, bought, dismantled stone by stone and rebuilt over a Colorado River canal in the desert, with an English village around it.
buzz: The story is better than the bridge and the boat tour under it is the fun; the lake is the real attraction for most visitors.

name: Yuma Territorial Prison
customer: History people, true crime fans, families
unique: A territorial prison built into a bluff above the Colorado, with cell blocks, a guard tower and the story of the inmates who built the railroad and died in the heat.
buzz: The cell block and the dark cell are the tour and the guides tell the stories well; it is a compact site and the river view is the setting.

name: Kofa National Wildlife Refuge
unique: Six hundred thousand acres of Sonoran desert protecting a herd of desert bighorn sheep, with rugged dirt roads, palm canyons and old mines.
buzz: The sheep are hard to see and that is the point; the roads need high clearance and the summer heat is lethal.

name: Colorado River State Historic Park
unique: The quartermaster depot and the siphon that diverted the Colorado to irrigate the desert, in a park on the river levee.
buzz: The engineering story of the canal is the reason to stop and the buildings are restored; it is small and pairs with the prison.

name: Tumacacori National Historical Park
unique: The adobe ruins of a mission church on the Santa Cruz, with a museum on the O'odham and Yaqui people and a orchard of heirloom fruit trees.
buzz: The church walls and the quiet are the visit and the rangers explain the mission system honestly; the December fiesta is the local tradition.

name: Patagonia Lake State Park
unique: A 265 acre lake in a canyon of the Patagonia Mountains, with a beach, boat rentals and a birding trail where the hummingbird migration passes in summer.
buzz: The lake is the swimming and the birds are the reason naturalists come; the campground books out and the water is cold in spring.

name: Tonto Natural Bridge
unique: A 183 foot tall natural travertine bridge with a creek running under it, and trails down to the water through a cave and along the rim.
buzz: The trail under the bridge is steep and slick and the view from the top is the easy version; the park is small and the parking is limited.

name: Roosevelt Lake
unique: The reservoir formed by the Theodore Roosevelt Dam, the first big federal reclamation project, with a bridge named after the dam and desert mountains all around.
buzz: The lake is the fishing and the dam is the history; the water level varies and the summer heat is brutal.

name: Homolovi State Park
unique: Ancestral Puebloan village sites on the Little Colorado, with pottery sherds on the surface and a campground with a view of the Painted Desert.
buzz: The ruins are unexcavated and the rangers ask you not to pick up the pottery; the park is quiet and the sunset over the mesa is the reason to camp.

name: Fool Hollow Lake
unique: A lake in the White Mountains with a campground under ponderosa pines, a swim beach and a trail around the shore, at 6,300 feet.
buzz: It is the cool summer escape for Phoenix and the campground is the draw; the lake is small and the trout fishing is stocked.

name: Mount Graham
unique: A 10,720 foot sky island above the desert with a road to the top, a spruce fir forest and an observatory where the Vatican runs a telescope.
buzz: The drive from desert to alpine forest in an hour is the experience and the observatory tour needs booking; the mountain is closed to the public in some seasons for the red squirrel.

name: Gila Box Riparian National Conservation Area
unique: Twenty three miles of the Gila and San Simon rivers with cottonwood galleries, beaver and 200 bird species, in a desert canyon.
buzz: The float in spring is the reason to come and the creek trails are quiet; the water is seasonal and the roads are rough.

name: Cibola National Wildlife Refuge
unique: A Colorado River floodplain refuge where sandhill cranes and hundreds of thousands of geese winter, with a driving loop and a walk in aviary.
buzz: The crane season from November to February is the spectacle and the auto loop is easy; summer is empty and very hot.

name: Hi Jolly Monument
customer: Road trippers, history fans, RV snowbirds
unique: A stone pyramid over the grave of Hadji Ali, the Syrian camel driver who ran the army's 1850s camel experiment, in a town of rock shops and winter RVers.
buzz: The camel story is the reason to stop and the January rock and gem show is the other one; the town swells to a million visitors in winter.

name: Morenci Mine Overlook
unique: A viewpoint over one of the largest open pit copper mines in North America, where the pit is miles wide and the haul trucks look like toys.
buzz: The scale is the attraction and the overlook is free; the mine is active so check access and do not enter closed roads.

name: Chiricahua National Monument
unique: A forest of eroded rhyolite hoodoos and balanced rocks in the sky islands, with a loop trail through the columns and a view into the desert.
buzz: The Heart of Rocks loop is the hike and the far park is quiet; the road to the top is steep and the summer monsoon brings lightning.

name: Ramsey Canyon Preserve
unique: A canyon in the Huachuca Mountains where 15 species of hummingbird pass through in summer, with a shaded trail along a creek.
buzz: Hummingbird season from April to September is the reason to come and the feeders at the visitor center are the viewing; reservations are required.

name: Wupatki and Sunset Crater
unique: A lava flow and cinder cone beside a 900 year old pueblo of red sandstone with a ball court and a blowhole, on the same loop road.
buzz: The contrast between the black lava and the red pueblo is the photograph; the Wupatki ruins are quiet and the loop drive is 35 miles.

name: Grand Canyon Railway
unique: A restored train that runs 65 miles from Williams to the South Rim, with a 1920s parlor car, a buffet car and a staged train robbery on the way back.
buzz: The dome car and the wild west show are the family draw; the train arrives at the rim and the return is a long day, so book the class you want.

name: Petrified Forest National Park
unique: A drive through the Painted Desert and fields of petrified wood, with a 225 million year old log jam, petroglyphs and a 1930s inn built of stone.
buzz: The Blue Mesa trail is the walk and the Painted Desert at sunset is the photograph; removing petrified wood is illegal and the park is 50 miles from anywhere.

name: Montezuma Castle
unique: A five story cliff dwelling built into a limestone alcove by the Sinagua, with a path along the creek below and a sycamore grove.
buzz: The dwelling is viewed from below and the scale is the surprise; it is a one hour stop and the Well nearby is included.

name: Jerome
unique: A copper mining town built on a 30 degree slope above the Verde Valley, once called the wickedest town in the west, now galleries, wine bars and a state park.
buzz: The sliding jail and the state park are the history and the view from the upper streets is the photograph; parking is on a steep hill and the town is busy on weekends.

name: Museum of Flight
unique: A collection that includes a Concorde, the first Boeing 747 and a SR-71 Blackbird, with a walk through the original Red Barn where Boeing built its first planes.
buzz: The SR-71 and the 747 are the two planes people photograph and the Red Barn is the history; the museum is on Boeing Field and the tower tour is extra.

name: Chihuly Garden and Glass
unique: A glasshouse and garden of Dale Chihuly's work at the foot of the Space Needle, with a ceiling of glass flowers and towers that light up at night.
buzz: The glasshouse and the garden at dusk are the two visits; the combo ticket with the Space Needle saves money and the exhibits are indoors on rainy days.

name: Discovery Park
unique: Five hundred and thirty four acres of forest, meadow and sea cliffs on the old Fort Lawton, with a lighthouse and a beach on Puget Sound.
buzz: The loop trail to the lighthouse is the walk and the meadow is the birding; the park is big and the beach is a steep climb back.

name: Point Defiance Zoo and Aquarium
unique: A zoo and aquarium in a 760 acre park on Puget Sound, with polar bears, walruses and a Pacific seas aquarium, plus a ferry to the park.
buzz: The walruses and the aquarium are the family draw and the park around it has trails and a beach; the hill is steep and the zoo is compact.

name: Museum of Glass
unique: A museum with a working hot shop where you can watch a team gather and blow glass, and a cone of steel and glass on the Thea Foss waterway.
buzz: The hot shop demonstrations are the reason to come and the Chihuly bridge of glass outside is free; the museum is small enough for two hours.

name: LeMay America's Car Museum
unique: A silver wave shaped building above Interstate 5 holding 300 cars from the LeMay collection, including a 1906 Cadillac and a Tucker, with a driving simulator.
buzz: Car people say the collection is one of the best in the country and the building is the landmark; the rotating exhibits keep it fresh.

name: Riverfront Park
unique: A park built for the 1974 world's fair on the Spokane River, with a gondola over the falls, a 1909 carousel and a giant red wagon you can climb on.
buzz: The falls and the wagon are the photographs and the gondola is the ride; the park is free and the carousel is a dollar or two.

name: Manito Park
unique: Ninety acres with a formal Duncan garden, a Japanese garden, a rose hill and a greenhouse conservatory, all free in the middle of the city.
buzz: The Japanese garden and the Duncan garden are the two stops and the park is free; the greenhouse is the winter visit.

name: Northwest Museum of Arts and Culture
company: Northwest Museum of Arts and Culture
unique: A museum in a 1916 mansion with regional Native artifacts, a Campbell House next door and a gallery of western art, run by the historical society.
buzz: The Campbell House and the Native collection are the reasons to come; the museum is small and the mansion is a step back into 1898.

name: Boeing Future of Flight
unique: The tour of the Everett factory, the largest building by volume in the world, where 747s, 777s and 787s are assembled on catwalks above the floor.
buzz: The factory floor is the thing people cannot get over and the tour needs booking; the gallery has a 787 dreamliner you can walk through.

name: Jetty Island
unique: A man made island of sand and dune grass in Puget Sound, reached by a free ferry, with shallow warm water and a long empty beach.
buzz: The shallow water is warm by Puget Sound standards and the ferry is free; the island is only open in summer and the wind is constant.

name: Mukilteo Lighthouse
unique: A 1906 lighthouse on a point above the ferry landing, with a keeper's house, a beach and a view of Whidbey Island across the sound.
buzz: The lighthouse and the ferry crossing are the photograph and the beach is a good picnic; the tour is weekends only.

name: Hurricane Ridge
unique: A road that climbs to 5,242 feet in Olympic National Park for a view of the Bailey Range and the Strait of Juan de Fuca, with trails into alpine meadows.
buzz: The view on a clear day is the best drive in the park and the winter snowshoe is the local secret; check the road report, it closes for weather.

name: Dungeness Spit
unique: The longest natural sand spit in the country, five and a half miles into the Strait of Juan de Fuca, with a lighthouse at the end and a protected estuary behind it.
buzz: The walk to the lighthouse takes most of a day and most people turn around at the first mile; the estuary is closed in winter for birds.

name: Cape Flattery
unique: The northwestern tip of the contiguous United States, where a boardwalk leads to sea caves and a view of Tatoosh Island and the open Pacific.
buzz: The boardwalk and the sea stacks are the photograph and the drive is remote; a Makah recreation permit is required and the trail can be muddy.

name: North Cascades Highway
unique: The most scenic mountain pass in the state, crossing 5,477 feet through the North Cascades with trailheads to turquoise lakes and glaciers at every pullout.
buzz: The drive from Marblemount to Winthrop is the day and the Diablo Lake overlook is the photograph; the road closes with snow from November to April.

name: Mount Baker
unique: A 10,781 foot volcano with the world record for snowfall, a road to Artist Point at 5,100 feet and trails into the Heather Meadows.
buzz: Artist Point in July and August is the view of Shuksan and the mountain and the snow lingers into summer; the road is closed in winter below the lodge.

name: Fairhaven Historic District
unique: A brick Victorian district on Bellingham Bay built on a gold rush that never happened, with a village green, a bookstore and a ferry to the San Juan Islands.
buzz: The bookshop and the waterfront trail are the local stops and the Alaska ferry terminal is at the bottom of the hill; the district is small and walkable.

name: Lake Chelan and Stehekin
company: National Park Service and Lady of the Lake
unique: A 55 mile glacial lake that runs into the North Cascades, with a ferry to Stehekin, a roadless valley at the far end with a bakery and a waterfall.
buzz: The ferry ride up the lake is the day and Stehekin is the reward; the boat takes four hours each way, so many people stay overnight.

name: Icicle Gorge
unique: A loop trail along the Icicle River through a granite gorge, with a footbridge over the water and a view up to the Stuart Range.
buzz: The loop is four miles of easy walking and the bridge is the photograph; the trailhead is a rough road and the parking is limited.

name: Slidewaters
unique: A water park above Lake Chelan with slides built into the hillside and a view of the lake from the lazy river, in a town that gets 300 days of sun.
buzz: The view from the slides is the reason people drive from Seattle and the lines are short on weekdays; the park is small.

name: Lake Quinault
unique: A rain forest lake ringed by the largest trees in the state, with a loop trail through old growth spruce and a 1926 lodge on the shore.
buzz: The loop drive and the Rain Forest Nature Trail are the easy version and the Enchanted Valley trail is the epic; it rains most of the year.

name: Westport Light
unique: A 1898 lighthouse at the end of a jetty on the Pacific, with a boardwalk over the dunes and a view of Grays Harbor and the open ocean.
buzz: The boardwalk and the jetty are the walk and the beach is wide and windy; the town is the base for charter fishing.

name: Lady Washington
unique: A replica of the first American ship to round Cape Horn, sailing from Grays Harbor with passengers hauling lines and standing watch on the deck.
buzz: The crew lets passengers help sail and the ship appears in films; the sailings sell out in summer and the dock is in Aberdeen.

name: Yakima Valley Wine Country
unique: The oldest wine region in the state, with 90 wineries and vineyards in a desert valley below the Rattlesnake Hills, where the fruit gets ripe and the tasting rooms are cheap.
buzz: Wine people say the reds are the value and the tasting rooms are informal; book a driver, the valley is long and the roads are two lane.

name: Bale Breaker Brewing
unique: A brewery built in the middle of a hop field that the family has farmed for four generations, with a taproom that looks out over the bines.
buzz: The fresh hop beers in September are the reason beer people make the drive and the outdoor seating is the setting; the taproom is closed early on weekdays.

name: Toppenish Murals
unique: More than 70 murals painted on downtown walls telling the history of the Yakama Nation and the railroad town, best seen by horse drawn wagon.
buzz: The wagon tour in summer is the way to see them and the murals are genuinely good; the town is small and the drive from Yakima is 30 minutes.

name: Walla Walla Wine Tasting
unique: More than 120 wineries in a valley that produces some of the state's best syrah, with a walkable downtown of tasting rooms and a sweet onion festival in June.
buzz: Wine people rate the syrah with the best in the country and the downtown tasting rooms make a car unnecessary; spring and fall are the best weather.

name: Whitman Mission
unique: The site of the 1847 mission where the Whitmans were killed, with the foundation of the mission house, a wagon ruts trail and a museum on the Cayuse War.
buzz: The ranger talks tell the story from both sides and the wagon ruts are the real thing; it is free and the walk is flat.

name: Fort Walla Walla Museum
unique: A pioneer village of 17 original buildings, a horse era machinery hall and a military museum on the old fort grounds.
buzz: The pioneer village is the family draw and the machinery hall is the surprise; the living history weekends bring it alive.
